Verification packets (thesis Ch 7, task 7)

One packet per explained network, for Mike's verification of the Claude-drafted explanations. The 30 pre-registered packets are numbered in the pre-registered verification order (PREREG.md; PRE in build_explanations_csv.py): adult-s0, heart-s5, monk2-s2, then the rest of the fixed permutation. Verify down this order, as far as you get; do not skip or reorder. The supplementary packets (Heart-100, churn100, churn200) are in supplementary/, each set in its own order; they are not pre-registered and do not count towards the threshold.

Nothing here changes an explanation, a record or a number. The packets are generated from the records, the run tables and live_checks.json, a read-only re-run of the automatic checks.

How to verify one network

  • Read the packet top to bottom: header and summary, the annotation tree (each leaf's closed form, hypothesis and evidence), the refactoring operations, the checks, what resisted.
  • Start with "What to look at": 3 to 6 points specific to that network (largest closed-form error, the strongest claims, the splits that matter, anything the checks flag).
  • If you want the graph, open the genome in the UI (uv run python -m explaneat api, then Review → open the genome; the packet header has a direct link). The UI uses the same database.
  • Decide: is each leaf's hypothesis supported by its closed form and evidence, and does the composition say how the children combine? Note any change you make or would make.
  • Time yourself: the minutes go into the record as Mike's verification time, reported separately from Claude's.

How to record the verdict

Recording already exists and survives an explanations.csv rebuild (commit 1deebbf): build_explanations_csv.py reads the verdict from the JSON record and nowhere else. Two ways, which write the same field:

  • (a) Edit the record. Add a top-level block to experiments/10seed/explanations/<label>.json: "mike_verification": {"verified": true, "minutes": 25, "changes": "...", "notes": "..."}, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py.
  • (b) Use the UI. uv run python -m explaneat api → Review → open the genome → Tools → Review & verify. The form writes the same mike_verification field into the record of the checkout the API runs from. Rebuild the CSV afterwards as in (a).

One-line example for (a), using the same writer as the UI (atomic, keeps the rest of the record and its format):

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('adult-s0', True, minutes=25, changes='none', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Fields: verified (true or false), minutes (your time), changes (what you changed, empty if nothing), notes (optional). Commit the record and the rebuilt CSVs. To refresh the status column below, run uv run python experiments/10seed/verification/make_packets.py (no database needed).

All 60 records were re-checked live on 2026-11-11T12:25:06+13:00 (commit 77513b9): function preservation, per-leaf closed-form and numeric error, structural and compositional coverage, the hierarchy check and the operation counts. Every live value agrees with the orchestrator's record, and the agents' own (rounded) numbers agree too.

Files

  • NN_<label>.md: the 30 pre-registered packets; supplementary/: the 30 additional ones.
  • packets.html: all packets in one offline page (formulas pre-rendered to MathML with KaTeX; no CDN).
  • live_checks.json: the live check values, annotations, hypotheses, evidence and closed forms used here.
  • collect_live.py: writes live_checks.json, with a read-only DB session (the only step that reads the DB). make_packets.py + katex_render.js: write the packets from files only.

Summary (from the record)

P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(0.808 + sparse linear backbone over 41 inputs + capital-gain term + female/Priv-house-serv gate + 7 single-category offsets), additive in logit. Hidden units with one one-hot input are exact category offsets (unknown workclass, Without-pay override, Exec-managerial, Wife, Separated, Japan, a dead Private unit). Only real nonlinearities: a convex capital-gain hinge and an OR-like gate (+0.58 women, +2 to +3.6 Priv-house-serv). Train acc 0.852, AUC 0.906; backbone dominates (AUC 0.753 without it).

Annotations (root → compositions → leaves)

Closed forms are computed live with the same code as get_formula(force=True) on the replayed model state; a composition is shown with its children as named functions. Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 39,073 training rows.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(0.808 + linear_backbone + capital_gain_hinge + female_or_household_gate + 7 single-category offsets). Composition is purely additive in logit space; the children never feed each other. Category offsets (train logit deltas): unknown workclass +0.82, Without-pay +61 (override to <=50K, 17 rows), Exec-managerial -0.82, Wife -2.90, Japan +0.14 (two large near-cancelling terms), Separated +0.23, dead Private unit 0. Since every bump has a single binary input, each is exactly an affine function of that indicator; the network is therefore a logistic regression plus two genuine nonlinearities: a convex capital-gain hinge (slope -2.66 -> -3.08 above ~0.43 SD) and an OR-like ReLU gate that adds +0.58 logit for women and +2 to +3.6 logit for Priv-house-serv. 56 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, 39,073 rows): acc 0.852, AUC 0.906. Mean-ablation AUC drops: linear_backbone 0.906->0.753, capital_gain_hinge ->0.888, wife_bump ->0.887, exec_managerial ->0.903, female gate ->0.904; others <0.001. SHAP (500 rows) top: relationship:0 Husband, education-num, capital-gain, Married-civ-spouse, Wife, Exec-managerial, age, hours-per-week, relationship:1, sex.

Evidence (3 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Root closed form: sigmoid of bias plus weighted sum of all child exits; additive in logit space.
  • shap_importance: Whole-model SHAP (train, 500 samples).
  • ablation_study: Child importance by mean-ablation: linear_backbone >> capital_gain_hinge > wife_bump > exec_managerial_bump ~ female_or_household_gate > others; dead_private_unit exactly 0.

A.1 Leaf: capital_gain_hinge

Annotation idann_116
Entry nodes-63_ac (capital-gain_ac)
Exit nodes816_a, idn_o63
Internal / exit nodes in its own subgraph816_a, idn_o63
Dimensionality (in → out, incl. descendants)1 → 2
Live closed-form error (3 s.f. display)0.0233
Live numeric-function error0

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(1.16xcapital−gain_ac−0.5)y1=−2.66xcapital−gain_ac\begin{gathered}y_0 = \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.16 x_{capital-gain\_ac} - 0.5 \right)} \\ y_1 = - 2.66 x_{capital-gain\_ac}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Capital-gain (standardised; output is P(income<=50K)) enters the logit as a convex piecewise-linear decreasing function: a direct linear term -2.658*cg (via idn_o63) plus a ReLU hinge -0.364*relu(1.161*cg-0.500) that steepens the slope from -2.66 to -3.08 above cg~0.43 SD (raw ~$4.3k; ~5.7% of rows). Large capital gains push strongly towards >50K. Evidence (train, 39,073 rows): closed form verified by get_formula; viz summaries confirm the exits; mean-ablating this leaf's logit contribution gives acc 0.8359 / AUC 0.8877 (baseline 0.8518 / 0.9056), mean |dP| 0.0624, max |dP| 0.997. Removing only the hinge (keeping the linear term) barely changes performance (AUC 0.9054): the capital-gain effect is mostly linear in the standardised value.

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form of the exits (3 s.f.). Exits are read out by the output node with the weights given in the hypothesis.
  • empirical_viz: Train split, all 39,073 rows: get_viz_summary results plus a local mean-ablation (replace this leaf's logit contribution with its train mean).

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing structural. Capital-gain hinge 816 also feeds sex gate 369 (weight -0.0053): split 816 and capital-gain, consolidated two copies. Japan's net +0.14 is two near-cancelling large terms. Without-pay (17 rows) gets a +61 logit override, fitted to very few rows.

Tool notes (record): Root rejected if child exits listed in subgraph_nodes (paper style: entries only). A child exit with other outputs cannot be a sibling leaf entry. SHAP ~5e-4 on unconnected inputs (noise).

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: capital_gain_hinge (0.0233), then unknown_workclass_bump (0.0158). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in without_pay_override: its evidence includes a category or regime active on only 17 training rows. “On the rare standardised value (~48) the sum is ~+61 logit: an override that forces the prediction to <=50K for unpaid workers;” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in japan_cancelling_bump: its evidence includes a category or regime active on only 68 training rows. “native-country:24 (Japan, 68 rows) feeds an always-active ReLU 6081 (readout +0.205, ~+4.7 logit on the rare value) and a direct term (idn_o83, ~-4.6 logit).” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 1 hidden-node split(s), which decide how a unit's roles are divided: 816 → 816_a → capital_gain_hinge (exit); full_model (entry) | 816_b → female_or_household_gate (internal). Do the copies really play the different roles the annotations give them?

Summary (from the record)

Essentially logistic regression (18 direct edges; logit SD 3.18) plus one small nonlinear ischaemia correction (logit SD 0.78): a ReLU gate on oldpeak, thal:7 and restecg:0 that adds to risk directly and feeds a resting-BP-offset gate read out directly, via a high-threshold amplifier, and via an age term active only without ischaemia evidence. Nonlinear parts add ~+0.010 train AUC (0.932 linear-only vs 0.942).

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: logit z = -0.496 + LINEAR CORE + 0.117*st_ischaemia_gate_output + ischaemia_pathway readouts (0.135*290 + 0.165*1834 + 0.097*1987); prediction = sigmoid(z) (the genome output node is ReLU but the evaluator overrides it with sigmoid for binary classification, so it is a logistic score). LINEAR CORE (18 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.51, sex:0 -1.08, slope:1 -0.90, chol +0.53, cp:1 -0.53, trestbps +0.49, cp:3 -0.47, thal:3 -0.43, exang:1 +0.43, slope:3 -0.41, thal:6 -0.38, cp:4 +0.33, fbs:0 +0.28, thalach -0.25, restecg:0 -0.18, exang:0 +0.15, age +0.11, thal:7 -0.07. Signs match cardiology: more fluoroscopy-coloured vessels, male sex, high cholesterol/BP, exertional angina and asymptomatic chest pain raise risk; upsloping ST (slope:1), normal thallium (thal:3), typical/non-anginal pain and high max heart rate lower it. 6 inputs are unused (sex:1, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2, slope:2, thal:4 - mostly redundant one-hot complements or rare categories). COMPOSITION: purely additive in the logit - the two children add to the linear core. Child 1 (st_ischaemia_gate_output) adds a ReLU ischaemia score (oldpeak, thal:7, restecg:0); child 2 (ischaemia_pathway) adds a BP-adjusted, convexly amplified version of the same score, plus an age term that is active only when the score is quiet. oldpeak influences the output ONLY through these gates (it has no direct edge); thal:7 acts mainly through them (raising the risk) but also has a small direct edge in the linear core (-0.07), which lowers it and is its only effect where the gates are off. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.942 / acc 0.876; linear core alone AUC 0.932 (nonlinear parts add +0.010 train AUC); logit SD of linear core 3.18 vs 0.78 for all nonlinear readouts combined. Removing individual readouts: 290 -0.002, 1834 -0.0016, 204_a -0.0016, 1987 -0.0007, whole pathway -0.0055 AUC. Whole-model SHAP (prob scale): ca 0.139, sex:0 0.105, slope:1 0.099, thal:3 0.045, cp:3 0.041, exang:1 0.039, oldpeak 0.038, chol 0.033, cp:4 0.032. The model is essentially a logistic regression with one small nonlinear ischaemia correction.

Evidence (4 records, DB):

  • performance_metrics: Complete structural and compositional coverage with 10 function-preserving splits; explained network computes the same function as the evolved one.
  • ablation_study: The linear core carries most of the signal; the nonlinear ischaemia machinery adds ~+0.01 train AUC. Test split not inspected (protocol).
  • shap_importance: Top drivers ca, sex:0, slope:1 are all direct linear-core edges; oldpeak (gate-only input) ranks 7th.
  • analytical_formula: Closed-form root: an 18-term linear logit plus four additive nonlinear readouts from the two children.

Hypothesis (DB):

Serial composition of the ischaemia gate into a BP-adjusted gate and its readouts. (1) Gate 290 = ReLU(1.088*st_ischaemia_gate_bp - 0.817*trestbps + 0.151*cp:2 + 0.017*cp:3 + 0.046*thal:6 - 0.013*thal6_linear_passthrough - 0.485): it passes on the ischaemia evidence of 204_b, offset downward by resting blood pressure (high-BP patients need more ST-depression evidence to open it). (2) 1834 = ReLU(0.941*290 - 1.672): high-threshold amplifier, fires only when 290 > 1.78, making the pathway convex. (3) 1987 = ReLU(0.880*age - 1.585*290 + 0.179): an age term switched OFF by the gate, so age adds risk only for patients in whom 290 is quiet. Output contribution 0.135*290 + 0.165*1834 + 0.097*1987. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 290 active 56% (100/135 of its active cases have 204 on; 35 open from low BP alone, mean predicted risk 0.18); 1834 active 26%, only when 204 and 290 are both on, and 78% of those patients are diseased; 1987 active in 64% of patients with 290 quiet vs 13% with 290 active. The thal:6 chain is functionally inert. Interpretation: the network has exactly one nonlinear mechanism - an ischaemia pathway that amplifies strong ST-depression/defect evidence and uses age as a fallback signal when that evidence is absent.

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form of the composed pathway; 290 is a serial composition over the child gate, and 1834/1987 are readouts of 290 that respectively amplify strong ischaemia evidence and switch off the age term.
  • empirical_viz: Empirics agree with the formula: 1834 fires only in the regime where both 204 and 290 are on (26% of patients, 78% of them diseased) - an amplifier for strong ischaemia evidence. 1987 is on for 64% of patients with 290 quiet but only 13% when 290 is active, confirming that age acts as a fallback risk signal that the ischaemia pathway switches off. 290 is opened by 204 in 100/135 of its active cases; 35 cases open it from low resting BP alone and these patients have low predicted risk (mean 0.18).

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. Validator only treats direct-child nodes as internal, forcing a split of gate 204 (and its 3 inputs) because it reads out to both the output and gate 290. Nodes 290/1834/1987 take inputs from several annotations so live only in the ischaemia_pathway composition. thal:6 chain 3671->2116 is affine and near-inert (weight -0.013 into 290).

Tool notes (record): get_formula composition latex drops child terms (latex_collapsed correct); viz tools with annotation_id on compositions zero the children (use node_id); validator ignores grandchildren; detect_splits misses input fan-out across annotations; compute_shap tqdm on stderr; get_formula shows output ReLU but model applies sigmoid; tool compositional_coverage always 1.0.

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: st_ischaemia_gate_output (0.0217), then st_ischaemia_gate_bp (0.0217). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in thal6_linear_passthrough: “Since thal:6 >= -0.257 on the data both ReLUs are always active (100% on train), so 2116 = 1.003*thal:6 + 2.165 exactly (r = 1.000 on train).” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in st_ischaemia_gate_output: “This is the output-facing copy 204_a (bit-identical to 204_b);” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 1 hidden-node split(s), which decide how a unit's roles are divided: 204 → 204_a → st_ischaemia_gate_output (exit) | 204_b → st_ischaemia_gate_bp (exit). Do the copies really play the different roles the annotations give them?
  • Explained with protocol v2 tooling (the pilot): get_formula then showed the output node as ReLU, while the model applies sigmoid. Hypotheses and evidence that mention a ReLU output, or AUCs of the raw logit, predate the fix (the live closed forms above use sigmoid). Check the root's wording.
  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Summary (from the record)

Saturated logistic count: logit ~ 80 - 20k (k = number of first values); per-indicator drops 17.5-25 via 9 direct edges; hidden pathway is a lookup on (a3, a6, a1=3) supplying the a3 indicator. Output ~1 iff k<=3.

Agreement with the MONK-2 rule (record): Only an upper edge one step too high (k>=4/5 negative) and no lower edge: agrees with the rule on 41.4% of 432; output ~1 on 91.5% of train rows (acc 0.41, AUC 0.81).

Exhaustive check over all 432 configurations: logit 82..96 (k=0), 60..79 (k=1), 37..56 (k=2), 15..32 (k=3), -5.2..7.7 (k=4, 49% positive, depending on which attributes are first-valued: the a1/a4 indicators drop the least), <-16 (k>=5). The decision equals 'k <= 3' on 94.4% of the 432 configurations (all disagreements at k=4). The model is a saturated monotone 'at most three (sometimes four) first values' detector. Train (n=345): output median 1.0, mean 0.915; accuracy 0.41, AUC 0.81. Compared with the target rule (exactly two first values) it agrees on 41.4% of the 432 configurations: it learned only the upper edge of the k=2 peak (k>=4/5 -> negative), placed one step too high, and has no lower edge (k=0,1 -> positive).

Summary (from the record)

Essentially logistic regression over 17 inputs (logit SD 4.33) plus one sparse nonlinear correction: gate 665 is an exact AND of female, exercise angina and no LVH, firing on 8/242 train rows (7 positive); a flat-slope ReLU amplifies it super-additively (node 1650 values 0, 0.446, 2.10, 6.09; gate+flat slope 7/7 positive). Removing the amplifier: train AUC 0.945 -> 0.930.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: additive composition. The logit z of node 0 is a linear score over 17 direct standardized inputs (dominated by ca 1.93, sex:1 1.67, cp:4 1.21, slope:2 1.05, chol 0.72, oldpeak 0.71) plus 0.772 x flat_slope_amplifier plus 0.026 x restecg2_relay; 7 inputs (trestbps, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:1, exang:1, thal:3, thal:4) are disconnected. get_formula shows node 0 as ReLU, but for this binary task the model output is sigmoid(z) on the pre-activation (compute_performance train AUC 0.945 equals AUC of z; sigmoid(relu(z)) would give 0.912). Evidence (train, n=242, local forward passes): direct-linear logit SD 4.33 vs amplifier term SD 0.79 vs relay term SD 0.026. Dropping the amplifier term lowers train AUC 0.945 -> 0.930 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.868; the direct linear part alone gives AUC 0.931. So the network is essentially logistic regression plus one sparse nonlinear correction: a flat-slope bonus (+0.34 logit) and a large boost (+4.7 logit) for the 7 women with exertional angina, no LVH and flat ST slope. Kernel SHAP on the full model (train) ranks ca 0.149, sex:1 0.130, slope:2 0.121, cp:4 0.116, oldpeak 0.049, thal:7 0.046, chol 0.044 (mean |SHAP| on probability). Function preservation after the two input splits: max abs err 1.8e-15.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: serial composition H(G(sex:0, exang:0, restecg:2), slope:2). Node 3598 = relu(1.51 slope:2 + 1.05 G - 0.76) and node 1650 = relu(1.29 G + 1.31*3598 - 0.73). Because G takes only the values 0 or 2.117 and slope:2 is binary, 1650 has exactly four regimes on train: G=0 & slope not flat -> 0 (n=131, 27% positive); G=0 & flat slope (slope:2) -> 0.446 (n=103, 63% positive); G on & slope not flat -> 2.097 (n=1, negative); G on & flat slope -> 6.092 (n=7, all positive). So without the gate it is a small additional flat-ST-slope bonus (+0.34 logit after the 0.772 output weight, on top of the direct slope:2 weight); with the gate it amplifies the female-exertional-angina signal, and the flat-slope ReLU 3598 makes the two conditions super-additive (6.09 vs 0.45+2.10). Evidence: activation_profile on node 1650 (train): active 45.9%, mean 0.375, SD 1.018, max 6.092; values confirmed by local forward pass.

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Serial composition of the gate with a flat-slope ReLU.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: node 665 is a three-way AND gate that fires only for women (sex:0 set) with exercise-induced angina (exang:0 unset, i.e. exang=yes) and no left-ventricular hypertrophy on resting ECG (restecg:2 unset). The restecg:2 chain 2349 -> 2771 never leaves the ReLU linear region on standardized one-hot inputs (2349 in [1.15,3.11], 2771 in [1.99,3.72]), so the gate collapses exactly to relu(1.41 sex:0 - 1.71 exang:0 - 1.18 restecg:2 - 3.39). Evidence (train, n=242): pre-activation max is 2.117, reached only when all three conditions hold; removing any one condition drives it negative (no female: -0.86; no exang: -2.53; LVH present: -0.24). The gate is active on 8/242 rows (3.3%), always at the single value 2.117, and 7 of those 8 are positive cases. Closed form matches the forward pass (check_explanation closed-form err 0.0049, numeric err 0).

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. Two input splits (restecg:2, slope:2). 3598 and 1650 take input from gate 665 so live only in the flat_slope_amplifier composition. Inner restecg:2 ReLUs 2349, 2771 never clip (affine). Relay 2447 near-inert (logit SD 0.026). Gate evidence rests on only 8 active train rows: specificity solid, clinical meaning weakly supported.

Tool notes (record): Root validation failed with grandchild entry nodes, so they were left out of the root entry list. get_formula shows output as ReLU; agent reports train AUC 0.945 = AUC(z) while sigmoid(relu(z)) gives 0.912. compute_shap >120s, tiny nonzero SHAP (1e-5) on disconnected inputs (kernel-SHAP noise).

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: restecg2_relay_2447 (0.00827). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.

Summary (from the record)

Essentially logistic regression: 15 direct edges carry logit SD 5.3 of 7.0. ca enters by three parallel affine routes; cp:3 only via affine relay 1173; 2009 adds a small negative max-heart-rate term. The one consequential nonlinearity is gate 1801 = ReLU(1.48 restecg:0 + 0.805 oldpeak - 1.43): ST depression adds risk mainly when resting ECG is normal. Replacing all ReLUs by identity drops train AUC 0.939 -> 0.916, almost all from 1801.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: output node 0 computes the logit z = -0.160 + LINEAR CORE + hidden readouts, and (binary task) the model applies a sigmoid at the output (get_formula shows node 0 as ReLU; decision is z>0). LINEAR CORE: 15 direct edges, largest |w|: sex:0 -2.01 (female lowers risk), slope:2 +1.85, ca +1.53, cp:4 (asymptomatic) +1.32, thal:3 (normal) -1.04, chol +1.01, thal:6 -0.97, cp:1 -0.93, oldpeak +0.87, trestbps +0.72; SD 5.29 of a 7.04 total logit SD. Children add: +0.983*ca_slope2_gate (near-affine in ca, slope:2), -1.305*cp3_affine_relay (affine, -0.66 cp:3), +1.669*2245 and -0.165*2009 from ca_thalach_chain (mostly affine: +1.30 ca, small -thalach), and +1.335*normal_ecg_st_gate (the one real interaction: oldpeak adds extra risk only when restecg:0=+1). Composition is purely additive at node 0. Hypothesis (supported): the network is a logistic regression in which ca appears through three parallel affine routes (total ~+3.4 per SD), plus one gated ST-depression term. Evidence (train, n=242): AUC 0.939, acc 0.888. Replacing every ReLU by identity gives AUC 0.916, almost exactly the loss from removing only the 1801 ReLU (0.916), so 1801 is the only nonlinearity that matters; the other ReLUs change AUC by <=0.0002. Inputs age, sex:1, fbs:0, restecg:2, exang:1, slope:1, slope:3, thal:4, thal:7 are unconnected.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hidden node 664 = ReLU(0.601*ca + 0.326*slope:2 + 0.664), read out with +0.983. Hypothesis (supported): a near-affine risk term in number of major vessels coloured (ca) and flat ST slope (slope:2). On train the pre-activation ranges [-0.071, 2.607]; the ReLU clips only the 85 rows with ca at its minimum and slope:2=0, and only by <=0.071 (<=0.07 logit). Replacing the ReLU by identity leaves train AUC unchanged (0.9392 -> 0.9390); mean-ablating the node costs 0.002 AUC. Contribution SD 0.70 logit. So this is effectively +0.59*ca + 0.32*slope:2 added to the logit, on top of the direct ca and slope:2 edges.

Hidden node 1801 = ReLU(1.48*restecg:0 + 0.805*oldpeak - 1.43), readout +1.335. With restecg:0=+1 the gate passes ReLU(0.805*oldpeak + 0.05), active on 39.7% of those rows (exercise ST depression above about its median); with restecg:0=-1 it is active on 1/121 rows (needs oldpeak > 3.6 SD). So ST depression adds up to ~+3.4 extra logit, but only when restecg:0=+1. The ReLU matters: replacing it by identity drops train AUC 0.9392 -> 0.9162 (the linear version would add a large restecg:0 main effect); mean-ablating the whole node costs only 0.0001 AUC, so its value is the shape, not the extra ranking signal over the direct oldpeak edge (+0.869). Overall active rate 20%, contribution SD 0.55 logit.

Summary (from the record)

sigmoid(1.855 + Ramp - 7.41 Gate + 0.618 Chain): Ramp adds 3.6-10.5 logit per first value of a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 and ~-8 for a5=1; Gate fires iff >=3 of {a1,a2,a3,a4,a6}=1. Predicts positive roughly iff exactly two of those five AND a5!=1. Train acc 0.901, AUC 0.915.

Agreement with the MONK-2 rule (record): 'Exactly two of six' with a5 mishandled: a5=1 is a veto rather than an indicator, so all 20 train positives with a5=1 plus one other indicator are missed; approximate rule agrees with the model on 418/432 configurations.

Closed form (children as functions):

y0=e0.618a2a5bonuschain(−4c,−15)−7.41count_gate_atleast3_of5⁡(−1,−4b,−8,−9b,−16b,−17b)+1.0linear_indicator_ramp⁡(−2,−3,−4a,−7,−9a,−11,−12,−13,−16a,−17a)e0.618a2a5bonuschain(−4c,−15)−7.41count_gate_atleast3_of5⁡(−1,−4b,−8,−9b,−16b,−17b)+1.0linear_indicator_ramp⁡(−2,−3,−4a,−7,−9a,−11,−12,−13,−16a,−17a)+0.156\begin{gathered}y_0 = \frac{e^{0.618 a_{2 a5 bonus chain}{\left(-4_{c},-15 \right)} - 7.41 \operatorname{count\_gate\_atleast3\_of5}{\left(-1,-4_{b},-8,-9_{b},-16_{b},-17_{b} \right)} + 1.0 \operatorname{linear\_indicator\_ramp}{\left(-2,-3,-4_{a},-7,-9_{a},-11,-12,-13,-16_{a},-17_{a} \right)}}}{e^{0.618 a_{2 a5 bonus chain}{\left(-4_{c},-15 \right)} - 7.41 \operatorname{count\_gate\_atleast3\_of5}{\left(-1,-4_{b},-8,-9_{b},-16_{b},-17_{b} \right)} + 1.0 \operatorname{linear\_indicator\_ramp}{\left(-2,-3,-4_{a},-7,-9_{a},-11,-12,-13,-16_{a},-17_{a} \right)}} + 0.156}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

The output composes the three children additively under the sigmoid: logit = 1.855 + Ramp - 7.413*Gate + 0.618*Chain. Ramp: the first value of a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 raises the sum (by 3.6-10.5 each), so with the bias it crosses zero between one and two active indicators among {a1=1,a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} when a5!=1 (lower edge of a response peak); a5=1 instead costs about 8 logit units, pushing count-two cases below zero (an a5=1 veto). Gate: when three or more of the same five indicators are active it fires (pre-activation >=1.76) and its -7.41 readout overwhelms the Ramp (upper edge). Chain: +0.89 when a2!=1 and a5!=4; flips only 2 train predictions and is near-vestigial. Net: the model predicts positive approximately iff exactly two of {a1=1,a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1} hold AND a5!=1. Evidence (train, n=345): this rule agrees with the model on 331/345 rows (418/432 of all configurations); the 14 disagreements are near-boundary cases (|logit| < 1.8). Train accuracy 0.901, AUC 0.915; every train positive with a5=1 and exactly one other indicator (20 rows) is missed. Ablation: zeroing the gate drops train accuracy to 0.58; zeroing the chain gives 0.907. Inputs a2:2, a2:3, a4:2, a5:3 have no enabled edges and are zero-effect entries (sensitivity exactly 0).

Evidence (4 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Output = sigmoid(1.855 + Ramp - 7.41 Gate + 0.618 Chain); 0.156 = exp(-1.855).
  • empirical_viz: Output sensitivity on full train split; the four unconnected inputs have exactly zero effect.
  • input_output_sampling: cnt5 = number of {a1=1,a2=1,a3=1,a4=1,a6=1}. The model predicts positive almost only for cnt5==2 with a5!=1; all 20 train positives with a5=1 plus one other indicator are missed (the a5=1 veto).
  • ablation_study: The gate is essential (removing it drops train accuracy to 0.58). The chain flips only 2 train predictions and its removal slightly improves train accuracy (0.907): it is a near-vestigial nudge.

Hypothesis (DB):

An at-least-three-of-five indicator detector over {a1=1, a2=1, a3=1, a4=1, a6=1} that ignores a5. The largest two-indicator sum (a3+a6 = 31.08) leaves it at -0.52 (off); the smallest three-indicator sum (a1+a2+a4 = 33.37) reaches +1.76 (on). So the unit fires iff at least three of these five indicators are active. Evidence (train, n=345, and all 432 configurations): fires iff >=3 of the five indicators hold, agreement 1.0; max pre-activation with <=2 active is -0.525. Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(−1.12xa5:4−0.915relu⁡(0.732xa2:1_c+0.632)+0.9)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 1.12 x_{a5:4} \\ &\quad - 0.915 \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.732 x_{a2:1\_c} + 0.632 \right)} \\ &\quad + 0.9 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

A small serial chain giving a bonus when neither a2=1 nor a5=4. Node 1701 = ReLU(0.632 + 0.732 z(a2:1)) is always positive (0.111 if a2!=1, 1.660 if a2=1), so it is a linear relay of a2:1. Node 2480 = ReLU(0.900 - 1.120 z(a5:4) - 0.915 * n1701) takes three values: 1.445 when a2!=1 and a5!=4, 0.026 when a2=1 and a5!=4, and 0 when a5=4 (ReLU clips). Through its +0.618 readout it adds about +0.89 to the output logit only when a2!=1 and a5!=4: a weak, AND-of-negations nudge. Evidence (train, n=345): n2480 > 1 iff a2!=1 and a5!=4, agreement 1.0. Local ablation: zeroing its readout flips only 2 train predictions and slightly raises train accuracy (0.901 -> 0.907), so it is near-vestigial.

Evidence (3 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form of the subgraph (inputs are train-standardised one-hot columns).

Hypothesis (DB):

A linear indicator ramp with an a5=1 veto. Evaluated per attribute value, the direct connections contribute: a1 = 1/2/3: +3.85/-2.84/-1.31; a2 = 1/other: +7.00/-3.54; a3 = 1/2: +3.93/-4.14; a4 = 1/2/3: +2.98/-0.63/-2.19; a6 = 1/2: +4.40/-4.63. So for a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 the first value raises the sum by 3.6 to 10.5 units, making the sum rise roughly linearly with the number of these indicators. Attribute a5 is inverted: a5 = 1/2/3/4 contributes -6.25/+2.51/+1.90/+1.90, i.e. a5=1 is an 8-unit penalty rather than a positive indicator. Together with the output bias (+1.855) the ramp crosses zero between one and two active indicators among {a1,a2,a3,a4,a6} when a5!=1, and an a5=1 pushes it back below zero. Evidence: the per-value contributions are exact (linear in the one-hot columns); sensitivity on train is largest for a2:1 (4.98), a3:1 (4.04), a6:2 (3.73), a5:1 (3.54), a1:2 (3.16). Note a5=1 acts as a veto, not an indicator.

Summary (from the record)

sigmoid(-2.36 + Lin + Veto + 2.55 Gate - 0.60 A5): Lin +4..+12 per first value of a1,a2,a3,a4,a6; Veto a ReLU count unit, 0 for <=2 and down to -70 for >=3; Gate +9..+11 when a5!=1 (bonus with a3=1). Predicts 'exactly two of {a1,a2,a3,a4,a6}, preferably a5!=1'. Train acc 0.887, AUC 0.925.

y0=110.6e−2.55a5a3bonusgate(−3b,−12b,−12c,−16c,−7c,−11b)+0.599a5in24penalty(−12d,−14)−1.0atleast_3_of_five_veto⁡(−1b,−4b,−7b,−9b,−16b)−0.735inert_a32_unit⁡(−8)−1.0linear_first_value_score⁡(−1a,−2,−3a,−4a,−5,−6,−7a,−9a,−11a,−12a,−15,−16a)+1\begin{gathered}y_0 = \frac{1}{10.6 e^{- 2.55 a_{5 a3 bonus gate}{\left(-3_{b},-12_{b},-12_{c},-16_{c},-7_{c},-11_{b} \right)} + 0.599 a_{5 in 2 4 penalty}{\left(-12_{d},-14 \right)} - 1.0 \operatorname{atleast\_3\_of\_five\_veto}{\left(-1_{b},-4_{b},-7_{b},-9_{b},-16_{b} \right)} - 0.735 \operatorname{inert\_a32\_unit}{\left(-8 \right)} - 1.0 \operatorname{linear\_first\_value\_score}{\left(-1_{a},-2,-3_{a},-4_{a},-5,-6,-7_{a},-9_{a},-11_{a},-12_{a},-15,-16_{a} \right)}} + 1}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Two-of-five peak with an a5 handicap. The output is sigmoid(s) with s = -2.363 + Lin + Veto + 2.547*Gate - 0.599*A5 + 0.735*Inert, where Inert is identically 0. Lin (linear_first_value_score) rises by +4..+12 for each first value among a1, a2, a3, a4, a6 and is the rising edge: with at most one such first value s < 0 on all 432 configurations (max -0.42). Veto (atleast3_of_five_veto) is exactly 0 for at most two first values and <= -70 for three or more, so it is the falling edge: s < 0 for every configuration with three or more. Gate (a5_a3_bonus_gate) adds +8.5..+11 when a5 != 1 (more when a3 = 1) and nothing when a5 = 1 and a3 = 2; A5 is a -0.72 penalty for a5 in {2,4}. Net: with exactly two first values among {a1,a2,a3,a4,a6} the model predicts positive in 113 of 114 configurations when a5 != 1 but only 23 of 38 (61%) when a5 = 1 (the a5_a3 gate is weak or off there; pairs (2,3) and (3,4) always fail). So the network computes approximately 'exactly two of the five attributes a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 take their first value, and preferably a5 != 1': it agrees with [count5 == 2] on 96.3% of all 432 configurations and 95.9% of training rows, and reaches 88.7% train accuracy (AUC 0.925). Inputs a4:2, a5:2, a6:2 have no enabled connections and are zero-effect entries. Evidence: on train, ablating the veto drops accuracy 0.887 -> 0.562 and ablating the gate 0.887 -> 0.690; the score sign is negative for every configuration with <=1 or >=3 such first values. Comparison with the target rule (exactly two of all six attributes take their first value): the network has replaced a5=1 as a rule indicator with a5 != 1 as a bonus, so it is correct on two-of-six cases where a5 != 1 (113/114) but misses all 28 two-of-six cases in which a5 = 1 is one of the two, and wrongly accepts 23 of 38 three-of-six cases that include a5 = 1 (agreement with the rule 88.0% over all 432 configurations).

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Additive composition of five children under the output sigmoid.
  • empirical_viz: Score is negative for <=1 and >=3 first-values among a1,a2,a3,a4,a6 on every configuration; positive for exactly two except mostly when a5=1.

A clipped bonus that rewards a5 != 1 and a3 = 1. Node 1223 = ReLU(2.47 + 1.41 z(a3:1) + 0.30 z(a4:3) - 1.86 z(a5:1) - 0.69*1717). Summary (from the record)

P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(z): essentially logistic regression over 44 direct inputs (married-civ-spouse -3.4 logit, education-num -1.15/SD, male -1.2, wife -1.5) plus one real nonlinearity, a concave piecewise-linear capital-gain penalty (kinks ~3.8k and 4.8k USD); removing it: train acc 0.852 -> 0.824, AUC 0.907 -> 0.888. Other hidden nodes are one-hot indicators; rare categories with standardized values 20-66 act as saturating switches.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis (supported): additive composition. Output = P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(z) (class 1 is '<=50k'). z = 1.653 + a sparse linear score over 44 directly connected standardized inputs + capital_gain_term + five one-hot indicator terms (native_country37_gate x0.030, relationship0_indicator x0.205, occupation4_indicator x-0.459, occupation2_gate x0.0086, native_country22_switch x-0.024). 57 of the 107 inputs (e.g. most native-country and several education/occupation one-hots) have no edges and are listed here as zero-effect entries; native-country:15 has a direct edge but is constant on train, so it is also inert.
Mechanism: the network is essentially logistic regression plus one nonlinear feature, a concave piecewise-linear capital-gain penalty. The direct linear part lowers P(<=50K) for married-civ-spouse (-3.38 logit when set), wives (-1.51), males (-1.18), not-in-family (-1.02), each SD of education-num (-1.15), age (-0.44), hours-per-week (-0.41) and capital-loss (-0.28); it raises it for other-service (+1.10) and farming-fishing (+1.05) occupations. Counter-intuitively, education:3/4 (1st-4th, 5th-6th grade; n=189, 406) lower P(<=50K) by ~2.0 logit when set, which partly cancels the education-num slope for these rows; I cannot give a substantive reason for this. Very rare one-hots (workclass Never-worked n=9, two native countries n=72-82, Preschool n=64) have standardized values of 20-66, so their small weights become +25 to +61 logit 'saturators' that force a <=50K prediction. Category names are inferred from PMLB's alphabetical coding.
Evidence (train, n=39073): acc 0.852, AUC 0.907, logit SD 7.25. Term SDs: capital_gain_term 5.54, direct linear 4.16, occupation4 0.26, others <0.05. Mean-ablation: capital_gain_term acc 0.852->0.824, AUC 0.907->0.888 (3571 flips); occupation4 777 flips, AUC ->0.905; relationship0 181 flips with no accuracy loss; the three rare-country/occupation gates flip <=6 predictions; the 7-node workclass_occupation_aggregator inside native_country22_switch is masked (output change exactly 0). SHAP (KernelExplainer, 500 train rows, probability scale) ranks marital-status:2 (0.173), education-num (0.092), sex and capital-gain (0.042 each), age (0.033), relationship:1 (0.030), hours-per-week (0.026) and occupation:4 (0.025) highest; capital-gain's mean |SHAP| is modest because 91% of rows have zero gain, while its ablation effect is the largest.

Evidence (3 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Additive composition at the output; 57 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries.
  • empirical_viz: Full train split. Effects are logit changes of P(<=50K) when a one-hot is set (w*(hi-lo)) or per SD for numeric inputs.
  • shap: Top features by mean |SHAP| on 500 train rows.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis (supported): the full capital-gain contribution to the logit of P(income<=50K) (identity node cg_term collects the direct edge, relay 194 and hinges 1266/8342). It is a concave, monotonically decreasing piecewise-linear function of standardized capital-gain: slope -1.62 up to x=0.359 (~3.8k USD), -3.76 up to x=0.496 (~4.8k USD), then -5.83, because ReLU 1266 = relu(0.976x-0.35) and 8342 = relu(0.893*1266-0.12) switch on in sequence and both carry negative output weights. Relay 194 = relu(1.24x - 0.485 nc20 + 0.867) is always active except for native-country:20 (Iran, 50 train rows), where it is zeroed, giving those rows a steeper linear slope (-3.11) and +0.25 logit at zero gain. Evidence (train, n=39073): term = +1.30 at zero gain (91% of rows), -0.19 at x=0.52, -7.2 at x=1.73, -74 at the 99999 cap; logit-term SD 5.54 (largest single term). Mean-ablating it drops train accuracy 0.852->0.824 and AUC 0.907->0.888 (3571 predictions flip). Interpretation: any sizeable capital gain is strong, increasingly steep evidence of income >50K. Closed-form (3 s.f.) max err 0.070.

Evidence (3 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form; concave piecewise-linear in capital-gain with two kinks.
  • empirical_viz: Full train split; ablation replaces the term by its train mean.
  • empirical_viz: Tool line plot over all 39073 train rows: the term falls monotonically from +1.54 to -74.0 across the capital-gain range (r=-0.996).

Hypothesis (supported, functionally inert): node 3996 adds up affine relays of six one-hot inputs: 3996 = relu(1.24 nc6 + 0.942 wc1 + 0.943*15610 + 0.916*2322 + 0.912*9651 + 0.30), where 9651/2447 are always-active affine relays of workclass:5 (Self-emp-inc, inferred), 3479->16792 are exact indicators of occupation:3 (Craft-repair, inferred) that feed 2322 together with occupation:3 and native-country:41, and 15610 is a workclass:1 relay that switches off only for occupation:2 rows. On train it takes 13 distinct values in [0.46, 32.3] and is always positive. Its only consumer is node 594 in native_country22_switch, which outputs >=13 whenever native-country:22 is set and 0 otherwise regardless of 3996 (3996 would need to exceed ~99). So the whole 7-node subtree is masked: setting 3996 to 0 or to its train maximum changes the network output by exactly 0 on all 39073 train rows. It is evolutionary residue with no effect on the predictions; I found no meaningful named function for it beyond 'workclass/occupation/country one-hot score'.

Summary (from the record)

Descending linear ramp switches the output off at >=3 first values; a single ReLU gate (node 217) fires at 0-1 and suppresses via -5.64: sigmoid(Ramp - 1.20 - 5.64 Gate), peaking at exactly two. Mirrors the paper's construction with reversed ramp.

Agreement with the MONK-2 rule (record): Ranking matches 'exactly two of six' on all 432 configurations (AUC 1.0); at 0.5 it computes 'exactly two except most pairs with a6=1 and some a2&a4 / a4&a5', 89% of 432 correct.

Hypothesis (DB):

Output = sigmoid(Ramp - 1.20 - 5.64*Gate): an additive composition under the output sigmoid. Unconnected inputs a2:2, a4:2, a4:3, a5:2, a5:3 and a5:4 are zero-effect entries; the model never consults them. When no indicator is active the gate is about 13, and its -5.64 readout overwhelms the ramp (logit about -54). With one active indicator the gate still wins (logit <= -8.96). With two, the gate is (almost) off and the logit equals the ramp, -3.34 to +5.63. With three or more, the ramp itself is <= -3.41. So the network produces a peak at count two of the six rule indicators. The ramp makes the upper edge and the gate makes the lower edge: the mirror image of a single gate plus ramp construction. Because the ramp weights are uneven, the peak is not level. Pairs involving a6=1 (with a1, a2, a4 or a5) get logits -3.34 to -1.07 and fall below p=0.5, and so do some a2&a4 and a4&a5 configurations; a3&a6 stays positive because I3 is light. Train evidence (n=345): AUC 1.0, since every count-2 logit (>= -3.337) exceeds every other logit (<= -3.408), a margin of only 0.07. Accuracy at 0.5 is 0.890: 38 false negatives, all count-2 rows, and no false positives. Local ablation with the gate set to 0 drops train accuracy to 0.632 and turns every count<=1 row positive.

Evidence (2 records, DB):

Hypothesis (DB):

A fewer-than-two-indicators gate. Write I_k = 1 when attribute k takes its first value (a3:2 = 1-I3 and a6:2 = 1-I6, since a3 and a6 are binary). In these terms node 217 computes ReLU(13.02 - 8.77 I1 - 7.32 I2 - 6.57 I3 - 6.43 I4 - 9.36 I5 - 7.15 I6 - 0.20[a1=3] + 0.39[a2=3]), a near-uniform weighted count of active indicators (weights 6.4 to 9.4) subtracted from 13. It outputs about 13 when no indicator is active, 3.5 to 7.0 when exactly one is, and zero once two or more are. The one leak: the lightest pair (I3+I4) leaves at most +0.41, so the gate fires weakly on 6% of count-2 configurations. Evidence (train, n=345): node 217 ranges 12.82-13.40 at count 0, 3.46-6.98 at count 1, 0-0.41 at count 2, and exactly 0 at count>=3; sensitivities are about 0.8-1.15 for the six indicator columns and about 0.03-0.05 for a1:3 and a2:3, which are negligible.

y0=−4.17xa1:1_a−0.25xa1:2−4.47xa2:1_a−0.212xa2:3_a−3.32xa3:1−0.692xa3:2_a−4.63xa4:1_a−3.92xa5:1_a−4.77xa6:1+1.2xa6:2_a\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= - 4.17 x_{a1:1\_a} \\ &\quad - 0.25 x_{a1:2} \\ &\quad - 4.47 x_{a2:1\_a} \\ &\quad - 0.212 x_{a2:3\_a} \\ &\quad - 3.32 x_{a3:1} \\ &\quad - 0.692 x_{a3:2\_a} \\ &\quad - 4.63 x_{a4:1\_a} \\ &\quad - 3.92 x_{a5:1\_a} \\ &\quad - 4.77 x_{a6:1} \\ &\quad + 1.2 x_{a6:2\_a} \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

A descending linear count ramp. The direct input-to-output connections sum, in rule-indicator terms, to 20.80 - 8.72 I1 - 9.45 I2 - 5.25 I3 - 10.01 I4 - 9.04 I5 - 11.95 I6 - 0.53[a1=2] - 0.45[a2=3]. a3 and a6 enter through both of their one-hot columns, which combine into single indicator weights. Each active indicator subtracts 5 to 12, and the weights are not uniform: I6 is heaviest (11.95) and I3 lightest (5.25). With the output bias (-1.20) the ramp is +18.6 to +19.6 at count 0, +6.7 to +14.4 at count 1, -3.3 to +5.6 at count 2, and at most -3.41 at every count>=3 (train). It forms the upper edge of the response: three or more active indicators always switch the output off. Evidence: closed form, plus per-count ranges on the train split (n=345).

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form of the direct input-to-output sum, rewritten in rule-indicator terms.
  • empirical_viz: Ramp plus output bias falls monotonically with the number of active indicators; it is below -3.4 for every count>=3 row.

Generalised additive logistic model of P(income<=50K): logit = 2.407 + capital + household + education + work + background, no cross-group interactions. Train acc 0.850, AUC 0.906.

Output = logit P(income <= 50K) (train target y=1 is <=50K, base rate 0.761); positive = toward low income. Inputs z-scored; category names inferred from alphabetical codes, consistent with train frequencies. ROOT. HYPOTHESIS: a generalised additive logistic model, logit = 2.407 + capital + household + education + work + background, with no cross-group interactions (every hidden relu sees inputs from one feature group). EVIDENCE (train n=39,073): acc 0.850, AUC 0.9064; best all-affine fit of the logit has AUC 0.9008 (residual sd 0.59 of logit sd 7.53), so ~0.0055 AUC is due to nonlinearity, mostly capital gain. Block mean-ablation AUCs: capital 0.884, household 0.856, education 0.884, work 0.891, background 0.898. SHAP (compute_shap, train, max_samples=500): marital-status:2 0.168, education-num 0.080, capital-gain 0.042, sex 0.042, age 0.037, relationship:0 0.036, hours-per-week 0.028. Summary (from the record)

Linear ramp over first values of a2,a3,a4,a6 (a1 weak) plus a count gate (1158, -6.92) that fires at three of {a2,a3,a4,a6} (or a3 plus one other with a1!=3), a direct a5=1 veto (-15.7), a small a5=3 penalty, an always-zero chain and an always-active affine node. Train acc 0.786, AUC 0.794.

Agreement with the MONK-2 rule (record): Rough 'about two first values' peak counting a2,a3,a4,a6 (a1 weakly) with a5=1 as a veto: 65 false negatives (all exactly-two: 28 a5 veto, 16 gate, 21 weak ramp) and 34 false positives on 432 inputs.

Hypothesis (DB):

The output composes the five children additively under the final sigmoid: logit = 0.371 + Ramp + Veto - 6.921*Gate - 0.207*A5_3 - 0.125*Inert (Inert identically zero). Inputs a1:2 and a4:3 have no enabled connections and are zero-effect entries. With a5 in {3,4} the baseline logit is about -4.99; the ramp adds a1=1 +1.25, a2=1 +5.24, a3=1 +3.70, a4=1 +2.28, a6=1 +4.05, so it turns positive once about two strong indicators (a2,a3,a4,a6) are present (lower edge of a response peak). The count gate pulls the logit back down when three of {a2,a3,a4,a6} are first-valued (upper edge), weakly also for a3 plus one other. The a5=1 veto makes the output negative whenever a5=1; a5=3 subtracts a further 0.46-0.60. Net: an approximate 'about two of {a2,a3,a4,a6} (a1 weak), and a5 must not be 1' peak detector. Evidence: closed form composition; train sensitivity of the output (gate 0.53, ramp and veto 0.076 each, 708 0.016, 1057 0.010, unconnected 0); enumeration: 111/432 positive; by total indicator count k: k=0 0%, k=1 4%, k=2 54%, k=3 27%, k>=4 0%. Against the MONK-2 target: 65 false negatives all at k=2 (28 with a5=1 vetoed; 16 a3+one-other pairs suppressed by the gate; 21 where the ramp is too weak: 20 pairs a1=1 with a3, a4 or a6, plus one a3+a4 pair with a1=3), 34 false positives (30 at k=3, mostly a1=1 plus two others where the gate is weak or silent; 4 at k=1 with a2=1 alone). Train accuracy 0.786, AUC 0.794; function preservation error 3.3e-16.

Hypothesis (DB):

A veto on a5=1. The direct edge a5:1 -> output has weight -6.82 on the z-score: +3.96 when a5!=1, -11.74 when a5=1, a jump of -15.70. Summary (from the record)

Mostly logistic regression: 14 direct edges (logit SD 3.42, train AUC 0.926 alone). One nonlinear block (logit SD 1.04): a two-gate sex x exercise-angina interaction; gate 1213 scores 'female without exercise angina' (read out -0.760), gate 47 fires for no-angina patients with low 1213 score (mostly men) and adds +0.384. Exercise angina has no direct edge, so its whole effect runs through this block. Block adds +0.020 train AUC (0.926 -> 0.946). slope:1 term (3660) is an inert affine pass-through.

Recorded formula (evidence record)
h1213=relu⁡(1.23xsex:0+1.31xexang:0−0.509xcp:2−0.563xfbs:0+0.476xthal:7+0.091),  g47=relu⁡(1.43+0.956xexang:0−1.93h1213)\begin{gathered}h_{1213}=\operatorname{relu}(1.23x_{sex:0}+1.31x_{exang:0}-0.509x_{cp:2}-0.563x_{fbs:0}+0.476x_{thal:7}+0.091),\; g_{47}=\operatorname{relu}(1.43+0.956x_{exang:0}-1.93h_{1213})\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: a sex x exercise-angina interaction built from two chained ReLU gates. Gate 1213 = relu(1.23 sex:0 + 1.31 exang:0 - 0.509 cp:2 - 0.563 fbs:0 + 0.476 thal:7 + 0.091) is a female-without-exercise-angina score; gate 47 = relu(1.43 + 0.956 exang:0 - 1.93 h1213) fires for patients without exercise angina whose 1213 score is low (mostly men) and is shut off by 1213. The output reads -0.760 h1213 + 0.384 g47. Evidence (train, n=242): group mean block logit is +0.04 (male, exang), +0.18 (male, no exang), -0.39 (female, exang), -1.76 (female, no exang). Exercise angina has no direct edge to the output, so its entire effect is this block: flipping exang no->yes raises the logit by +1.81 on average for women (range 0.78..2.11) but by -0.17 for men (range -0.78..1.87). g47 is active for 84% of men without angina but 19% of women without angina. cp:2, fbs:0 and thal:7 only shift h1213 (sensitivities 0.22-0.26 vs 0.57-0.60 for sex:0/exang:0). Odd signs (thal:7 and fbs:1 making the block slightly less protective / more protective respectively) are small modifiers we do not interpret clinically. Ablating gate 47 to its mean drops train AUC 0.9457->0.9414; ablating 1213->output drops it to 0.9347.

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form: one ReLU gate on sex:0/exang:0 (plus small cp:2, fbs:0, thal:7 modifiers) and a second gate inhibited by it.
  • empirical_viz: Train split, full sample (242). The block is a sex x exercise-angina interaction: flipping exang from no to yes raises the logit by +1.81 for women on average but by -0.17 for men.

Summary (from the record)

logit P(income<=50K): bias + eight disjoint additive terms. Mostly linear: household block (marital, relationship, sex) largest (ablation AUC 0.910 -> 0.853), then numeric terms and category offsets. Three nonlinear pockets: a one-knot capital-gain ReLU; a youth gate (below-median age, threshold moved by Handlers-cleaners); hub 350, an off-switch shared by Exec-managerial, Farming-fishing, Doctorate, Without-pay and Armed-Forces. Train acc 0.854, AUC 0.910.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root composition: P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(1.127 + capital_gain_effect + age_youth_gate + occupation_hub_350 + race_white_effect + gated_category_offsets[idn_gatedcats] - 0.115*gated_category_offsets[10878] - 0.0056*gated_category_offsets[7734] + household_linear + numeric_linear + category_linear). The composition is purely additive in logit space. Children share no nodes and none feeds another, so the network is a generalised additive model with a few interaction pockets, all inside children: the capital-gain knot (with a native-country:32 knot shift), the age x occupation:6 youth gate, the shared off-switch of hub 350, and the occupation:7 switch in 3845. Ablation ranking on train (term replaced by its mean; baseline acc 0.854 / AUC 0.910): household_linear (AUC 0.853, 13.3% of predictions flip) > capital_gain_effect (0.892, 8.1%) > numeric_linear (0.893, 7.0%) > age_youth_gate (0.903, 5.2%) > category_linear (0.905, 3.2%) > occupation_hub_350 (0.906, 2.5%) > gated_category_offsets (0.909, 1.2%) > race_white_effect (0.910, 0.7%). SHAP on the full model (train, max_samples=500) agrees: top features are marital-status:2 0.122, relationship:0 0.081, relationship:1 0.061, age 0.049, education-num 0.047, capital-gain 0.045, relationship:5 0.027, relationship:4 0.026. 42 of 107 inputs have no enabled edge and are zero-effect entries of this root: -4, -6, -9, -15, -20, -21, -22, -29, -32, -33, -34, -35, -37, -39, -41, -44, -54, -59, -66, -67, -68, -69, -73, -74, -75, -77, -78, -79, -80, -81, -82, -83, -84, -90, -91, -93, -94, -97, -99, -102, -103, -107. Output class 1 = <=50K; category names are inferred from PMLB alphabetical label encoding.

Closed form:

y0=−2.49xcapital−gain−2.32relu⁡(0.576xcapital−gain−0.0522xnative−country:32−0.274)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= - 2.49 x_{capital-gain} \\ &\quad - 2.32 \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.576 x_{capital-gain} - 0.0522 x_{native-country:32} - 0.274 \right)} \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Capital-gain term (exit idn_capgain, added to the output logit): f = -2.49*cg - 2.32*relu(0.576*cg - 0.0522*nc32 - 0.274), inputs z-scored. For the 91.6% of train rows with zero capital gain (cg_z=-0.146) the gate is off and f=+0.36. The ReLU 1690 opens at cg_z=0.476 (5.2% of rows), steepening the slope from -2.49 to -3.83 per SD: a monotone one-knot piecewise-linear decrease in logit P(<=50K). Any substantial gain forces a >50K prediction (f=-5.7 at cg_z=1.66, -50 at the max). native-country:32 (Portugal, 51 rows) shifts the knot to cg_z~3.0 for those rows only. Evidence: line plot on the full train split (39,073 rows) gives corr(cg, f)=-0.999; ablation (term replaced by its train mean) drops train accuracy 0.854->0.838 and AUC 0.910->0.892 and flips 8.1% of predictions, the largest nonlinear term. Category names (in parentheses) are inferred from PMLB's alphabetical label encoding and checked against category frequency and P(<=50K) on train; the network sees only the index. Output class 1 is income <=50K (train base rate 0.761), so negative terms push toward >50K.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hub ReLU 350 plus direct occupation/workclass terms (exit idn_hub350). Every input is a one-hot, so on the data the subgraph is a lookup table over 16 observed category combinations. 7974 (occupation:4 only) and the 10971->3077 chain (native-country:4 only) are single-input relays. With none of the seven categories set, 350=1.21 and f=+0.33. Each of occupation:4 (Exec-managerial), occupation:5 (Farming-fishing), occupation:2 (Armed-Forces), education:10 (Doctorate) and workclass:8 (Without-pay) turns 350 off; the direct weights then set the category value: Exec-managerial f=-0.35, Doctorate +0.04, Farming-fishing +1.33, Without-pay +1.03, Armed-Forces +0.34, Sales (occupation:12) +0.12 with 350 still on. native-country:4 (Columbia, 64 rows, 98% <=50K) drives 350 to ~43.5 and f to +10.4, a hard-coded 'Columbia => <=50K' rule. So the hub works as an off-switch shared by several high- or low-income categories, plus one memorised country rule. Evidence: per-combination enumeration on full train; sensitivity on train (largest: native-country:4 0.34, occupation:4 0.23); ablation flips 2.5% of predictions, AUC 0.910->0.906. Category names (in parentheses) are inferred from PMLB's alphabetical label encoding and checked against category frequency and P(<=50K) on train; the network sees only the index. Hypothesis (DB):

Linear one-hot offsets (exit idn_catlinear) for the remaining workclass, education, occupation, race and native-country categories. Inputs are z-scored one-hots, so a rare category gets a large on-value and a small weight becomes a large effect. On-vs-off logit effects: occupation:9 (Priv-house-serv) +6.27, native-country:38 (Trinadad&Tobago) +3.23, native-country:35 (South) +1.32, native-country:40 (Vietnam) +1.23, education:13 (Preschool) +1.16, native-country:29 (Peru) +1.15, occupation:0 (unknown) +1.06, education:14 (Prof-school) -0.72. Most are rare low-income categories, memorised as offsets. Evidence: sensitivity on full train equals |weights|; ablation flips 3.2% of predictions, AUC 0.910->0.905. Category names (in parentheses) are inferred from PMLB's alphabetical label encoding and checked against category frequency and P(<=50K) on train; the network sees only the index. Output class 1 is income <=50K (train base rate 0.761), so negative terms push toward >50K.

Summary (from the record)

Output = sigmoid(1.383 + Ramp - 4.009 Veto - 0.888 Pool). Ramp is a descending linear count of first-value indicators (positive only when <=2 active); Pool is a rectified count of I4 and I5; Veto fires when <=1 indicator is active and overrides the ramp. Net: a window on exactly two active indicators. Train accuracy 0.991, AUC 1.0.

Agreement with the MONK-2 rule (record): 428/432 configurations agree with the MONK-2 rule; all 4 disagreements are a2=1 & a5=1 veto-leak cases. Implements the window in reverse to the paper's model: descending ramp sets the upper edge, low-count veto sets the lower edge.

Annotations (root → compositions → leaves)

Closed forms are computed live with the same code as get_formula(force=True) on the replayed model state; a composition is shown with its children as named functions. Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 345 training rows.

Closed form (children as functions):

y0=10.251e0.888x389−1.0linear_count_ramp⁡(−1a,−4a,−7a,−9a,−12a,−17)+4.01low_count_veto_gate⁡(−1b,−4b,−6,−7b,−16,x389)+1\begin{gathered}y_0 = \frac{1}{0.251 e^{0.888 x_{389} - 1.0 \operatorname{linear\_count\_ramp}{\left(-1_{a},-4_{a},-7_{a},-9_{a},-12_{a},-17 \right)} + 4.01 \operatorname{low\_count\_veto\_gate}{\left(-1_{b},-4_{b},-6,-7_{b},-16,x_{389} \right)}} + 1}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Exactly-two window = descending ramp minus low-count veto. Output = sigmoid(1.383 + Ramp - 4.009 Veto - 0.888 Pool). The linear part (bias + ramp + pool readout) by number of active first-value indicators: 0 -> 18.1, 1 -> 9.2 to 13.8, 2 -> 0.49 to 5.67, 3 -> -8.0 to -2.75, 4 or more -> below -11.5; it is positive iff at most two indicators are active (upper edge of the window). The veto is at least 5.16 whenever at most one indicator is active, so -4.009 Veto <= -20.7 overrides the ramp's maximum of 18.1 (lower edge). The output is therefore above 0.5 exactly when two indicators are active, with one exception: for count two made of a2=1 and a5=1, the veto leaks 0.62, and 0.62 x 4.009 = 2.49 exceeds the ramp margin 1.56 (pre-activation -0.93), so the 4 such configurations (a1 in {2,3}, a2=1, a3=2, a4 in {2,3}, a5=1, a6=2) are scored negative. The inputs a1:2, a1:3, a2:2, a3:2, a4:3, a5:2, a5:3 have no enabled connections and zero effect; they are listed here as zero-effect entry nodes. EVIDENCE: Train split (n=345, full sample): accuracy 0.991, AUC 1.000. Linear part (bias + ramp - 0.888 pool) per count: 0 -> 18.11; 1 -> 9.22..13.75; 2 -> 0.49..5.67; 3 -> -7.98..-2.75; 4 -> -16.39..-11.48; 5 -> -24.48..-20.37; 6 -> -29.50. Output > 0.5 for 0% of count 0/1/3/4/5/6 rows and 97.3% of count 2 rows; the 3 misses are the a2=1,a5=1 veto leak (output 0.283). Sensitivity of the output: veto 0.213, ramp 0.053, pool 0.047, all seven unconnected inputs 0.0. Over all 432 configurations the network agrees with 'exactly two indicators' on 428 (the 4 a2=1,a5=1 count-2 configurations are the only disagreements).

Closed form (children as functions):

y0=relu⁡(−5.12xa1:1_b−3.69xa2:1_b+0.351xa2:3−4.92xa3:1_b−5.91xa6:1−3.38a4a5firstvaluepool(−10,−9b,−12b,−15)−0.156)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 5.12 x_{a1:1\_b} \\ &\quad - 3.69 x_{a2:1\_b} \\ &\quad + 0.351 x_{a2:3} \\ &\quad - 4.92 x_{a3:1\_b} \\ &\quad - 5.91 x_{a6:1} \\ &\quad - 3.38 a_{4 a5 first value pool}{\left(-10,-9_{b},-12_{b},-15 \right)} \\ &\quad -0.156 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Low-count veto gate, a serial composition Veto(a1, a2, a3, a6, Pool(a4, a5)). Node 288 = ReLU(17.125 - 10.71 I1 - 7.81 I2 + 0.74 [a2=3] - 9.85 I3 - 11.82 I6 - 3.378 Pool). Through the pool, I4 alone subtracts 10.3 (12.0 when a5=4), I5 alone 8.7, both 21.5. Every active first-value indicator thus removes 7.8 to 11.8 from a bias of 17.1: the gate is on (5.16 to 17.87) for every configuration with zero or one active indicators and off for two or more, with one exception: I2 + I5 (a2=1 and a5=1) leaves 17.125 - 7.81 - 8.69 = 0.62 > 0, a small leak. So 288 detects 'at most one of the six rule indicators is active'. EVIDENCE: Train split (n=345, full sample), by number of active first-value indicators: count 0 (19 rows) gate 17.13..17.87, on 100%; count 1 (70) gate 5.16..9.32, on 100%; count 2 (113) on 2.7% (3 rows, all a2=1 and a5=1, value 0.62); count >=3 (143) off 100%. Sensitivities: a6:1 1.58, a1:1 1.37, a3:1 1.31, a2:1 0.98, pool 0.90, a2:3 0.09. Over all 432 configurations the same pattern holds (on for count <=1; on at count 2 only for the 4 a2=1,a5=1 configurations).

Hypothesis (DB):

A4/a5 first-value pool (with an inert a4:2 sub-unit). Write I_k for 'attribute k takes its first value'. In indicator form node 389 = ReLU(-0.744 + 3.793 I4 + 3.317 I5 + 0.492 [a5=4] - 0.0006 u), where u = node 2443 = ReLU(0.997 [a4=2] - 1.281) is identically zero on the whole domain (maximum pre-activation -0.284), so the a4:2 branch is inert (and its readout weight is -0.0006 anyway). With neither a4 nor a5 at its first value the pool outputs 0 (pre-activation -0.744 or -0.252); a4=1 alone gives 3.05 (3.54 when a5=4), a5=1 alone gives 2.57, both give 6.37. The pool is therefore a rectified, near-additive count of the two rule indicators I4 and I5, which the downstream gate does not receive directly. EVIDENCE: Train split (n=345, full sample): node 2443 is 0 on every row; sensitivity of the pool to a4:2 is 0.0, to a4:1 0.86, a5:1 0.71, a5:4 0.10. The pool takes exactly five values on train: 0 (176 rows), 2.573 (a5=1, 62), 3.049 (a4=1, 57), 3.541 (a4=1, a5=4, 25), 6.366 (a4=1 and a5=1, 25).

Hypothesis (DB):

Ramp falls with weighted indicator count (upper edge); L subtracts up to 41.6 when there are 0-1 indicators (lower edge); P adds an extra penalty (0.918 x 0.95..13.4) when >=2 of a2/a3/a6 are first values and, through L, closes the lower edge. Unconnected inputs a4:2, a4:3, a5:2, a5:3 (no enabled edges) have zero effect; a4 and a5 are read only through a4:1, a5:1, a5:4. Evidence: mean output pre-activation by number of first values (432 inputs): -26.9, -15.4, +0.55, -5.4, -13.2, -21.3, -29.7 for 0..6, a peak at two. Positive predictions: 0/24, 9/92 (8 of them a1=1 alone), 87/142, 4/113, 0/61. The peak is imperfect because the indicators are weighted unequally: a4=1 and a5=1 each count almost double, so pairs containing a5 and {a2,a4},{a4,a5} mostly score negative, while a1=1 alone often scores positive. Train (n=345): accuracy 0.855, AUC 0.946; agreement with the MONK-2 rule on all 432 inputs 0.843. Train sensitivity of output: L 0.31, Ramp 0.053, P 0.049.

Summary (from the record)

Additive logit under a saturating sigmoid, dominated by ReLU node 263 (about 19 with no first values, dropping 6.8-9.3 per first value of a2, a3, a4, a6). Direct linear term penalises a1=1 and a5=1 (about -15 each) and gives a1=3 +24.9. Nodes 1855 and 3471 are minor.

Agreement with the MONK-2 rule (record): Learned only the upper edge (>=3 first values, >=4 when a1=2, makes output negative); no lower edge, so 0-1 first values get the highest logits; ignores the count entirely when a1=3. Predicts positive on 85.5% of train rows; train accuracy 0.472.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: additive composition under the output sigmoid, logit = 2.58 + Linear + 5.14*Ramp + 1.53*A5not4 + 0.105*A6. a4:2, a4:3, a5:3 have no enabled connections (zero-effect entries). The model is an upper-edge-only count detector: for a1 in {1,2} it is positive while few attributes take their first value and negative once about three of {a2,a3,a4,a6} (a1=1) or four (a1=2) do; a5=1 counts only through Linear's -14.8, which is not enough to flip a1=1 inputs with one other first value. There is no lower edge: inputs with zero or one first value get the largest logits. a1=3 inputs are all positive (107/107 on train) via Linear's +24.9. Evidence (train, n=345): positive rate by (a1, count) - a1=1: count<=2 100%, 3 74%, >=4 0%; a1=2: count<=3 100%, 4 29%, 5 0%; a1=3: 100% at every count. Predicts positive on 85.5% of train rows (accuracy 0.472 at 0.5). Logits reach |~130| so the sigmoid saturates; the sigmoid-output AUC 0.807 is inflated by ties at 1.0, the logit ranking AUC is 0.734. Compared with the MONK-2 target (exactly two first values): the network captures only the upper edge (>=3-4 first values -> negative) and none of the lower edge (0-1 -> negative), and ignores the count entirely when a1=3.

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing structural. Closed-form error 0.065 is 3-s.f. rounding on a linear leaf with range -33..+32. The a1=1/count-3 boundary is pattern-specific (74% positive), described via per-indicator weights rather than a clean rule. One root evidence payload says a1=3 '108/108 positive' (correct: 107/107; narrative corrected, payload corrected by the 2026-11-11 errata).

Tool notes (record): Root annotate failed when subgraph_nodes included child exits ('already covered'); worked with output + unconnected inputs. Sigmoid saturation (|logit| up to ~130) makes many outputs tie at exactly 1.0, so the sigmoid AUC (0.807, = fitness) is higher than the logit ranking AUC (0.734).

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: direct_linear (0.065), then few_first_values_ramp (0.0413). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • 6 split(s), all of input nodes (an input feeding two annotations). These are routine; check only that each input copy sits in the annotation whose hypothesis uses it.
  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Summary (from the record)

Almost a sparse logistic regression on 55 of 107 inputs (direct edges carry logit SD 3.37 of 3.85; mean-ablating every hidden unit: acc 0.856 -> 0.838, AUC 0.910 -> 0.895). One consequential nonlinearity: an age hinge turning the age slope into a U-shape (high-income share peaks mid-career; keeping only that unit recovers AUC 0.904). Remaining hidden units are affine relays, category lookups, or dead structure.

Hypothesis (DB):

ROOT (supported). Output 0 = sigmoid(z), z = 1.399 + 48 direct input terms + 12 hidden readouts (9 child annotations); 52 of the 107 one-hot/standardized inputs are unconnected and listed here as zero-effect entries. Class 1 is the 76% majority (presumably <=50K), so negative weights push toward high income. The model is essentially a sparse logistic regression with one consequential nonlinearity. Direct edges carry logit SD 3.37 of 3.85 (mean-ablating them drops train AUC 0.910->0.518); all hidden readouts together carry SD 1.32 and mean-ablating every hidden unit costs only acc 0.856->0.838, AUC 0.910->0.895. The only nonlinearity that matters is age_late_career_hinge (4647): keeping it alone recovers acc 0.850 / AUC 0.904. It turns the direct age slope (-0.88) into a U-shaped age effect with its minimum at age z~0.8. The other children are lookups or affine relays: capital_gain_affine_relay steepens the capital-gain slope to -2.54/SD; relationship1_indicator (-1.03 for relationship:1), occupation0_country0_gate (+0.92 for occupation:0 unless native-country:0), occupation8_relays (+0.45) and occupation1_relays (+0.37) are category offsets; country32_affine_relay and the native-country:4 part of the age hinge memorise rare countries; occupation6_relationship1_gate is near-inert (<=0.10 logit); dead_relationship_chain (613->2245->8678->170) and node 2114 are identically 0 on every valid input. Children combine ADDITIVELY in the logit (each child exit has one readout edge into node 0; no child feeds another). Largest exact logit-space attributions (mean |phi|, full train): relationship:0 0.82, education-num 0.72, marital-status:2 0.70, capital-gain 0.68, age 0.51, relationship:1 0.39, relationship:5 0.24, sex 0.23, occupation:8 0.21, hours-per-week 0.18.

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(0.439xcapital−gain_b+0.85)\begin{gathered}y_0 = \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.439 x_{capital-gain\_b} + 0.85 \right)}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

SUPPORTED: affine relay. 1870 = ReLU(0.439*capital-gain + 0.850) never clips on train, so it is a linear rescaling of capital-gain that adds -0.702*cg - 1.359 to the logit and steepens the direct capital-gain term (-1.841) to a total slope of -2.54 per SD. No nonlinearity is used on the data domain (the knot sits at cg z = -1.94, below the data minimum -0.147). EVIDENCE: Always active on train (pre-activation in [0.786, 6.636], 39,073/39,073 rows), so on the data domain 1870 = 0.439*cg + 0.850 exactly and its logit contribution is -0.702*cg - 1.359 (range [-10.61, -1.26], SD 0.70). Combined with the direct edge (-1.841), the total capital-gain slope is -2.54 logit per SD, pushing toward class 0 (the 24% minority, presumably >50K). line_plot on train (39,073 rows): exit vs capital-gain correlation 1.000 (exactly linear over the observed range); 91.6% of rows sit at the zero-gain floor (cg z = -0.147). Mean-ablation of 1870 (replace by train mean): acc 0.8558->0.8553, AUC 0.9099->0.9093 (small, because the direct edge carries the same signal).

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(1.25xage_b+0.711xnative−country:4−0.968)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 1.25 x_{age\_b} \\ &\quad + 0.711 x_{native-country:4} \\ &\quad -0.968 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

SUPPORTED: a single-knot age hinge giving a U-shaped (in class-1 logit) age effect. Below age z~0.80 the direct age term dominates (class-1 logit falls with age, i.e. the high-income share rises); above the knot 4647 reverses the slope to +0.65 per SD, so older workers drift back toward class 1, matching the empirical rate (minimum P(y=1) ~0.60 near z 0.8). native-country:4 (64 rows, standardized value 24.7) rides on the same unit as a large class-1 offset (memorisation of a rare category). EVIDENCE: Knot (for rows not in native-country:4, where nc4 = -0.041) at age z = 0.798. Active for 21.9% of those rows. Net age effect on logit = -0.881*age + 1.224*ReLU(1.249*age + 0.711*nc4 - 0.968): slope -0.881 below the knot and +0.648 above it. Logit contribution range [0, 24.36], SD 1.00 (the largest hidden-node contribution). The 64 native-country:4 rows (value 24.69) have 4647 ~ 16.6 (+20 logit), i.e. they are forced to class 1. line_plot on train (39,073 rows): exit 0 below z~0.8 then linear; scatter exit range [0, 19.9] (the top from nc4 rows). Local binned net age effect (non-nc4 rows): z=-1.5: +1.31, z=-1: +0.88, z=0: -0.02, z=0.5: -0.44, z=0.8: -0.67 (minimum), z=1.5: -0.26, z=2: +0.07, z=3: +0.73. Empirical P(y=1) follows the same U: 0.999, 0.944, 0.664, 0.606, 0.597, 0.662, 0.764, 0.816. Mean-ablation of 4647: acc 0.8558->0.8436, AUC 0.9099->0.9009 (largest hidden-node effect).

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. Most hidden structure trivial on the domain: five units never clip (affine relays); 2114 and the 4-deep chain 613->2245->8678->170 are identically 0 for every valid one-hot input (shown analytically); three readouts <0.02. Only the age hinge 4647 is consequential. native-country:4 and :32 are memorised rare categories. No semantic category names claimed.

Tool notes (record): compute_shap (500) ran ~20 min at load ~90 with no result; killed and replaced by an exact local logit-space interventional Shapley on full train (additivity error 0.0014). get_coverage needs child-exit->output readout edges in the root's subgraph_connections (redone).

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: country32_affine_relay (0.0121). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in occupation0_country0_gate: “SUPPORTED: an AND-NOT gate: +0.92 class-1 logit for occupation:0 workers, cancelled when native-country:0 is set (34 rows).” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in capital_gain_affine_relay: “EVIDENCE: Always active on train (pre-activation in [0.786, 6.636], 39,073/39,073 rows), so on the data domain 1870 = 0.439*cg + 0.850 exactly and its logit contribution is -0.702*cg - 1.359 (range [-10.61, -1.26], SD 0.70).” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?

Summary (from the record)

Essentially logistic regression on 15 inputs (logit SD 4.96); ca effective weight 2.60 via direct edge plus affine 148. Four small additive one-sided corrections (combined logit SD 1.41): oldpeak hinge above +0.39 SD; protective no-exercise-angina gate (stronger for women); -3.19 correction for fixed thal defect with normal fbs (n=10); near-inert cp:2 offset. Readouts fixed at means: train AUC 0.9437 -> 0.9295.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: logit z = -0.954 + LINEAR CORE + 1.893*vessel_count_linear_boost - 0.452*sex_exang_protective_gate - 0.942*fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate + 1.108*oldpeak_hinge - 0.154*cp2_constant_offset; prediction = sigmoid(z) (get_formula shows the output node as ReLU, but the evaluator overrides it with sigmoid for binary classification; compute_performance on train, AUC 0.9437 and acc 0.888, matches sigmoid(z)). LINEAR CORE (standardised inputs): +2.065 ca, +1.665 sex:1, -0.070 sex:0, +1.298 slope:2, -0.499 slope:1, +1.075 chol, -0.972 cp:3, -0.916 cp:1, +0.618 cp:4, -0.057 cp:2, -0.667 fbs:1, +0.616 trestbps, +0.461 thal:7, -0.419 thalach, +0.205 age. Inputs restecg:0/1/2, exang:1, slope:3 and thal:3 are disconnected in the phenotype and enter the root with zero effect. CHILDREN (all additive, read out directly by the output; no serial composition): vessel_count_linear_boost is affine (never clips), raising the effective ca weight to 2.60; sex_exang_protective_gate lowers the logit by 0.43 (men) or 1.67 (women) only when there is no exercise angina; oldpeak_hinge adds 1.11 per SD of ST depression above +0.39 SD (the only oldpeak pathway); fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate subtracts 3.19 for the 10 training patients with a fixed thallium defect and normal fasting sugar (likely an overfitted correction); cp2_constant_offset is a near-inert -0.044 offset for cp:2. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): the linear core dominates (logit sd 4.96 vs 1.41 for all readouts); with every readout fixed at its mean, train AUC is 0.9295 and accuracy 0.860, vs 0.9437 and 0.888 for the full model. SHAP (probability scale) ranks ca 0.158, sex:1 0.104, slope:2 0.092, cp:3 0.053, chol 0.044, cp:4 0.041. So the network is a logistic regression (more vessels, male sex, flat ST slope, high cholesterol, asymptomatic chest pain mean more risk) with two clinically plausible one-sided terms (marked ST depression adds risk; no exertional angina lowers it, more for women) and one small-sample correction.

Evidence (4 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Root closed form: affine core in 15 inputs plus five child readouts; sigmoid at output.
  • shap_importance: Train-split SHAP (probability scale): ca 0.158, sex:1 0.104, slope:2 0.092, cp:3 0.053, chol 0.044, cp:4 0.041 dominate; restecg, exang:1, slope:3, thal:3 are exactly 0 (disconnected).
  • ablation_study: Linear core carries most of the logit variance (sd 4.96 vs 1.41 for all readouts). Readouts add +0.014 train AUC and +2.9 points accuracy; the largest single effects are the fixed-defect gate and the oldpeak hinge.
  • performance_metrics: Train performance of the explained network (sigmoid output).

Note: the analytical_formula stored with this annotation's evidence differs from the live text (it was recorded at explanation time, with that day's tooling). Both are shown; the live one is authoritative.

Recorded formula (evidence record)
y0=relu⁡(1.16xfbs:0+1.02xthal:6−1.03)\begin{gathered}y_0 = \operatorname{relu}\left(1.16 x_{fbs:0} + 1.02 x_{thal:6} - 1.03\right)\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Node 2034 = ReLU(-1.027 + 1.156*fbs:0 + 1.016*thal:6), read out with -0.942. An AND gate: it is 3.386 only for patients with a fixed thallium defect (thal:6) AND normal fasting blood sugar (n=10 on train), 0.018 for fixed-defect patients with high sugar (n=5), and 0 for everyone else (93.8%). It subtracts 3.19 logits for that small group. Evidence suggests it is a training-set correction rather than a clinical rule: among the 10, the linear core over-predicted 4 of 5 negatives as positive; the gate moves all 5 negatives below 0 while the 5 positives stay above 0. This is the only thal:6 pathway and the only fbs:0 pathway. Mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.9437 -> 0.9388 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.872 (largest single-gate effect), but it rests on 10 patients, so treat it as likely overfitted.

  • empirical_viz: AND gate: 3.386 only for fixed-defect patients with normal fasting sugar (n=10), ~0 otherwise. Subtracts 3.19 logits for those 10, which flips 4 false positives to correct negatives while all 5 positives stay positive.
