What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. Single hidden layer: 5 hidden nodes each read out directly, flat root. 148 never clips (affine); 3229 is a constant -0.044 offset for cp:2. 2034 (fixed thal defect AND normal fbs) acts on 10 training patients, looks like an overfitted correction (flips 4 FP to negatives). 6 disconnected inputs (restecg:0/1/2, exang:1, slope:3, thal:3) added to root as zero-effect entries.

Tool notes (record): activation_profile needs node_id. get_coverage lists disconnected inputs as uncovered until annotated. get_formula output shown as ReLU; compute_performance matches sigmoid(z). One transient empty begin_explanation output. compute_shap ~3.7 min.

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate (0.0129). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in fbs_normal_fixed_defect_gate: “An AND gate: it is 3.386 only for patients with a fixed thallium defect (thal:6) AND normal fasting blood sugar (n=10 on train), 0.018 for fixed-defect patients with high sugar (n=5), and 0 for everyone else (93.8%).” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in oldpeak_hinge: “It is the network's only oldpeak pathway, so the network treats small ST depression as uninformative and only marked depression as risk.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 4 split(s), all of input nodes (an input feeding two annotations). These are routine; check only that each input copy sits in the annotation whose hypothesis uses it.
  • Explained with protocol v2 tooling: get_formula then showed the output node as ReLU, while the model applies sigmoid. Hypotheses and evidence that mention a ReLU output, or AUCs of the raw logit, predate the fix (the live closed forms above use sigmoid). Check the root's wording.
  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/heart-s9.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('heart-s9', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

Essentially logistic regression: 17 direct edges (logit SD 4.44; ca +2.16, slope:2 +1.08, sex:1 +0.85). One meaningful nonlinearity: discrete gate 2065 = ReLU(0.795 thal:6 - 0.885 fbs:1 - 0.719), firing only for fixed-defect patients with normal fasting sugar and lowering their logit by ~3.6, cancelling the linear core's over-calling in that group. cp:2 indicator (3497) and floored thalach relay (707->3677) near-inert. Train AUC 0.942 vs 0.934 linear core.

y0=relu⁡(−0.885xfbs:1_b+0.795xthal:6−0.719)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 0.885 x_{fbs:1\_b} \\ &\quad + 0.795 x_{thal:6} \\ &\quad -0.719 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Note: the analytical_formula stored with this annotation's evidence differs from the live text (it was recorded at explanation time, with that day's tooling). Both are shown; the live one is authoritative.

Recorded formula (evidence record)
y0=relu⁡(−0.885 xfbs:1+0.795 xthal:6−0.719)\begin{gathered}y_0 = \operatorname{relu}(-0.885\,x_{fbs:1} + 0.795\,x_{thal:6} - 0.719)\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Fixed-thallium-defect correction gate. 2065 = ReLU(0.795*thal:6 - 0.885*fbs:1 - 0.719) on z-scored one-hots is a discrete indicator: 0 unless thal:6=1 (fixed defect), 2.727 if additionally fasting blood sugar is normal, 0.148 if fbs>120. It enters the logit with weight -1.117 (-3.05) and, via identity_707, adds 2.178*2065 to the thalach gate 707 (a further ~-0.52 through 3677). Its role is to cancel the linear core's over-prediction of disease for thal:6 patients with normal FBS (the linear core gives them +0.60 through the thal:3 edge and other terms). EVIDENCE: TRAIN n=242: 2065 is exactly 0 for all thal:6=0 patients (227/242). thal:6=1 & fbs:1=0 (n=10): 2065=2.727; thal:6=1 & fbs:1=1 (n=5): 2065=0.148. Active 6.2%. Sensitivity (mean |grad|): fbs:1 0.055, thal:6 0.049. Readout: direct -1.117*2065 => logit -3.05 for fixed-defect/normal-FBS patients; via identity_707 -> 707 -> 3677 a further ~-0.52. Mean-ablating 2065 lowers train AUC 0.9424 -> 0.9363 and acc 0.884 -> 0.872. On the 10 thal:6&normal-FBS patients (disease rate 0.5) the linear core alone gives mean logit +3.78 (9/10 predicted diseased; thal:6 patients get +0.60 from the negative thal:3 edge); with the gate the mean logit is +0.25 and all 10 are classified correctly. Thus it is a learned correction for a 10-patient subgroup the linear core over-calls (likely partly fitted to train noise).

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: logit z = -0.210 + LINEAR CORE - 0.582*age_hr_reserve_gate + 0.225*st_slope_chol_gate + 0.377*oldpeak_hinges[1946] + 0.411*oldpeak_hinges[3284]; prediction = sigmoid(z) (the genome output node is shown as ReLU, but for binary classification the evaluator applies a sigmoid, so z is a logistic score). LINEAR CORE (16 direct input->output edges, z-scored inputs): ca +1.68, cp:4 +0.99, sex:0 -0.74, chol +0.61, slope:2 +0.49, slope:1 -0.47, trestbps +0.47, sex:1 +0.45, cp:2 +0.42, fbs:1 -0.31, thal:7 +0.29, exang:1 +0.28, thal:6 -0.28, cp:1 -0.18, thalach -0.10, restecg:1 +0.07. The signs mostly match cardiology: more fluoroscopy-coloured vessels (ca), asymptomatic chest pain (cp:4), male sex, higher cholesterol and resting BP, flat ST slope and exertional angina raise risk, and upsloping ST (slope:1) lowers it. Exceptions are cp:2 +0.42 and fbs:1 -0.31, which run against the usual clinical direction and are left unexplained. Eight inputs are unused (cp:3, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:2, exang:0, slope:3, thal:3, thal:4). Age and oldpeak have no direct edge: they act only through the gates. COMPOSITION: purely additive in the logit. The three children add three nonlinear corrections to the linear core: (1) age_hr_reserve_gate, a protective ReLU that is on when max heart rate is high for the patient's age and there is no reversible thallium defect; (2) st_slope_chol_gate, a flat-ST-slope detector scaled up by oldpeak and down by cholesterol; (3) oldpeak_hinges, a convex two-kink dose-response in ST depression. The children share no hidden nodes. They are coupled only through shared input features (thal:7, thalach, chol and slope:2 also have direct edges, and oldpeak feeds both (2) and (3)). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): full model AUC 0.943, acc 0.884 (sigmoid(z) reproduces the evaluator exactly). Linear core alone gives AUC 0.930, so the nonlinear children add +0.013. Logit SD is 3.28 for the linear core vs 0.91 for all nonlinear readouts. Removing one readout at a time: 1718 -0.0057, 1476 -0.0017, 1946 -0.0007, 3284 -0.0004 AUC; all oldpeak-driven terms together -0.0064. Top SHAP features: ca, cp:4, sex:0, slope:2, slope:1 (all with direct edges). Interpretation: close to logistic regression, plus a protective heart-rate-reserve-for-age gate (blocked by a reversible defect) and two oldpeak/flat-slope ischaemia corrections.

Evidence (4 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Root closed form: additive logit of linear core plus three child readouts.
  • performance_metrics: Full coverage with 5 input splits; the explained network computes the same function.
  • ablation_study: Linear core carries most of the signal; the nonlinear children add +0.013 train AUC, mostly via the heart-rate-reserve gate.
  • shap_importance: Top drivers are direct-edge features; oldpeak (gate-only) ranks 10th and age (gate-only) 0.013.

Hypothesis (DB):

Heart-rate-reserve gate 1718 = ReLU(-0.812 - 1.490*age + 1.024*thalach - 0.762*thal:7 - 0.720*R3195), with relay R3195 = ReLU(0.981 + 1.073*thal:7). Hypothesis: 3195 is an always-on affine relay of thal:7 (thal:7 is one-hot, z-scored to {-0.769, 1.300}, so 3195 in {0.155, 2.376} > 0), which makes the gate's net thal:7 coefficient -1.535 and bias -1.518. The gate fires for patients whose achieved max heart rate is high for their age (thalach up, age down) AND who do NOT have a reversible thallium defect; its readout into the output is -0.582, so it is a protective (risk-lowering) term. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 3195 is active for 100% of patients, so the gate reduces exactly to 1718 = ReLU(-1.518 - 1.490*age + 1.024*thalach - 1.535*thal:7). Active 33% overall: 51% of patients without a reversible defect vs 3% with one. Disease rate 11% when active vs 60% when inactive. Mean |sensitivity|: age 0.49 > thalach 0.34 > thal:7 (two copies) 0.25 each. Removing its readout drops train AUC 0.943 -> 0.938, the largest single nonlinear effect (readout logit SD 0.64). Supported.

  • analytical_formula: Closed form; relay 3195 is affine on the data so the gate is a single ReLU of age, thalach and thal:7.
  • empirical_viz: Gate is a protective 'good heart-rate reserve for age, no reversible defect' detector.

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. Clinically counter-directional signs reported, not explained: cp:2 +0.42, fbs:1 -0.31 in the linear core, negative chol inside the flat-slope gate. Relays 3195 (thal:7) and 3464 (chol) are affine on the data (100%/93% active).

Tool notes (record): get_formula shows output as ReLU (sigmoid(z) reproduces train AUC 0.9434). compute_shap >120s. Input fan-out splits (-26,-15,-9,-20,-18) found by hand.

  • Largest closed-form error: age_hr_reserve_gate (0.011). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in age_hr_reserve_gate: “The gate fires for patients whose achieved max heart rate is high for their age (thalach up, age down) AND who do NOT have a reversible thallium defect;” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?

Summary (from the record)

P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(2.095 + linear backbone + capital-gain penalty + youth hinge + categorical offsets), additive. Backbone a sparse logistic regression (education-num, married-civ-spouse, husband, wife, male, hours, capital-loss; Without-pay switch). Capital-gain chain is a concave piecewise-linear penalty with kinks ~3.9k and 4.9k USD (ablation AUC 0.913 -> 0.891). Age adds up to +2.15 logit only below the mean. Nine small one-hot gates add per-category offsets. Train acc 0.858, AUC 0.913.

Closed forms are computed live with the same code as get_formula(force=True) on the replayed model state; a composition is shown with its children as named functions. Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 39,073 training rows.

Closed form:

y0=−2.29relu⁡(1.14relu⁡(1.47xcapital−gain+1.13)−1.91)−2.37relu⁡(0.221xrelationship:1+1.01relu⁡(1.14relu⁡(1.47xcapital−gain+1.13)−1.91)−0.0918)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= - 2.29 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.14 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.47 x_{capital-gain} + 1.13 \right)} - 1.91 \right)} \\ &\quad - 2.37 \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.221 x_{relationship:1} + 1.01 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.14 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.47 x_{capital-gain} + 1.13 \right)} - 1.91 \right)} - 0.0918 \right)} \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Capital-gain hinge penalty with a relationship:1 (Not-in-family) offset. 3273 = 1.467*cg + 1.129 is always active (a linear rescaling). 6463 = ReLU(1.671*cg - 0.626) switches on above cg = 0.375 SD (about 3.9k USD). 7310 = ReLU(0.222*rel1 + 1.006*6463 - 0.092) is a constant 0.284 for Not-in-family rows and, for other rows, passes 6463 through once 6463 > 0.22 (cg about 0.51 SD, about 4.9k USD). Output cg_out = -2.29*6463 - 2.37*7310 (logit of P(<=50K)): -0.67 for Not-in-family, otherwise 0 below the first kink, then a concave piecewise-linear decline (slope about -3.8 then -7.8 logit per SD of capital gain) reaching -100 at the maximum. Large capital gains force P(<=50K) towards 0. EVIDENCE (train split, 39,073 rows): closed form from get_formula matches the forward pass (check_explanation). Empirical: 5.98% of train rows lie above the first kink; observed P(<=50K) there is 0.196 and the model's mean prediction 0.200 (vs 0.761 overall). Heatmap (train, all rows) confirms cg_out depends on capital-gain and only shifts by the relationship:1 offset. Kinks are almost the same as in adult-s1 (about 3.8k and 4.8k USD). Mean-ablation of the contribution: acc 0.858 -> 0.820, AUC 0.913 -> 0.891.

Hypothesis (DB):

Age hinge: age_out = 1.625*ReLU(0.024 - 0.826*age) + 0.0002*age. Below the mean age (hinge at age = +0.03 SD, about 39 years) each SD younger adds 1.34 logit to P(<=50K), up to +2.15 for the youngest; above the hinge the contribution is flat (about 0). The direct age edge is negligible. EVIDENCE (train split, 39,073 rows): closed form from get_formula matches the forward pass (check_explanation). Empirical (train): mean age_out by age band: <-1 SD 1.77 (obs P(<=50K) 0.989), -1 to -0.5 SD 1.07 (0.863), -0.5 to 0 SD 0.39 (0.726), above the mean 0.00 (0.63-0.69). Line plot correlation -0.84 with age; flat beyond the hinge, so the model does not reproduce the slight rise in P(<=50K) for older people. SHAP rank 4 (mean |SHAP| 0.051, 200 samples). Mean-ablation of the contribution: acc 0.858 -> 0.852, AUC 0.913 -> 0.905.

Hypothesis (DB):

Linear backbone: 49 direct input edges summed at lin_agg (logit of P(<=50K)). Dominant terms per SD: education-num -0.88, marital-status:2 (Married-civ-spouse) -0.69, relationship:0 (Husband) -0.62, relationship:5 (Wife) -0.52, sex (male) -0.34, hours-per-week -0.30, capital-loss -0.26 (linear in capital loss), occupation:8 (Other-service) +0.27, occupation:4 (Exec-managerial) -0.22. workclass:8 (Without-pay, 17 rows, value 47.9) is a saturating switch (+50 logit). Remaining one-hot terms (mostly native countries) are small. EVIDENCE (train split, 39,073 rows): closed form from get_formula matches the forward pass (check_explanation). Empirical: sensitivity viz returns exactly the edge weights (linear). Alone, sigmoid(2.095 + lin_agg) gives train acc 0.833, AUC 0.879. SHAP (model output, 200 samples) top features are all backbone terms: marital-status:2 0.074, education-num 0.074, relationship:0 0.069, sex 0.025, hours-per-week 0.023. Mean-ablation of the contribution: acc 0.858 -> 0.801, AUC 0.913 -> 0.681.

Dead/redundant nodes: 4607 never active; Scotland gate masked by its saturating direct edge; 12550/15301 linear and near-inert. Age effect flat above the mean. Category names and USD kinks inferred.

Summary (from the record)

P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(1.382 + 10 independent additive logit terms). Largest: sparse linear backbone over 47 inputs (removing it: AUC 0.907 -> 0.714). Two real nonlinearities: concave piecewise-linear capital-gain penalty (kinks ~4.4k and 4.7k USD; ablation AUC 0.890) and convex hours term (kinks ~19 h and 50 h). Remaining hidden units are single-category offsets or saturating switches. Train acc 0.851, AUC 0.907.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root composition. P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(1.382 + linear_backbone + capital_gain_hinge + hours_chain_thailand + preschool_protective_gate + bachelors_offset + withoutpay_otherservice_iran - 0.451 unmarried_unit - 0.076 honduras_unit + 0.329 never_married_unit - 0.024 prof_school_unit). Hypothesis (supported): purely additive composition in logit space of one sparse linear backbone and nine independent univariate or small-group terms; no child feeds another, so there are no cross-child interactions. The 46 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries (no edges; SHAP <= 9.4e-4 = noise). Evidence: closed form via get_formula; train acc 0.851, AUC 0.907; whole-model SHAP (train, 200 samples) ranks Husband, Married-civ-spouse, education-num, Not-in-family, capital-gain, hours, age, Wife, sex. Mean-ablation on train: backbone AUC 0.907->0.714, capital gain ->0.890, hours ->0.902, Other-service group ->0.906, Unmarried ->0.906, others negligible. Function preservation vs original phenotype ~7e-16.

Evidence (4 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Root = sigmoid(1.382 + sum of child logit contributions); 0.251 = exp(-1.382).
  • shap_importance: Whole-model KernelSHAP on train, max_samples=200. Top: relationship:0 Husband, Married-civ-spouse, education-num, Not-in-family, capital-gain, hours, age, Wife, sex. Unconnected inputs <=9.4e-4 (sampling noise; they have no edges).
  • performance_metrics: compute_performance on full train split: acc 0.8512, AUC 0.9074.
  • ablation_study: Additivity is exact by construction (identity exits feed the sigmoid output with weight 1 or the unit's output weight). Backbone dominates; capital gain is the most important nonlinear child.

Largest regular effects (logit, 1 vs 0 or per SD): Wife -4.53, Husband -2.56, Not-in-family -2.02, Married-civ-spouse -1.79, education-num -1.09/SD (-0.43 per year), male -1.10, age -0.585/SD (-0.043/yr), Exec-managerial -0.84, Prof-specialty -0.47, Tech-support -0.69, capital-loss -0.31/SD, Farming-fishing +1.14, Handlers-cleaners +0.73, Self-emp-not-inc +0.68, unknown workclass +0.82. Rare categories act as switches because standardized one-hots are large when 1: Never-worked +20.4 (9 rows), Columbia +8.0 (64), Laos +3.2 (17), Philippines -1.6, Yugoslavia -1.5, Vietnam +1.3. Train mean-ablation: acc 0.851->0.799, AUC 0.907->0.714 (the dominant part of the model). Sensitivity (get_viz_summary) equals |w_i|, consistent with linearity. Supported.

Tool notes (record): None (agent-side zsh wrapper issue; stray np.save files moved out of repo). SHAP ~9e-4 on unconnected inputs (noise).

  • Strong claim in hours_chain_thailand: “Thailand (26 rows) adds a direct +1.15 offset and its -1.55 weight shuts unit 11637, which only matters below ~19 h, so the 'interaction' is practically inert.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in preschool_protective_gate: “Hypothesis (supported): Preschool is a saturating override, Protective-serv a plain offset;” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • No splits: every node sits in one annotation as evolved.

A.1 Leaf: age_profile

Annotation idann_121
Entry nodes-1 (age), -80 (native-country:21), -97 (native-country:37)
Exit nodesidentity_age
Internal / exit nodes in its own subgraph2134, 2990, 5070, identity_age
Dimensionality (in → out, incl. descendants)3 → 1
Live closed-form error (3 s.f. display)0.0173
Live numeric-function error8.88e-16

Closed form:

y0=−1.03xage−0.0464xnative−country:21+0.0192xnative−country:37+0.975relu⁡(1.03relu⁡(1.45xage+0.137relu⁡(−0.673xnative−country:21+0.854xnative−country:37−0.705)−0.481)−0.317)−0.124relu⁡(−0.673xnative−country:21+0.854xnative−country:37−0.705)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= - 1.03 x_{age} \\ &\quad - 0.0464 x_{native-country:21} \\ &\quad + 0.0192 x_{native-country:37} \\ &\quad + 0.975 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.03 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.45 x_{age} + 0.137 \operatorname{relu}{\left(- 0.673 x_{native-country:21} + 0.854 x_{native-country:37} - 0.705 \right)} - 0.481 \right)} - 0.317 \right)} \\ &\quad - 0.124 \operatorname{relu}{\left(- 0.673 x_{native-country:21} + 0.854 x_{native-country:37} - 0.705 \right)} \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Piecewise-linear age term in the logit of P(income<=50K), with a Thailand override. Direct age edge gives -1.03 per SD (-0.075/yr). 2990=relu(1.446 age+0.137*2134-0.48) and 5070=relu(1.031*2990-0.32) form a stacked hinge that switches on at age ~46 (z=0.545) and adds +1.45/SD, so the net slope above 46 is +0.42/SD (+0.031/yr): the probability of earning >50K rises with age to a peak at ~46 and then declines. 2134 is a Thailand indicator (native-country:37); for Thai respondents (26 rows) it adds -4.0 directly and pushes 2990 permanently on (removing the hinge). Ireland (native-country:21) only adds a direct -1.57 and keeps 2134 off. EVIDENCE: Train evidence (39,073 rows): mean contribution by age (non-Thai) +1.63 at 17, +0.65 at 30, -0.10 at 40, minimum -0.55 at exactly 46, -0.29 at 55, +0.17 at 70, +0.79 at 90, which confirms a V shape with its vertex at 46. Thailand (26 rows): the -4.0 direct term and the released hinge almost cancel, so being Thai changes the logit by only +0.10 on average. Mean-ablation of the leaf: acc 0.8578->0.8534, AUC 0.9118->0.9051.

Note: the analytical_formula stored with this annotation's evidence differs from the live text (it was recorded at explanation time, with that day's tooling). Both are shown; the live one is authoritative.

Hypothesis (DB):

Additive composition: identity_cg = capital_gain_hinge - 1.842*capital_gain_country_gate. Together a concave piecewise-linear penalty on the logit of P(<=50K): -0.337 per $1000 everywhere, steepening to -0.485 per $1000 above ~$4.8k and -0.644 per $1000 above ~$5.2k, plus a constant -2.44. Ecuador removes the $5.2k kink; 9th grade, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Philippines and Scotland remove the $4.8k kink. Observed P(<=50K) falls from 0.71 to 0.10 across $4.5k-8k, where the kinks sit. Ablating the whole composition: AUC 0.912->0.894, acc ->0.837.

Thailand gate's -4.0 direct effect and age-hinge release nearly cancel (net +0.10 over 26 rows). Rare standardised one-hots act as extreme switches (Married-AF-spouse -59, Never-worked +30 logit). What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: capital_gain_hinge (0.0408), then age_profile (0.0173). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in capital_gain_country_gate: “It is switched off for education=9th, and for Jamaica, Nicaragua, Philippines and Scotland via 2391 (a relu OR-detector of those four countries, native-country 23/27/30/34).” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?

  • 1 consolidation(s): copies merged back after a split. Check that the merged copies carry the same role.

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/adult-s5.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

One-line equivalent (same writer as the UI):

Summary (from the record)

Mostly logistic regression: 16 direct edges (logit SD 3.9) plus two additive nonlinear readouts. Main: an exertional-ischaemia hinge 855 = ReLU(trestbps, oldpeak, exang:1 up; cp:1, slope:1 down) with clipped complement 1501 - flat below threshold, steep above (train AUC 0.947 -> 0.926 without it). Minor serial chain age -> 1669 (no exertional angina) -> 3353 (+cp:4), read out -0.515, tempering cp:4 and making age protective for older patients without exertional angina (AUC -0.002). Linear-only 0.924/0.851 vs full 0.947/0.897.

Hypothesis (DB):

ROOT: HEART-DISEASE LOGIT. p = sigmoid(z) (get_formula prints ReLU at the output, but the model applies a sigmoid for this binary task). z = -0.796 + LINEAR CORE + 1.300*855 + 0.814*1501 - 0.515*3353, an additive composition. (1) LINEAR CORE: 16 direct input edges; largest weights ca +2.09, sex:1 +1.42, cp:4 +1.21, slope:2 +1.06, chol +0.76, thal:7 +0.66, cp:2 +0.58, fbs:0 +0.52, thal:4 +0.42; small negative terms exang:1 -0.33, thalach -0.20, exang:0 -0.15. Logit SD 3.94. (2) exertional_ischaemia_hinge (855/1501): a hinge on an ischaemia score (trestbps, oldpeak, exang:1 up; cp:1, slope:1 down) that is nearly flat below threshold and adds risk steeply above it (logit SD 1.64). (3) age_noangina_cp4_chain (1958->1669->3353): a risk-lowering correction that tempers the cp:4 weight and makes age protective for older patients without exertional angina (logit SD 0.34). Eight inputs (cp:3, fbs:1, restecg:0/1/2, slope:3, thal:3, thal:6) are unconnected. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): AUC 0.947, accuracy 0.897. Mean |SHAP| (probability): ca 0.162, sex:1 0.106, slope:2 0.094, cp:4 0.088, thal:7 0.056, chol 0.043, oldpeak 0.042. Ablation ladder (child readout replaced by train mean): linear core only AUC 0.924 / acc 0.851; without hinge 0.926 / 0.847; without chain 0.945 / 0.888. So the network is mostly logistic regression plus one meaningful nonlinear ischaemia hinge and a minor damping chain.

Evidence (3 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Additive composition: the linear core plus the two child readouts, all summed into the output logit.
  • empirical_viz: Train SHAP (full split): ca, sex:1, slope:2, cp:4 and thal:7 dominate.
  • ablation: Nonlinear parts add +0.023 train AUC over the linear core, almost all from the ischaemia hinge.

Hypothesis (DB):

EXERTIONAL-ISCHAEMIA HINGE. Node 855 = ReLU(1.055*trestbps + 0.896*oldpeak + 0.850*exang:1 - 1.358*cp:1 - 0.937*slope:1 - 0.802) is a sparse ischaemia score: high resting BP, ST depression and exercise-induced angina push it up; typical angina (cp:1) and upsloping ST (slope:1) push it down. Node 1501 = ReLU(0.393 - 1.428*855) is its clipped complement. Read out together (+1.300*855 + 0.814*1501) they form a hinge: contribution = 0.320 + 0.138*855 while 855 < 0.276, and 1.300*855 above. So below threshold these five features have almost no effect (effective slopes ~0.12-0.19), and above it they act with full weight (trestbps +1.37, oldpeak +1.17, exang:1 +1.11, slope:1 -1.22, cp:1 -1.77 per SD). EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 855 active 36% (mean 0.75, max 7.9); 1501 saturated at 0.393 whenever 855=0; mean 855 is 0.23 without vs 1.78 with exercise angina; positive rate 80% when 855 active vs 24% when zero. Sensitivity of 855: cp:1 0.49, trestbps 0.38, slope:1 0.34, oldpeak 0.32, exang:1 0.31. Ablation (local, readout replaced by train mean): AUC 0.947->0.926, accuracy 0.897->0.847, the largest nonlinear effect in the network.

Evidence (3 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form from get_formula(force). The pair is a hinge: 1501 is the clipped complement of 855, so the combined output contribution is nearly flat (+0.32) until the ischaemia score passes 0.276, then rises with slope 1.30.
  • empirical_viz: Train split (n=242, max_samples 100000). 855 is a sparse gate (36% active); when active 80% of cases are positive vs 24% when zero. Exercise-induced angina raises its mean 8x.
  • ablation: Largest nonlinear contribution: removing it costs 0.021 train AUC and 5 points accuracy.

Recorded formula (evidence record)
y3353=relu(0.813xcp:4+1.09relu(1.46xexang:0+1.1relu(1.05xage+0.0607)−0.916)−0.234)\begin{gathered}y_{3353}=relu(0.813 x_{cp:4} + 1.09 relu(1.46 x_{exang:0} + 1.1 relu(1.05 x_{age} + 0.0607) - 0.916) - 0.234)\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

AGE / NO-ANGINA / CP:4 DAMPING CHAIN. Serial ReLU chain: 1958 = ReLU(1.049*age + 0.061) passes age above about the mean; 1669 = ReLU(1.104*1958 + 1.460*exang:0 - 0.916) is active exactly when there is NO exercise-induced angina (100% of exang:0 cases, 0% otherwise) and grows with age; 3353 = ReLU(1.089*1669 + 0.813*cp:4 - 0.234) adds asymptomatic chest pain. It is read out with -0.515, so it LOWERS risk. Effect: (1) for cp:4 patients (always active) it trims the direct +1.213 cp:4 weight to a net +0.79; (2) for older patients without exertional angina it subtracts up to ~0.65 per SD of age, reversing the small direct +0.236 age effect in that subgroup, and adds ~-0.82 per SD on exang:0. Reading: an asymptomatic-chest-pain patient who is older but does NOT get angina on exercise is less likely diseased than cp:4 alone suggests. EVIDENCE (train, n=242): 3353 active 54.5% (100% with cp:4, 18% otherwise); mean readout -0.77 for cp:4 & no exertional angina, -0.35 for cp:4 & angina, -0.09 for no cp:4 & no angina, 0 otherwise. Sensitivity of 3353: exang:0 0.45, cp:4 0.44, age 0.26. Ablation (local, readout replaced by train mean): AUC 0.947->0.945, accuracy 0.897->0.888: a minor correction (logit SD 0.34 vs 3.9 for the linear part).

Evidence (3 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form from get_formula(force): a three-stage serial ReLU chain age -> (age, no exertional angina) -> (+ asymptomatic chest pain).
  • empirical_viz: Train split (n=242). 1669 is active exactly when there is no exercise angina; 3353 is always active for asymptomatic chest pain (cp:4) and otherwise only for older patients without exertional angina.
  • ablation: Small effect: removing it costs 0.002 train AUC and 0.8 points accuracy.

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. Six inputs (age, exang:0, exang:1, oldpeak, slope:1, cp:4) split by hand (not flagged by tools). The age/no-angina/cp:4 chain is real but small (AUC -0.002, logit SD 0.34); its 'damping correction' hypothesis rests on weight signs and subgroup means. First root (structural 0.784) undone and re-annotated with 8 unconnected inputs as entries.

Tool notes (record): get_viz_summary rejects 'line_plot' (valid 'line'). activation_profile needs node_id. get_formula shows output ReLU; compute_performance applies sigmoid. compute_shap >2 min. Tool compositional_coverage always 1.0.

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: exertional_ischaemia_hinge (0.019). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in age_noangina_cp4_chain: “1669 = ReLU(1.104*1958 + 1.460*exang:0 - 0.916) is active exactly when there is NO exercise-induced angina (100% of exang:0 cases, 0% otherwise) and grows with age;” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 6 split(s), all of input nodes (an input feeding two annotations). These are routine; check only that each input copy sits in the annotation whose hypothesis uses it.
  • Explained with protocol v2 tooling: get_formula then showed the output node as ReLU, while the model applies sigmoid. Hypotheses and evidence that mention a ReLU output, or AUCs of the raw logit, predate the fix (the live closed forms above use sigmoid). Check the root's wording.
  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/heart-s8.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Summary (from the record)

Essentially logistic regression: 19 direct edges (logit SD 4.90; ca +2.61, female -1.57) plus three one-sided ReLU corrections: an ischaemia gate on oldpeak and thal:7 (SD 0.78); a Boolean AND of female sex and exercise angina adding +2.07 logit, cancelling most of the female protective term (SD 0.56); a protective gate on high thalach mostly with non-anginal pain (SD 0.49). Linear core train AUC 0.930 vs 0.947 full; mean-ablating each gate gives 0.938, 0.940, 0.945.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root hypothesis: an additive composition that is essentially logistic regression plus three one-sided ReLU corrections. Logit z = -0.680 + LINEAR CORE + 0.746*st_depression_gate + 1.730*female_exang_and_gate - 0.918*thalach_cp3_protective_gate, and the prediction is sigmoid(z) (get_formula renders the output as ReLU, but for this binary task the model applies a sigmoid to the output pre-activation). LINEAR CORE = 19 direct input->output edges, dominated by ca (+2.607, number of vessels), sex:0 (-1.573, women lower risk), chol (+0.870), slope:1 (-0.833, upsloping ST protective), cp:1 (-0.785), slope:2 (+0.743), cp:3 (-0.743), fbs:0 (+0.627), trestbps (+0.519), thal:7 (+0.490), thalach (-0.470), sex:1 (+0.390), thal:4 (+0.383), thal:6 (-0.351), cp:4 (+0.312); age, restecg:0, exang:0/1 near zero. cp:2, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2 are unused. Corrections: (a) ischaemia evidence (ST depression, reversible thal defect) adds risk; (b) women with exercise angina lose most of their sex protection (AND gate, +2.07 logit); (c) high max heart rate, especially with non-anginal pain, removes extra risk. Evidence (train, n=242): accuracy 0.876, AUC 0.947. Linear core logit SD 4.90 vs gates 0.78 / 0.56 / 0.49. Linear core alone AUC 0.930; mean-ablating each gate gives AUC 0.938 / 0.940 / 0.945, so together the nonlinear parts add ~+0.017 train AUC. SHAP (probability scale): ca 0.170 >> sex:0 0.080 > slope:1 0.063 > cp:3 0.058 > slope:2 0.053 > thal:7 0.050 > chol 0.038 > thalach 0.034 > oldpeak 0.029. Function preservation of the refactored model 1.8e-15; all leaf closed forms exact up to 3-s.f. display rounding (max 0.027).

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: hidden gate 557 = ReLU(1.283*oldpeak + 0.559*thal:7 - 1.076*slope:3 - 0.417*fbs:0 + 0.085) is a one-sided ischaemia-evidence detector. It switches on mainly with exercise-induced ST depression (oldpeak), more readily when there is a reversible thal defect (thal:7), is pushed down by a downsloping ST segment (slope:3, which is clinically counter-intuitive; it is rare, 7%, and the direct linear core has no slope:3 term, so this is probably how the network absorbs slope:3 at all), and slightly by normal fasting sugar (fbs:0). It enters the logit with weight +0.746, so it only ever adds risk. Evidence (train, n=242): closed form exact (single ReLU); active on 47.9% of patients (83% with thal:7, 27% without); max 4.72, logit contribution SD 0.78; sensitivity oldpeak 0.62 > slope:3 0.52 > thal:7 0.27 > fbs:0 0.20; replacing it by its mean drops train AUC of the logit from 0.947 to 0.938, the largest of the three gates.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: a protective high-exercise-capacity gate. Serial chain thal:3 -> 3818 -> 2124. 3818 = ReLU(1.003*thal:3 - 0.192) is a normal-thallium indicator taking only the values 0 (abnormal thal) and 0.702 (normal thal, 56% of patients). 2124 = ReLU(1.338*thalach + 0.763*cp:3 - 0.108*3818 - 0.932) fires when maximum heart rate is high, much more readily with non-anginal chest pain (cp:3): active on 80% of cp:3 patients but 10.5% of others (30.6% overall, max 2.88). It enters the logit with weight -0.918, so it only ever lowers risk, adding a hinge to the direct linear thalach (-0.470) and cp:3 (-0.743) terms. The thal:3 branch only moves the threshold by -0.076 (sensitivity 0.025 vs thalach 0.41, cp:3 0.23) and is nearly inert. Evidence (train, n=242): closed form exact; logit contribution SD 0.49; mean-ablation drops train AUC only 0.947 -> 0.945, the weakest of the three gates.

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. 4 hidden nodes form 3 independent one-sided ReLU gates feeding the output. 6 input splits (fbs:0, thal:7, sex:0, exang:1, cp:3, thalach). Weak spots: thal:3->3818 branch nearly inert; in gate 557 slope:3 suppresses risk (clinically counter-intuitive; rare 7%, no direct edge) - reported as what the network computes. Unconnected inputs (cp:2, fbs:1, restecg:1, restecg:2) added to root entries.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: z = -0.054 + linear_core + age_effect + bp_slope_effect + chest_pain_effect + thal_effect, and P(disease) = sigmoid(z). get_formula shows the output as ReLU, but the evaluator applies a sigmoid to the pre-activation for binary classification. The composition is purely additive, so the model is a generalised additive logistic model: one linear backbone over 11 features plus four per-feature-group shape functions (age inverted-U, saturating BP with an upsloping-ST discount, a per-category chest-pain lookup, and an additive thallium term). Unused inputs: sex:0, fbs:1, restecg:1, thal:7 (mostly redundant one-hot complements; thal:7 acts as the reference via thal:3/thal:6). Only two pieces are materially nonlinear: the age hinge (1499) and the BP/slope:1 hinge (3392). The cp:2 and thal:4 gates are exactly affine on the binary data, and the cp:3 x slope:3 gate is near-inert. Replacing all five hidden gates with affine fits moves the logit by SD 0.16 and train AUC 0.9407 -> 0.9384, with identical accuracy (0.876). Closed form (children as functions):

y0=0.179xage_a−0.423age_gate⁡(xage_b)\begin{gathered}y_0 = 0.179 x_{age\_a} - 0.423 \operatorname{age\_gate}{\left(x_{age\_b} \right)}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Age shape function: identity_age = 0.179 age_z - 0.423 age_gate(age_z) = 0.179 age_z - 0.423 relu(1.045 age_z - 0.478). This is an inverted-U in the logit: it rises with age to a peak near 59 years (+0.05), then falls (-0.09 at 65, -0.24 at 70, -0.44 at 77; -0.39 at 35). So the model treats middle-to-late-50s as the riskiest age and gives the oldest patients a lower risk than the direct slope alone would. This is an evolved non-monotone age effect, a small one. What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. cp2 (3683) and thal4 (3731) exactly affine; cp3xslope3 (245) near-inert (<=0.14 logit, AUC change 0.0003). Only the age hinge (1499) and BP/slope:1 hinge (3392) are material nonlinearity; replacing all gates with affine fits: train AUC 0.9407 -> 0.9384. Counterintuitive: fixed-defect thal:6 (-1.58 logit, n=15) and fbs:0 (+0.37).

Tool notes (record): get_viz_summary activation_profile on identity nodes overrides them with relu (clips); computed locally. get_formula for the root drops composition children in both latex and latex_collapsed (root formula written by hand). Annotate validator rejects grandchild entry nodes. Output shown/extracted as relu(z); compute_performance applies sigmoid.

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: linear_core (0.0152), then age_gate (0.0117). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in cp2_indicator: “cp:2 (atypical angina) is binary (z = -0.458 or 2.182), so the gate is exactly 0 when cp:2=0 and 2.075 when cp:2=1: an exact indicator, i.e.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in thal4_passthrough: “It is always active (min pre-activation 0.405 on train), so the ReLU never clips: on the data it is the affine pass-through 0.496 + 0.997 thal:4_z.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?

  • Explained with protocol v2 tooling: get_formula then showed the output node as ReLU, while the model applies sigmoid. Hypotheses and evidence that mention a ReLU output, or AUCs of the raw logit, predate the fix (the live closed forms above use sigmoid). Check the root's wording.

Summary (from the record)

P(income<=50K) = sigmoid(-1.468 + 11 additive logit terms). Sparse linear backbone dominates (ablation AUC 0.911 -> 0.611). Capital gain acts twice: a convex hinge and a gate cancelling a +4.25 (never-married +2.34) offset towards <=50K once gains pass ~0.5 SD. An OR gate (youth outside Other-service, or Other-service) pushes towards <=50K; exactly linear Widowed term; rare-category overrides. Train acc 0.854, AUC 0.911; 44 of 107 inputs unconnected.

SHAP (200 train rows, mean |dP|): Married-civ 0.245, Never-married 0.066, education-num 0.052, age 0.050, Husband 0.045, capital-gain 0.036. Function preservation error 7e-16.

Hypothesis (DB):

Gate leaf (exit idn_gate). Main term 2.413*h1013 with h1013 = relu(1.473 - 0.438*NeverMarried + 0.619*Honduras - 1.17*relu(0.682*cg - 0.35)); plus 0.254*relu(0.176 + 0.845*NeverMarried) (unit 3583), plus Honduras' direct +1.88, plus a negligible chain 0.039*relu(-0.272 + 0.988*relu(-0.267 - 0.426*Cambodia + 0.512*h1013)). Behaviour: a constant offset towards <=50K of +4.25 logit for non-never-married rows and +2.34 for never-married rows (1013 shrinks more than 3583 grows), which a second capital-gain hinge (unit 1594, kink at cg 0.51 SD) removes as capital gain rises; the offset is gone above cg 2.74 SD (0.7% of rows). So capital gain also acts by cancelling a baseline offset, and its effect is larger for non-never-married people. Honduras (14 rows) gets +183 logit (forced to <=50K, fitted to 14 rows). Combined with the linear backbone's marital weights, the net marital effect is: Married-civ-spouse ~3 logit lower than Divorced/Never-married/Separated/Spouse-absent; Widowed in between. What resisted (from the record)

Nothing structural. Single-category overrides fitted to tens of rows (Armed-Forces -80 logit/12 rows, Honduras +183/14, Guatemala +4.6, Nicaragua +3.1); Own-child x Nicaragua interaction rests on a handful of rows. Marital status split across backbone and gate (net effect only readable across both). Cambodia chain and Japan unit effectively zero. Category names inferred.

Tool notes (record): get_viz_summary for a leaf whose exit is a hidden unit reports pre-weight activation, not logit contribution (narratives give both).

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: capgain_marital_gate (0.0915), then capital_gain_hinge (0.0386). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in widowed_offset: “Unit 8342 is always active on the data, so the leaf is exactly linear: -0.40 for non-widowed rows, -2.96 for the 1,188 widowed rows (a -2.56 shift towards >50K relative to other unmarried categories, partly offsetting the +4.25 ga…” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in age_youth_gate: “For Other-service workers the ReLU is dead and they get a flat +1.1 regardless of age: Other-service and youth are substitutes (OR-like), not additive.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?

  • 1 consolidation(s): copies merged back after a split. Check that the merged copies carry the same role.

Summary (from the record)

P(<=50K) = sigmoid(0.776 + sparse linear backbone + additive child terms); backbone does most of the work (ablation AUC 0.908 -> 0.748). Two nonlinear terms matter: a concave piecewise-linear capital-gain penalty (kink ~5.2k USD; ablation AUC 0.890) and a youth hinge (+0.16 logit per year below ~35; ablation AUC 0.900). Five tiny categorical gates. Train acc 0.852, AUC 0.908.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: the network is an additive logistic model. logit P(<=50K) = 0.776 + sparse linear backbone over 40 direct inputs + sum of 7 child contributions, then sigmoid. Backbone (direct edges, standardised inputs): education-num -1.41, marital-status:2 (Married-civ-spouse) -0.73, relationship:5 (Wife) -0.56, relationship:0 (Husband) -0.56, relationship:3 (Own-child) +0.43, sex (Male) -0.42, hours-per-week -0.33, capital-loss -0.30, plus small workclass/occupation/education/country offsets. Children: capital_gain_penalty (concave piecewise-linear, kink ~5.2k USD), youth_hinge (+0.16 logit per year below ~35), and five near-inert categorical gates (Handlers-cleaners/Doctorate relay, Tech-support, Priv-house-serv, China, Asian-Pac offset). The children have no multiplicative interactions; they meet only at the output sum. 54 one-hot inputs are unconnected (zero effect); native-country:15 is constant in train; four hidden nodes (9712, 5394, 12643, 2197) never activate. Evidence: closed form (get_formula); train acc 0.852, AUC 0.908 (n=39073); local mean-ablations: backbone AUC->0.748, capital gain ->0.890, age ->0.900, each gate costs <=0.0003 AUC; KernelSHAP (200 train samples) top mean|SHAP|: education-num 0.105, marital-status:2 0.068, relationship:0 0.054, identity_age 0.046, identity_capgain 0.040, sex 0.026. Supported.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: a youth bonus to P(<=50K). Evidence: closed form from get_formula; line plot on full train (n=39073) shows the hinge, corr -0.78; local ablation AUC 0.9078->0.9002. Supported.

Summary (from the record)

One hidden ReLU (an at-most-one-of-six gate, readout -7.61) plus a falling linear ramp (7-12 logit per first value): output = sigmoid(Ramp - 7.61 Gate - 0.93), peaking at count two. Mirrors the paper's MONK-2 construction with reversed ramp direction.

Agreement with the MONK-2 rule (record): Logit peaks at exactly two first values; ranks every count-2 row above all others (AUC 1.0) but only 86/113 count-2 rows exceed 0.5: computes the rule's ordering, not its threshold.

Recorded formula (evidence record)
y=σ(Ramp−7.61 Gate−0.929)\begin{gathered}y = \sigma(\mathrm{Ramp} - 7.61\,\mathrm{Gate} - 0.929)\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Output = sigmoid(Ramp - 7.61 * Gate - 0.93): an additive composition in logit space. The descending ramp makes counts >= 3 negative; the at-most-one gate overrides the ramp's high values at counts 0-1. The logit therefore peaks at exactly two first-value indicators. Inputs a1:3, a2:2, a3:2, a5:2, a5:4 have no enabled connections and are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, full sample): AUC 1.0 - every count-2 row outranks every other row - but the margin is thin (min positive logit -3.52 vs max negative -3.75), and the threshold is miscalibrated: only 86/113 count-2 rows exceed 0.5 (accuracy 0.922); the misses are pairs involving a3/a6/a5/a1 where the ramp's heavier weights push the logit below zero. No count != 2 row is predicted positive.

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Composition: additive in logit space under the output sigmoid; gate enters with weight -7.61, ramp with weight 1.
  • empirical_viz: Train split, full sample. Logit peaks at count two; all count-2 rows outrank all other rows (AUC 1.0) but with a thin 0.23-logit margin, and 27/113 count-2 rows (mostly pairs involving a3 or a6, whose ramp weights are largest) fall below 0.5, giving accuracy 0.922.

Hypothesis (DB):

A linear ramp that falls with the number of first-value indicators (upper edge of the peak). The ten direct input->output edges give each attribute's first value a contribution 7-12 lower than its other values (a1 -10.2, a2 -8.2 vs a2=2 / -11.9 vs a2=3, a3 -12.1, a4 -7.6/-6.9, a5 -10.0, a6 -12.2). Evidence (train, full sample): ramp + output bias lies in [21.3, 25.7] at count 0, [8.6, 18.2] at count 1, [-3.5, 7.9] at count 2 and below -3.7 for every count >= 3 row, so it crosses zero between two and three indicators. Weights are not uniform: a3 and a6 (binary attributes) carry the largest drops, so count-2 rows involving a3 or a6 sit closest to zero. Alone it ranks poorly (AUC 0.62) because counts 0-1 score highest.

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form. Every attribute's first value contributes 7-12 less than its other values, so the ramp falls linearly with the count of first-value indicators.
  • empirical_viz: Train split, full sample. Ramp+bias is positive on all count 0-1 rows, mostly positive on count-2 rows and negative on every count >= 3 row. Alone it ranks poorly (AUC 0.62) because count 0-1 rows score highest.

Summary (from the record)

sigmoid(-0.935 + 20-input linear logit (SD 3.15) + fbs step (+0.19 if normal) + one nonlinear pathway (SD 2.77)): an ischaemia score ReLU(oldpeak, thal:7, cp:2, restecg:0, -thalach) inhibited by high resting BP at gate 290 and amplified by a 3-node chain into one steep hinge (~+2.1 logit per unit, active on 71/242). Pathway at mean: train AUC 0.953 -> 0.926.

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Nonlinear pathway much stronger (logit SD 0.78 -> 2.77; +0.010 -> +0.027 train AUC); BP became an inhibitor of the ischaemia gate; single amplifier became a 3-node chain (gain ~2.4); thalach and cp:2 joined the ischaemia score; fbs entered as a step and amplifier threshold; age term gone.

Evidence: closed form (function preservation 3e-16); train AUC 0.953, acc 0.893; SHAP top features ca, sex:0, slope:1, oldpeak, cp:4; replacing (c) by its mean gives train AUC 0.926 (a refit plain logistic regression on all 26 inputs gets 0.937 on train), so the nonlinear pathway is a real contributor.

Hypothesis (DB):

Serial gate plus amplifier on ischaemia evidence. (1) Gate: 290 = relu(0.944*ischaemia_score - 1.44*high_bp_gate - 0.897): passes only strong ischaemia evidence (204 > 0.95) not cancelled by high resting BP; active in 71/242 train rows, of which 79% have disease (30% when off). (2) Amplifier: 5615 = 0.248 + 0.998*290 (always active, affine), 2335 = relu(0.893 + 0.898*290 - 1.02*high_bp_gate) (off only for high BP, 27 rows), and 1834 = relu(-1.96 + 0.81*290 + 0.85*2335 + 0.86*5615 + 0.69*fbs:1). With 2335 active and normal fbs, 1834 = relu(2.44*290 - 1.26 - 0.86*high_bp_gate), i.e. threshold 290 > ~0.52; with high fbs the threshold drops below 0 so 1834 is on even when 290 is off (20 rows, at most +0.57 logit). Fitted on train rows with both active: 1834 = 2.40*290 - 1.11. (3) Readout: logit += -0.062*204 + 0.439*290 + 0.747*1834, which on train is about 2.14*290 - 0.81 (resid SD 0.52) when 290 is active and 0.04 +/- 0.17 when off. So the pathway is effectively one steep hinge: risk logit rises ~2 per unit of BP-discounted ischaemia above threshold. Evidence: closed form; train sensitivity (oldpeak dominates, then thal:7, trestbps); local ablations on train: pathway at its mean AUC 0.953 -> 0.926 (log loss 0.283 -> 0.366), no BP inhibition 0.947, no fbs:1 term 0.951, drop 1834 readout 0.939. Pathway logit SD 2.77 vs linear part 3.15.

Evidence (3 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Composition of ischaemia_score and high_bp_gate through the 290 gate and the 2335/5615/1834 amplifier.
  • empirical_viz: Train sensitivity of 1834: oldpeak 1.27, thal:7 0.68, trestbps 0.57, cp:2 0.41, thalach 0.36, restecg:0 0.34, fbs:1 0.24.
  • ablation_study: Replacing the pathway output by its mean drops train AUC 0.953 -> 0.926 and raises log loss 0.283 -> 0.366. When 290 is active (71 rows) the pathway adds about 2.14*290 - 0.81 to the logit (resid SD 0.52); when 290 is off it adds 0.04 +/- 0.17 (only via fbs:1 into 1834).

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(1.57xtrestbps_b−0.663)\begin{gathered}y_0 = \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.57 x_{trestbps\_b} - 0.663 \right)}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

High resting blood pressure detector. 5320 = relu(1.57*trestbps - 0.663): zero for trestbps below +0.42 SD (about 2/3 of patients), linear above it. It is used only as an inhibitor inside bp_gated_ischaemia_amplifier (weights -1.44 into 290, -1.02 into 2335), so high BP subtracts from the ischaemia evidence before that evidence is amplified. Note this runs against the direct linear trestbps weight (+0.63 in linear_logit): BP raises risk linearly but damps the nonlinear ischaemia pathway. Evidence: closed form (exact); train line plot (84/242 rows active, corr 0.80 with trestbps); local ablation: removing the inhibition (5320=0 in the cascade) lowers train AUC 0.953 -> 0.947 and raises log loss 0.283 -> 0.324; in 9 rows it is what switches 290 off.

Evidence (2 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Single ReLU hinge on standardised trestbps; threshold at trestbps = 0.663/1.567 = 0.42 SD.
  • empirical_viz: Train (242 rows): 5320 is active in 84 rows (35%), exactly the rows with trestbps > 0.42 SD; line plot shows a hinge, zero below and slope 1.57 above.

Summary (from the record)

Linear score over 17 inputs (SD 3.46; AUC 0.918 alone) plus 1.43*node1650: gate 665 is a threshold over female, exercise angina, typical angina, flat slope, minus LVH and normal thal (fires on 38/242, 25 positive); a flat-slope ReLU chain amplifies it (+3.1 logit per unit) and adds a +1.42 flat-slope bonus withheld for asymptomatic pain. Removing 1650: train AUC 0.953 -> 0.919.

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Same core (angina gate amplified by flat slope); +4 hidden nodes (LVH step chain into the gate, thal=4 flag, near-inert angina x oldpeak ReLU); gate widened from 8 to 38 firing train rows; train AUC 0.945 -> 0.953.

Summary (from the record)

Mostly logistic regression (15 direct edges, logit SD 3.31 of 3.74; all hidden mean-ablated: AUC 0.951 -> 0.923). Main nonlinearity: normal_ecg_st_gate adds risk only with normal resting ECG and low ca. Second: ca_age_saturation, a ca pathway with a detector subtracting for ca=3 and younger ca=2, making ca's effect non-monotone.

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Kept 1173, 2245, 1801; dropped 664 (ca/slope:2 gate) and 2009 (thalach chain). 1801 gained thalach, a negative ca term and an oldpeak hinge; the ca relay grew into a deeper chain with an age-dependent high-ca detector making the ca effect non-monotone. Train AUC 0.939 -> 0.951.

Annotations (root → compositions → leaves)

Closed forms are computed live with the same code as get_formula(force=True) on the replayed model state; a composition is shown with its children as named functions. Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 242 training rows.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: 3196 = relu(0.629*2245 + 0.663*7562 - 2.102*5446 - 0.217) = relu(0.525 ca + 0.989 - 2.102*5446); 5364 = 0.884*3196 + 0.359 is an always-active relay. Together they add 2.379*3196 + 0.444 to the logit: +1.25 logit per SD of ca until the young-high-ca detector fires, then the excess ca is penalised (net -3.80 per SD). This is a saturating, age-modulated ca term, serial composition relay -> subtraction -> relay. Evidence (train, n=242): mean pathway logit by ca level 0:1.89, 1:3.29, 2:4.50, 3:2.25 (non-monotone); 3196 clipped on only 3 rows; sensitivity of 3196 to 5446 is 2.08 vs 0.62/0.65 for the relays. Combined with the direct ca edge (+1.110) the total ca effect peaks at ca=2. Mean-ablating the pathway: AUC 0.951 -> 0.935. Supported, with the caveat that only 12 train rows have ca=3, so the dip rests on little data.

Summary (from the record)

sigmoid(-0.156 + 12-input linear logit (SD 3.81) + nonlinear block (SD 2.14)). Gate 1213 scores 'female without exercise angina' (read out -1.27); through threshold node 5800 it shuts hub 47 (open for no-angina and low-max-HR angina patients, read out +0.89). Net: -3.5 logit for women without angina or cp:2, +1.4 to +2.3 for cp:2 patients. Train AUC 0.958 (0.905 with the block at its mean).

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Kept the sex x exercise-angina pair (1213, 47); added inhibitor 5800 (bringing in cp:2), feeders into 47 for low max heart rate and thal:4, and a downsloping-ST node into 1213. Block SD 1.04 -> 2.14 logit; its train AUC gain +0.020 -> +0.053.

Summary (from the record)

Logit = -0.586 + 15 direct terms (SD 2.84) + four hidden corrections (total SD 4.61); train AUC 0.960, 0.870 with all hidden mean-ablated. thal acts only through thal_defect_oldpeak; a no-angina gate lowers risk and makes BP matter only with exercise angina; an age hinge reverses the age slope for older patients with normal fasting sugar; a ca relay boosts ca.

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): cp:2 offset unit gone; new normal-thal flag and ca relay feed 2034, which grew from a 10-row correction into an 82-row age hinge; the oldpeak hinge took over thal:3 and cp:1 and became the main thal pathway; the no-angina gate gained a trestbps term cancelling the direct BP edge. Train AUC 0.944 -> 0.960.

Hypothesis (DB):

Additive composition at the logit: a 15-term linear model plus four hidden corrections, then sigmoid. Unlike a plain logistic regression, thal has no direct edge: it acts only through thal_defect_oldpeak (abnormal thal: +3 logit and steep oldpeak slope) and the age hinge. no_angina_bp_gate subtracts risk without exercise angina and makes BP matter only with it. older_normal_fbs_age_hinge flattens/reverses the age effect for older normal-sugar patients with abnormal thal. ca_relay is an affine boost to the ca weight. Hidden units carry substantial signal: mean-ablating all of them drops train AUC from 0.960 to 0.870. cp:2, restecg:0, restecg:2 and thal:7 are unconnected, zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, n=242): Root logit = -0.586 + direct linear terms (SD 2.84) + 1.658*ca_relay (SD 0.48) - 0.678*no_angina_bp_gate (SD 1.21) + 1.749*thal_defect_oldpeak (SD 2.38) - 1.469*older_normal_fbs_age_hinge (SD 1.09); total logit SD 4.61. Train AUC 0.9605, acc 0.897. Mean-ablating all four readout hidden nodes: AUC 0.870. Largest direct weights (per SD): ca 1.33, slope:2 1.08, trestbps 0.84, sex:1 0.71, fbs:1 -0.68, chol 0.62, cp:3 -0.59, age 0.56. Inputs cp:2, restecg:0, restecg:2, thal:7 have no edges (zero effect); thal enters only via hidden units.

A.1 Composition: older_normal_fbs_age_hinge

Annotation idann_37
Entry nodes-1_b (age_b), -10 (fbs:0), -25 (thal:6), 148, 7566
Exit nodes2034
Internal / exit nodes in its own subgraph2034
Childrenca_relay, normal_thal_flag
Dimensionality (in → out, incl. descendants)5 → 1

Closed form (children as functions):

y0=relu⁡(0.944xage_b+1.41xfbs:0+0.793xthal:6+0.906ca_relay⁡(−22b,−24)−0.578normal_thal_flag⁡(−23b)−1.01)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 0.944 x_{age\_b} \\ &\quad + 1.41 x_{fbs:0} \\ &\quad + 0.793 x_{thal:6} \\ &\quad + 0.906 \operatorname{ca\_relay}{\left(-22_{b},-24 \right)} \\ &\quad - 0.578 \operatorname{normal\_thal\_flag}{\left(-23_{b} \right)} \\ &\quad -1.01 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Serial composition of ca_relay and normal_thal_flag into an age hinge for patients with normal fasting blood sugar. 2034 switches on above an age threshold that depends on thal (fixed defect: always; reversible defect: ~+0.3 SD; normal: ~+0.8 SD) and drops with ca; it never fires when fbs>120. Once on it subtracts 1.39 logit per age SD, reversing the direct age slope (+0.56) to -0.82, i.e. among older, normal-sugar, abnormal-thal patients the model predicts slightly less risk with age, matching a negative age-outcome correlation in that train subgroup (r=-0.12, n=82). Modest effect (AUC 0.9605->0.9484 when mean-ablated); plausibly a fit to this subgroup rather than a clinical mechanism. Evidence (train, n=242): 2034 = relu(-1.014 + 0.944 age + 1.407 fbs:0 + 0.793 thal:6 + 0.906*ca_relay - 0.578*normal_thal_flag), read out -1.469. Train: active 82/242; 0/33 with fbs>120. Age-SD thresholds (fbs normal, ca=0): normal thal +0.83, reversible defect +0.31, fixed defect -3.2 (always on); each ca level lowers the threshold ~0.2 SD. Past the hinge, logit slope in age = 0.563 (direct) - 1.469*0.944 = -0.82/SD. Empirically corr(age, y) is -0.12 among the 82 active rows vs +0.23 among inactive rows, consistent with the reversal. Mean contrib among active -1.40 (min -6.92). Mean-ablation AUC 0.9605 -> 0.9484; zeroing it flips 6 predictions (4 previously correct).

y0=relu⁡(−1.01xcp:1_b+1.44xoldpeak−1.25xthal:3_a−0.373)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 1.01 x_{cp:1\_b} \\ &\quad + 1.44 x_{oldpeak} \\ &\quad - 1.25 x_{thal:3\_a} \\ &\quad -0.373 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Thal-defect x oldpeak gate. For patients with an abnormal thallium scan (fixed or reversible defect) and chest pain other than typical angina, it is always on and affine: +2.37 logit offset plus +2.51 logit per oldpeak SD. For normal thal, it is off unless oldpeak exceeds +0.81 SD (11/123 train rows). Typical angina (cp:1) shifts it down by 1.76 logit. It carries the network's main thal effect (mean +3.0 logit abnormal vs +0.16 normal) and makes oldpeak matter far more with a thal defect. Most important hidden unit: mean-ablation train AUC 0.9605->0.9187. Hypothesis (DB):

Protective no-exercise-angina gate (read out -0.678). On for patients without exercise-induced angina (all women, 96% of men), off for men with exercise angina; contributes -1.78 logit on average without angina (larger for women: -2.68) and ~0 with it. While on, its trestbps term cancels the direct trestbps edge, so resting blood pressure only raises predicted risk for patients with exercise angina (net +0.84 logit/SD) and has ~zero net effect otherwise. Evidence: closed form, stratified activation on train, sensitivity, mean-ablation AUC 0.9605->0.9409. Evidence (train, n=242): 791 = relu(0.474 + 1.006 sex:0 - 0.151 sex:1 + 1.276 trestbps + 2.323 exang:0 - 0.559 exang:1), read out -0.678. Train active fractions: female no-exang 64/64 (mean 3.95), male no-exang 92/96 (mean 1.75), female exang 5/19, male exang 0/63. Mean logit contribution: no exercise angina -1.78, exercise angina -0.06. When on, trestbps slope -0.678*1.276 = -0.866 cancels the direct +0.838 edge. Sensitivity (train): exang:0 1.57, trestbps 0.86, sex:0 0.68. Mean-ablation AUC 0.9605 -> 0.9409, 20 flips.

Summary (from the record)

sigmoid(0.228 + 15-input linear logit (SD 3.88) - 1.63 gate + 0.48 oldpeak hinge + 0.14 BP hinge). Gate 2065 opens for men, angina patients, cp:2 men and thal:6/7; fbs:1 shuts it; high BP/HR narrows it. Makes male sex and exercise angina sub-additive (male effect +3.06 without angina vs +1.36 with). Train AUC 0.954; gate at mean 0.920; linear core alone ~0.910.

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Kept gate 2065 and the linear core; grew the gate from a thal:6/fbs:1 correction into a male x angina sub-additivity gate with sex:1, exang:1, slope:3, thal:7 inputs and two feeder subnetworks; added an oldpeak hinge and a BP hinge (4 -> 8 hidden nodes; train AUC 0.942 -> 0.954).

Closed form (children as functions):

y0=relu⁡(0.483xexang:1_b−1.26xfbs:1_b+0.847xsex:1_b−0.473xslope:3+0.51xthal:6+0.136xthal:7+0.625angina_bp_chain⁡(−17cd,−8b,−5b)−0.299bp_hr_ramp⁡(−8a,−15b)−0.618)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 0.483 x_{exang:1\_b} \\ &\quad - 1.26 x_{fbs:1\_b} \\ &\quad + 0.847 x_{sex:1\_b} \\ &\quad - 0.473 x_{slope:3} \\ &\quad + 0.51 x_{thal:6} \\ &\quad + 0.136 x_{thal:7} \\ &\quad + 0.625 \operatorname{angina\_bp\_chain}{\left(-17_{cd},-8_{b},-5_{b} \right)} \\ &\quad - 0.299 \operatorname{bp\_hr\_ramp}{\left(-8_{a},-15_{b} \right)} \\ &\quad -0.618 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Composition (parallel children feeding one ReLU): 2065 = relu(-0.618 + 0.847 sex:1 - 1.26 fbs:1 + 0.483 exang:1 - 0.473 slope:3 + 0.51 thal:6 + 0.136 thal:7 + 0.625 angina_bp_chain - 0.299 bp_hr_ramp), read out -1.63 into the logit. Hypothesis: a sub-additivity correction for the linear score's male and angina terms. It opens for men (60% open vs 7% of women), angina patients (71% vs 28%), cp:2 men (88%), thal:6/thal:7; fasting sugar fbs:1 closes it completely (0 of 33 open); higher resting BP/HR (via both children) narrows it. When open it subtracts 1.63*2065 (mean 2.3 logit among the 42% open). Evidence (train, 242 rows, counterfactual flips through the full model): male-vs-female effect +3.06 logit without angina but +1.36 with angina (linear part alone +3.25); angina effect +1.61 for women but +0.06 for men (linear part +2.23); cp:2 effect -1.48 in men vs -0.27 in women; d logit/d trestbps +0.81 per SD in gate-open patients vs +0.10 in closed. So: male sex and exercise angina are each strong risk signals but do not add up, and among such patients cp:2 chest pain and low BP mark lower risk. Mean-ablating the gate drops train AUC 0.954 -> 0.920 and raises log-loss 0.281 -> 0.379; within the open subgroup AUC 0.949 vs 0.903 without the gate. Hypothesis (DB):

1754 = relu(0.914 relu(trestbps + 0.5 thalach + 1.17) - 0.013): two stacked ReLUs that act as an almost linear ramp in resting BP plus half max heart rate (corr 0.98 with trestbps+0.5 thalach; floor at 0 for 16% of patients with very low BP/HR). Hypothesis (DB):

Serial chain on exercise angina, resting BP and cp:2. 7659 = relu(1.04 exang:1 - 1.31) is a constant flag (0.153 for angina patients, 0 otherwise). 6931 = relu(0.945 exang:1 - 0.629 trestbps + 0.955*7659 + 0.31): for angina patients about 1.78 - 0.63 trestbps (active 99%), for others only when BP is low (32%). 4652 = relu(1.02*6931 + 1.17 cp:2 - 0.30): large for cp:2 (mean 2.51, always active) and for angina with low BP. So the exit encodes 'angina or non-anginal chest pain (cp:2), the more so the lower the resting BP'. Feeds protective_gate with +0.63. Evidence: closed form exact; train sensitivity exang 0.67, cp:2 0.55, trestbps 0.23.

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/heart100-s4.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

One-line equivalent (same writer as the UI):

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('heart100-s4', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

sigmoid(-0.35 + 12-input linear logit (SD 2.31; AUC 0.850 alone) + nonlinear block (SD 3.21)); train AUC 0.959. Largest nonlinear term: a two-kink oldpeak hinge opened by a thallium defect (+3.1 logit average for thal:7, up to +7). Next: a protective heart-rate-reserve gate for young normal-thal patients; an age/cholesterol brake makes age an inverted U; a flat-ST-slope indicator.

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Reserve gate and flat-slope gate kept; added a thal-defect score opening a convex oldpeak hinge, an older-age/cholesterol brake, two dead nodes and tiny thalach ramps. Nonlinear share logit SD 0.91 -> 3.21, now larger than the linear part.

  • Strong claim in age_chol_brake: “…8) - 2.06), read out -0.60, lowers the logit for older patients: active for 1/81 youngest-tertile, 16/72 middle, 67/89 oldest (mean 1.52), more so with high cholesterol (3464 is an affine chol relay, active 213/242), typical angin…” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in thal_defect_score: “3956 = ReLU(-0.88*3138 - 1.25) is provably dead (always 0), so its -0.69 readout never contributes.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 9 split(s), all of input nodes (an input feeding two annotations). These are routine; check only that each input copy sits in the annotation whose hypothesis uses it.
  • 1 consolidation(s): copies merged back after a split. Check that the merged copies carry the same role.
  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/heart100-s2.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

One-line equivalent (same writer as the UI):

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('heart100-s2', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Verification packet H100 08 · heart100-s8

Supplementary, not pre-registered. Heart-100 (additional analysis): reported separately, not counted towards the Ch 7 threshold. Order within this set: 8 of 10.

Open in the UI (with uv run python -m explaneat api running): genome view, then Tools → Review & verify. Back to the README and progress table.

Summary (from the record)

sigmoid(-0.775 + 12-input linear logit (SD 2.43) + 2.09 x ischaemia hinge 855 + protective young/fit block + thal:4 bump). The hinge is the largest term (logit SD 3.40; AUC 0.964 -> 0.894 without it); the block gives -1.56 logit on average to young patients without exercise angina (AUC -> 0.948 without it). Linear part alone: train AUC 0.860.

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Hinge 855 kept, gained fbs:1 and thal:7 inputs, readout up to 2.09; the small age chain (AUC -0.002) became a 7-node protective young/fit block (-0.016 AUC); new thal:4 flag.

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/heart100-s8.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('heart100-s8', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

Logit = -1.258 + 15 direct terms (SD 3.19) + hidden terms (SD 2.84); train AUC 0.959 (0.874 with all hidden mean-ablated). Hub is an ischaemia gate 557 (oldpeak, flat slope, reversible thal defect, high sugar) vetoed by a low-BP/downsloping-ST unit; read out +1.47 and feeding a risk-factor gate counting female sex, diabetes, exercise angina and ischaemia that cancels the protective direct female and diabetes terms when they co-occur.

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Kept gates 557, 1239, 2124 and added 7 hidden nodes: 557 gained slope:2, a restecg:2 relay and a BP/slope:3 veto; 1239 grew from a female-AND-exang gate into a soft risk-factor count; 2124 changed inputs; new cp:3 and exang:0 indicators and a thal chain. Train AUC 0.947 -> 0.959.

Hypothesis (DB):

Serial composition: 557 = ReLU(-0.612 + 1.585 oldpeak + 0.699 slope:2 + 0.543 thal:7 - 0.954 slope:3 - 0.559 fbs:0 + 0.048*8140 - 1.255*slope3_lowbp_veto), with 8140 = 2.242 + 0.996 restecg:2 an always-on affine relay (adds 0.06 or 0.16). It is a one-sided ischaemia score (ST depression, flat slope, reversible thal defect, high fasting sugar) that the low-BP/downsloping veto 2961 switches off. It is the hub of the network: read out +1.470 directly and also feeds the risk-factor gate 1239 and its second hinge 9147. Evidence (train): Train n=242: 557 on in 84/242 rows (35%); y=0.80 when on vs 0.25 off. By thal: on in 12% of normal-thal rows, 66% of reversible-defect rows. Sensitivity: oldpeak 0.55, veto 2961 0.43, slope:3 0.33, slope:2 0.24, fbs:0 0.19, thal:7 0.19, restecg:2 0.02. Without the veto 557 would be on in 98 rows. Directly read out +1.470 (contribution SD 1.75) and also feeds 1239/9147. Mean-ablating 557 (all downstream): AUC 0.9589 -> 0.9236, the largest single drop.

Nothing resisted coverage. Four hidden nodes sit in compositions. thal chain 5405->8833->3860 effectively a bias term. No-angina unit 6805 slightly raises risk (counter-intuitive).   • Largest closed-form error: thalach_protective_gate (0.0146). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.

Summary (from the record)

GAM-like: z = -0.552 + linear core (SD 2.05) + inverted-V age shape + saturating BP effect (hinge moved by upsloping ST) + chest-pain lookup with an atypical-angina gate + exercise-test block with an age x normal-ST interaction. Train AUC 0.9515; all hidden mean-ablated 0.918; all ReLUs replaced by identity 0.833 (the clipping matters).

Compared with the 40-generation network (record): Hidden units doubled (5 -> 10): age hinge and BP/slope:1 hinge kept; cp:2 indicator became a 5-input cp:2 x sex/ca/slope:3/thal:4 gate; 245 now scores a normal ST response, turned into an age x ST interaction; new oldpeak and thalach hinges; thal:4 passthrough gone. Train AUC 0.941 -> 0.952.

Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 242 training rows.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: identity_exercise = 1.274 slope:2 - 0.354 thalach + 0.263 exang:1 + 1.044 oldpeak_hinge + 0.167*h245 + 0.282*h4376 combines the exercise-test findings. Flat ST slope and ST depression raise risk directly; the normal_st_age_module adds a positive term that is large only when the ST response is normal, and grows with age. Net: the oldpeak effect is non-monotone: for non-flat slope the full-model PD over oldpeak_z -0.87/-0.67/-0.03/0.48/1.49/2.5 is -1.62/-1.90/-2.21/-2.32/-1.91/-0.82 (dips, then rises), for flat slope 1.01/0.81/1.14/1.69/2.79/3.89 (rises). With oldpeak=0 the age PD is an inverted U (-3.28 at age_z -1.96 to -1.07 at 0.76, back to -2.26 at 1.69); with oldpeak_z > 0.5 it is flatter (2.60..3.56..2.38). Evidence: logit SD 1.34, range -0.90..5.72; mean-ablating the component drops AUC to 0.9219 (second largest). SHAP: slope:2 0.065, oldpeak 0.037, exang:1 0.028, thalach 0.021.

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing resisted coverage. One leaf holds 4 hidden nodes with two exits. 5402 never clips; 5302 has no effect. Counter-intuitive, plausibly sample-fitted: the age x normal-ST module adds risk for normal ST response growing with age (making oldpeak non-monotone); cp2_vessel_gate makes atypical angina raise risk for women and lower it for men; thal:4 term rests on n=2.

Tool notes (record): activation_profile with only annotation_id fails (computed locally).

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: bp_slope1_saturation (0.0173), then normal_st_age_module (0.0173). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.

Hypothesis (DB):

Customer-service-calls threshold. identity_csc = 1.635*CSC (direct edge); 1255 = relu(0.003 - 2.878*state37 + 0.129*dayMinutes - 0.595*CSC) read out with weight 2.598, cancelling the CSC slope while 1255 is on (0-2 calls) and releasing it from 3-4 calls on. Net: flat logit for 0-2 calls, then ~+1.25 logit per extra call. State 37 rows switch 1255 off.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Customer-service-calls threshold. Logit term = 1.635*CSC + 2.598*relu(0.0033 - 0.595*CSC + 0.129*dayMinutes - 2.878*state37). For CSC 0-2 the relu is on in 95-98% of rows and cancels the slope (net 1.635-2.598*0.595 = +0.09/sd): mean term 0.94, 1.04, 1.11 for 0, 1, 2 calls. From 3 calls the relu shuts off (on in 3% at 3 calls, 0% at 4+): mean term 1.79, 3.04, 4.30, 5.55 for 3-6 calls, about +1.25 logit per call. Train churn by calls: 0-3 ~0.11, 4: 0.44, 5: 0.57, 6: 0.68, so the network places the threshold at 3-4 calls. A linear model cannot do this (linear R2 of the term 0.73). State 37 (84 rows, z=6.83) drives the relu negative, so for those rows CSC is linear throughout: logit effect of being in state 37 runs from -2.0 (0 calls) to +0.97 (3+ calls). Train AUC: mean-ablation 0.898 -> 0.819; replacing the term by its best linear fit 0.898 -> 0.879.

Hypothesis (DB):

High-usage hinge: 3227 = relu(-1.044 + 0.972*dayMinutes + 0.363*eveMinutes + 0.371*relu(0.177+0.382*eveMinutes)), read out with weight 3.019. Zero for typical usage, rising steeply for the heaviest day (and evening) users, the well-known high-bill churn segment.

Evidence (train, n=4000): High-usage hinge 3.019*relu(-1.044 + 0.972*dayMin + 0.363*eveMin + 0.371*relu(0.177+0.382*eveMin)). Zero for the lower 50% of day minutes; active in 13% of the 6th-7th deciles, 48% of the 9th and 93% of the top decile, where its mean logit term is +2.32 and train churn is 0.49 (vs 0.06-0.17 elsewhere). The inner eve-minutes relu makes the eve slope 0.363 (low eve) or 0.505 (high eve): heavy day+eve users (high total bill) churn. Linear R2 of the term only 0.41. Train AUC: mean-ablation -> 0.860; linearised -> 0.873.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Category offsets (exact linear in the one-hots, linear R2 1.0). 5685: state 11 only (73 rows, churn 0.041), logit -2.08. 5853: state 0 (56 rows, churn 0.071), -1.10 hidden (+0.25 direct) = net -0.85. 10761: state 21 (86 rows, churn 0.186), +0.56. 1529 = relu(0.688-0.455*state41-0.521*state44): -0.98 for everyone, switched off for state 41 (66 rows, net +0.98) and state 44 (89 rows; +0.98 cancels the direct -0.91, net +0.08). These are large effects learned from ~60-90 rows each. Train AUC: mean-ablation 0.898 -> 0.895.

  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Summary (from the record)

Logit = linear term + three hinge groups: (1) service-call hinges (>=3-4 calls raise churn, much more for low day usage: +3.8 logit, 95% empirical churn at 4 calls with day z<-1); (2) day-usage hinges + total-charge chain gated by voice-mail plan (no plan with high day and eve: +5.2 logit, 94% churn); (3) linear terms (international plan: direct +2.62, average whole-model effect for holders +2.67; voice-mail plan: direct -1.96, average whole-model effect for holders -2.37; per-state offsets). Rare-state hidden units and relay essentially inert. No international plan x intl minutes interaction learned.

Hypothesis (DB):

HYPOTHESIS: churn logit = -2.00 + linear term (direct edges) + dayUsageHinges + totalChargeChain + serviceCallsHinges + rareStateUnits + an always-on affine relay; output = sigmoid. Additive (parallel) composition at the output, plus a serial path: 553 (serviceCalls), 9871 (charge) and 3854 (states) feed the relay 12977/2377 -> 5868 -> 7162 -> output, which is active on all 4000 training rows and so contributes a constant (about -1.28) plus small linear terms. Linear term: international_plan +0.77/SD (direct term +2.62 logit for plan holders; average whole-model effect for holders +2.67), voice_mail_plan -0.86/SD (direct term -1.96 for holders; average whole-model effect for holders -2.37), vmail messages +0.41, intl minutes +0.45, eve minutes +0.22, night charge +0.22, account_length +0.12, and 17 per-state offsets (largest: state:46 -1.89, state:4 +1.48, state:47 +1.22, state:31 +0.86, state:0 -0.82, state:50 -0.76 logit on their 41-90 rows). 33 inputs are unconnected (zero effect). EVIDENCE (train, local mean-ablation and linearisation): full AUC 0.910; all hidden parts mean-ablated (direct edges only) 0.717; all hidden parts replaced by their best joint linear fit 0.835 (cf. L2 logistic regression train 0.843). So the nonlinear gain over a linear model is ~0.07 AUC, from service-call hinges with the low-usage interaction (0.021 alone) and the day/total-charge hinges with the voice-mail-plan gate (0.025 jointly), plus synergy between them (joint linearisation 0.074). rareStateUnits and the relay contribute ~0.
