Hypothesis (DB):

HYPOTHESIS: two ReLU hinges on daytime usage that raise churn for heavy day users, mainly those without a voice-mail plan. total_day_minutes and total_day_charge are identical after z-scoring (max diff 5e-4), so the leaf uses both interchangeably. 1254 = relu(0.42*day - 0.73): on for day z > 1.74 (164 rows, churn 62% vs 12%), logit +2.08 per unit (up to +1.26). 3460 = relu(0.86*day - 0.83*voice_mail_plan - 0.85): on for day z > 0.39 without a voice-mail plan, z > 2.5 with one (995 rows, churn 28% vs 9.5%), logit +2.25 per unit (up to +5.3). EVIDENCE (train, n=4000): closed form above (max err 0.002); sensitivity: 3460 driven by voice_mail_plan (0.21) and day (0.21 total). Combined usage logit (with totalChargeChain): no voice-mail plan, day z>1 and eve z>1 -> +5.2 logit, empirical churn 94%; same usage with a voice-mail plan -> churn 10%. Replacing this leaf by its best linear fit costs 0.008 train AUC; mean-ablating 3460 costs 0.016.

EVIDENCE: closed form (max err 0.008), sensitivity (4045: eve 0.14, day 0.22; 387: vmail messages 0.81, intl minutes 0.42). Linearising the leaf costs 0.008 AUC; jointly with dayUsageHinges 0.025 (the two overlap: both are day-usage hinges).

Hypothesis (DB):

HYPOTHESIS: customer-service-call hinges, with an interaction against day usage: many calls by low-usage customers = churn. 9203 = relu(0.66*cs - 0.67) is on at >=3 calls (848 rows, churn 25%), logit +1.41 per unit. 5395 = relu(0.71*cs - 0.65*day_charge - 0.75) is on at >=4 calls unless day z > ~0.9, or 3 calls with below-average day usage (810 rows), logit +1.93 per unit (up to +6.0). 553 = relu(0.51*cs + 0.28*international_plan - 0.68*state:41 - 0.66): >=1 call with an international plan or >=4 without (555 rows, churn 46%); reaches the logit only via the always-on relay (+0.14 per unit, max +0.45); state:41 rows switch it off (66 rows, effect <= 0.15 logit). EVIDENCE (train): table of this leaf's logit contribution / empirical churn by calls x day z-bin: 4 calls & day z<-1: +3.8 / 95%; 4 calls & day z>1: +0.8 / 33%; 5 calls & day z<-1: +5.6 / 100%; <=2 calls: ~0 / 5-9% (except the high-usage bin, handled by the usage leaves). number_customer_service_calls has no direct edge to the output, so this leaf is its only route: mean-ablating the leaf costs 0.113 train AUC; replacing it by its best linear fit costs 0.021, the largest nonlinear gain of any part.

EVIDENCE: closed form (max err 0.022, sympy rounding through the deep cascade); sensitivities all <0.04 except 7740/state:44 (0.98 per unit of activation but output weight 0.05). Mean-ablating the whole leaf changes train AUC by -0.0002; its best linear fit has R2 1.000. The large per-state effects in this network are in the root's direct linear edges, not here.

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: rareStateUnits (0.0224). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in serviceCallsHinges: “state:41 rows switch it off (66 rows, effect <= 0.15 logit).” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in rareStateUnits: “HYPOTHESIS (revised): rare-state units that are almost inert.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 8 split(s), all of input nodes (an input feeding two annotations). These are routine; check only that each input copy sits in the annotation whose hypothesis uses it.
  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn100-s1.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.729 + sparse linear backbone + per-state offset table + ReLU hinges on usage and service calls), additive. Backbone: international plan +0.77, voicemail plan -0.74, intl charge +0.32, night minutes +0.24. State units are exactly affine in their one-hots (offsets that only look nonlinear). Real nonlinearities encode the classic churn rules: churn rises steeply with combined day+evening usage (more so without voicemail), and with 4+ customer-service calls, most of all with low day usage (88% churn on train for 4+ calls and <160 day minutes). Train AUC 0.908, acc 0.909.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.729 + linear_backbone + state_offsets + usage_service_nonlinear + minor_hinges), additive in logit; the four children never feed each other. 26 unconnected inputs (24 state one-hots, areaCode:510, totalEveCalls, totalEveCharge, totalIntlMinutes, totalIntlCalls and others) are zero-effect entries. Interpretation: a logistic-regression backbone (international plan +, voicemail plan -, intl charge +, night minutes +), a per-state offset table (exactly linear in the one-hots), and a block of genuine ReLU hinges on day/evening usage and customer-service calls that implements the known churn rules (heavy day usage without voicemail; 4+ service calls, especially with low day usage). Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): AUC 0.908, acc 0.909. Mean-ablation AUC: linear_backbone -> 0.826, usage_service_nonlinear -> 0.709, state_offsets -> 0.902, minor_hinges -> 0.908. Replacing every hidden unit by its least-squares linear fit on its own inputs gives AUC 0.836 (L2 logistic regression on all 71 inputs: 0.843), so essentially all of the gain over a linear model comes from usage_service_nonlinear (Shapley share: heavy usage/service tradeoff 0.029, service calls with low day usage 0.018, day charge without voicemail 0.016, service-call hinge 0.007, day-minutes hinge 0.002). Rare-category effects (net logit, train rows): state:11 -2.14 (73 rows, 3 churners; empirical log-odds offset -1.20), state:4 +2.02 (41 rows; empirical +0.83), state:47 +1.17 (72), state:26 +0.92 (75), state:0 -0.76 (56), state:22 suppresses the low-usage service-call unit (in-state effect -1.97 to +0.98). These are 1.5-2.5x the empirical offsets: candidates for repair. SHAP (300 rows) top: day charge, customer-service calls, international plan, voicemail plan, eve minutes, day minutes (the same column as day charge after z-scoring), intl charge, night minutes, vmail messages, account length.

Hypothesis (DB):

Sparse linear backbone: 34 inputs add weighted terms, summed at identity node lin_agg (read out by the output with weight 1). Output is P(churn). Largest z-scored weights: internationalPlan +0.77, voiceMailPlan -0.74, numberVmailMessages +0.42 (offsets part of the voiceMailPlan term; the two are almost collinear), totalIntlCharge +0.32, totalNightMinutes +0.24, totalDayCalls +0.11, accountLength +0.10. State one-hots are rare (about 80 rows each) so their z-scored value is about 8.5 and small weights become large offsets: state:11 -2.14 logit (73 rows, 3 churners), state:47 +1.17, state:26 +0.92, state:50 -0.64, state:21 +0.64, state:8 +2.35 (cancelled by unit 3831, see state8_offset). totalEveMinutes (+0.01) and totalNightCharge (-0.01) are negligible here. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula (3 s.f. display matches exit activations to 0.00443); viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.826 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 1.094.

Hypothesis (DB):

Additive sum (identity node state_agg, read out with weight 1) of the five state-only hidden leaves. Every unit here has only state one-hot inputs, and the categories are mutually exclusive, so the block is exactly a per-state logit offset table: state:4 +2.02 (41 rows), state:8 -2.31 (cancels the backbone's +2.35), state:0 -1.25, state:22 +0.98, state:42 +0.59, state:46 +0.02, state:29 0, plus a constant. Closed form (children as functions):

y0=1.39day_charge_no_voicemail⁡(−58a,−61c)+0.965day_minutes_hinge_off_in_state37_0⁡(−59b,−1a,−32)+0.0322day_minutes_hinge_off_in_state37_1⁡(−59b,−1a,−32)+1.3heavy_usage_and_service_tradeoff_0⁡(−61ab,−62a,−36a,−71d)+1.22heavy_usage_and_service_tradeoff_1⁡(−61ab,−62a,−36a,−71d)+1.23service_calls_hinge⁡(−71c)+1.54service_calls_low_day_usage⁡(−71ab,−59a,−16a,−60a,−70a)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= 1.39 \operatorname{day\_charge\_no\_voicemail}{\left(-58_{a},-61_{c} \right)} \\ &\quad + 0.965 \operatorname{day\_minutes\_hinge\_off\_in\_state37\_0}{\left(-59_{b},-1_{a},-32 \right)} \\ &\quad + 0.0322 \operatorname{day\_minutes\_hinge\_off\_in\_state37\_1}{\left(-59_{b},-1_{a},-32 \right)} \\ &\quad + 1.3 \operatorname{heavy\_usage\_and\_service\_tradeoff\_0}{\left(-61_{ab},-62_{a},-36_{a},-71_{d} \right)} \\ &\quad + 1.22 \operatorname{heavy\_usage\_and\_service\_tradeoff\_1}{\left(-61_{ab},-62_{a},-36_{a},-71_{d} \right)} \\ &\quad + 1.23 \operatorname{service\_calls\_hinge}{\left(-71_{c} \right)} \\ &\quad + 1.54 \operatorname{service\_calls\_low\_day\_usage}{\left(-71_{ab},-59_{a},-16_{a},-60_{a},-70_{a} \right)} \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Additive sum (identity node nl_agg, weight 1) of the five leaves on the continuous usage and service-call inputs. The leaves never feed each other; they are summed in logit. Together they encode the classic churn rules: churn rises sharply with heavy day+evening usage (heavy_usage, day_charge_no_voicemail, day_minutes_hinge) and with 4+ customer-service calls (service_calls_hinge), especially when day usage is low (service_calls_low_day_usage), while heavy users are not penalised again for calls (10992). This block is where the network beats logistic regression: replacing each leaf by its least-squares linear fit on its own entry inputs lowers train AUC from 0.908 to 0.836 (L2 logistic regression on all 71 inputs: 0.843). Shapley split of that 0.072 AUC: heavy_usage_and_service_tradeoff 0.029, service_calls_low_day_usage 0.018, day_charge_no_voicemail 0.016, service_calls_hinge 0.007, day_minutes_hinge 0.002. Evidence (train, 4,000 rows): closed form from get_formula; viz summary attached; local mean-ablation of this part's logit contribution gives AUC 0.709 (baseline 0.908), logit SD 1.541; replacing it by its best linear fit on its inputs gives AUC 0.836.

Summary (from the record)

Logit = -1.96 + usageResponse + intlPlan offset (+2.88) + always-on voicemail/state-41 affine unit + per-state offsets + small linear terms. All nonlinearity is in usageResponse: a day/evening/night usage hinge (never active for voicemail-plan customers), a convex second hinge for the heaviest users (+3.94 logit in the top day decile), and a service-calls gate (shut for 0-2 calls, +0.81 at 3 calls which the data do not support, +2.1 at 4, +3.6 at 5) that only works while usage is near zero. No intl-plan x intl-usage interaction. Train AUC 0.919.

Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 4,000 training rows.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: logit = -1.959 + usageResponse + 1.671*intlPlanSwitch - 1.406*voicemailState41Offset + stateOffsets + linearBackbone, output sigmoid. Purely additive combination of five children; the only nonlinearity (and all of the AUC gain over a linear model) is inside usageResponse: a usage hinge that is shut for voicemail-plan customers, a customer-service-calls gate that opens at 3+ calls only for light users, and a convex second hinge for the heaviest users. The 35 unconnected inputs (states, areaCode 408/415, day/eve calls, eve/night charge, intl minutes) are zero-effect entries.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train AUC 0.919. Replacing every child by its least-squares linear fit gives 0.834 (a refit L2 LR on all 71 inputs: 0.843). The whole +0.085 gain comes from usageResponse (restoring it alone onto the linearised model: +0.085; the other four children are exactly linear, R2 1.0, gain 0). Inside usageResponse, linearising the direct usage slope, the service-calls gate or the second usage hinge alone costs 0.010, 0.020 and 0.011 AUC. Mean-ablation: usageResponse 0.655, intlPlanSwitch 0.862, stateOffsets 0.912, linearBackbone 0.915, voicemailState41Offset 0.919. Rare-category offsets are linear but oversized: state46 -1.88 logit on 80 rows (warranted -0.81), state39 -1.23 (-0.60), state47 +1.09 (+0.44), state5 -1.09 (-0.43), state45 -0.97 (-0.42), state26 +0.81 (+0.43), state49 -0.69 (-0.15), state0 -0.68 (-0.25), state10 -0.63 (-0.18).

(2) Service-calls gate 4344: closed for 0-2 calls (0% on), opens from 3 calls (68% on, mean term +0.81), 4 calls +2.12, 5 +3.61, 6 +5.32. Train churn by calls 0.115,0.110,0.110,0.106,0.437,0.571,0.679: the threshold is at 4 calls, and at 3 calls the gate already adds +0.8 logit that the data do not support (churn 0.106). Train AUC 0.919; replacing this term by its least-squares linear fit in its 7 raw inputs gives 0.834 (all the gain over linear); mean-ablating it gives 0.655. Sub-parts restored alone onto the fully linearised model: usage hinge 879 slope +0.048, gate +0.038, second hinge +0.053 AUC.

Total-usage score. 1406=relu(0.537*dayCharge-0.882*state41-0.508); 7558=relu(0.511+0.660*eveMinutes+1.204*1406); 879=relu(-0.996+0.548*7558+0.521*dayMinutes+0.213*nightMinutes-1.011*voiceMailPlan). A hinge on a weighted sum of day (charge and minutes, identical after z-scoring), evening and night usage, lowered by having a voicemail plan; zero for ~2/3 of customers (light/average users).

Evidence (train, n=4000): 879 is a single hinge on a usage score. Pre-activation = -0.996 + 0.521*dayMinutes + 0.213*nightMinutes - 1.011*voiceMailPlan + 0.548*relu(0.511 + 0.660*eveMinutes + 1.204*relu(-0.508 + 0.537*dayCharge - 0.882*state41)). dayCharge and dayMinutes are the same column after z-scoring (max diff 5e-4), so day usage enters twice (directly and via 1406); eve and night likewise equal their charge columns. 879 is active in 34% of train rows: 1% of the lowest day-minute decile, 78% of the top decile. Voicemail-plan customers (1,061 rows): 879 is NEVER active (0/1061), so the whole usage risk is switched off for them; it is active in 46% of non-voicemail rows. State 41 (66 rows) forces 1406 off (0/66), removing the day-charge feed for those rows. Linear R2 of 879 on its inputs: 0.53. Sensitivity (train, n=4000): voiceMailPlan 0.34, dayMinutes 0.18, eveMinutes 0.11, state41 0.08, nightMinutes 0.07, dayCharge 0.05.

logit = -2.70 + 42-edge linear backbone (dayCharge +1.92/z, internationalPlan +0.67, voiceMailPlan -0.69, eve +0.74) + two CSC x low-usage units (heavy service callers churn unless day usage is high: 0.87-1.0 churn at day z<-0.5 vs 0.14 at z 0.5-1) + negligible day/night hinges + affine state offsets, additive. Uses both members of the day and eve duplicate pairs interchangeably. Train AUC 0.905 vs 0.843 LR, 0.839 all-linearised.

Hypothesis (DB):

The 24 unconnected inputs (21 states, areaCode415, nightMinutes, intlCharge) have zero effect. EVIDENCE (train): full AUC 0.905; refit L2 LR 0.843; all non-backbone children replaced by their least-squares linear fits 0.839. The gain over linear (+0.066) comes almost entirely from the two CSC x usage units: restoring either alone recovers +0.050 (776) or +0.056 (4496), together 0.905; the usage hinges and state units add nothing. They encode the known churn pattern that heavy service callers (4+ calls) churn unless their day usage is high (churn 0.87-1.0 at low day usage vs 0.14 at day z 0.5-1), together with the convex high-day-usage effect. State effects are one-hot offsets plus a state29 switch that disables 776.

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(−0.138xstate:22_b−0.589xstate:29_b−0.836xtotalDayCharge_b+0.0536xtotalDayMinutes_a+1.56relu⁡(0.603xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_ac−0.325)−0.0858relu⁡(0.993xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_ac−0.196)−0.567)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 0.138 x_{state:22\_b} \\ &\quad - 0.589 x_{state:29\_b} \\ &\quad - 0.836 x_{totalDayCharge\_b} \\ &\quad + 0.0536 x_{totalDayMinutes\_a} \\ &\quad + 1.56 \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.603 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_ac} - 0.325 \right)} \\ &\quad - 0.0858 \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.993 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_ac} - 0.196 \right)} \\ &\quad -0.567 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

HYPOTHESIS: 776 = relu(-0.567 + 1.565*relu(0.603*CSC-0.325) - 0.086*relu(0.993*CSC-0.196) - 0.782*day - 0.138*state22 - 0.589*state29) (day = dayCharge = dayMinutes after z-scoring; -0.836*dayCharge + 0.054*dayMinutes), read out with +1.646 on the logit. It is a customer-service-calls x low-day-usage interaction. The CSC term turns on from 3 calls (6258) and grows linearly; the unit is on when day usage is below a threshold that rises with CSC: day z < -0.6 for 0-2 calls (a weak low-usage hinge), < 0.0 at 3 calls, < 0.8 at 4, < 1.6 at 5+. EVIDENCE (train, n=4000): on for 26% of rows with 0-2 calls but 78-100% with 4+ calls; mean logit contribution 0.2 (0-2 calls) -> 1.07 (4 calls) -> 3.6 (6 calls); among 4+ callers with low day usage (z<-0.5) churn is 0.87-1.0 and the unit adds +2.5 to +4.9. Linear fit R2 0.54; linearising it alone drops train AUC 0.905 -> 0.894; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model gains +0.050 AUC. Sensitivity: dayCharge 0.28, state29 0.20, CSC 0.11. state29 (72 rows) switches the unit off entirely (z=7.4 gives -4.35 pre-activation): for the 28 state-29 rows where it would be on, it removes 0.95 logit on average (1 churner among them). state22 removes up to 0.86. These are rare-category switches. For 0-2 callers with very low day usage (z<-2, 93 rows) the unit and 4496 overshoot the direct day slope, giving a logit 0.7 above the empirical log-odds (mild U-shape artefact).

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing structural. A 7-node always-on chain collapses to one piecewise-linear g(CSC). Minor artefact: for 0-2 callers with very low day usage (93 rows) the CSC/usage units overshoot (logit ~0.7 above empirical). Four state units always on (affine offsets).

Summary (from the record)

logit = -1.07 + sparse linear backbone over 41 inputs (day minutes +2.02, voicemail plan -0.99, international plan +0.75, ...) + a CSC x low-usage gate + a CSC>=4 hinge + voicemail chain and state offsets (exactly linear). The gate is a low-day-minutes hinge whose kink moves up with each service call from 3 onward; with the direct day-minutes edge the logit is V-shaped in day minutes, so frequent callers with low usage churn (empirical 0.88). Service calls enter only through hinges. Train AUC 0.901, acc 0.906.

Closed forms are computed live with the same code as get_formula(force=True) on the replayed model state; a composition is shown with its children as named functions. Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 4,000 training rows.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: logit P(churn) = -1.068 + linear_backbone + 1.59*807 + 1.81*1264 + 1.48*7208 - 0.88*1133 - 1.00*4051 + state offsets (+ negligible 252), purely additive in logit; the sigmoid is the only coupling. 22 inputs are unconnected (incl. totalDayCharge, totalNightCharge, totalEveCalls, totalIntlCalls, areaCode:408, 16 states) and have zero effect. Train AUC 0.901, accuracy 0.906. Performance sources (train): all children replaced by least-squares linear fits gives AUC 0.836; restoring csc_usage_gate alone gives 0.899, csc_hinge_7208 alone 0.851, voicemail_chain and state_offsets alone 0.836 (they are exactly linear on binary inputs). So the extra AUC over linear comes from the CSC x low-usage gate. Rare-category switches: backbone state:11/46/5 offsets of -2.2/-2.1/-1.4 logits on 73-80 rows (empirical -1.2/-0.8/-0.5), state:49 disabling the CSC>=4 hinge for 12 rows, state:33 offset of the wrong sign.

Evidence (4 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form from get_formula(force=true); check_explanation closed-form max abs err <= 0.0077 on train.
  • ablation_study: Least-squares linearisation of each child on its raw entry features (train). Nearly all of the gain over linear (0.836 -> 0.901) comes from csc_usage_gate.
  • sign_analysis: Counterfactual logit change from switching each binary input from on to off for the rows where it is on, against the empirical log-odds (rows with vs without, +0.5 smoothing).
  • shap_importance: KernelSHAP on 300 train rows (output probability scale).

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis: a low-usage hinge whose threshold rises with customer service calls (CSC). 807 = relu(-1.36 dayMin + 0.05 CSC + 0.69*2627 + 0.61*2796 - 1.30), where 2627 = 1.01 + 0.32 relu(0.87 CSC - 0.09) (always positive, affine in a CSC hinge) and 2796 = relu(0.41 - 1.00 eveCharge + 0.37 CSC + 0.15 state:41 + 0.34*12926), with 12926/13061 a two-stage CSC hinge that turns on at 3 calls. 1264 = relu(0.077 - 0.32 intlCharge + 0.39*807) adds 0.39*807 and a convex low-intl-charge hinge. Readout 1.59*807 + 1.81*1264 (252 is near dead, readout -2e-5, and holds a state:2/state:44/state:4 path). Evidence (train, n=4000): sensitivity of 807 is dayMin 0.63, eveCharge 0.22, CSC 0.20. Mean gate logit rises 1.1 -> 7.4 from 0 to 7 calls. With the backbone +2.02 dayMin, the logit is V-shaped in day minutes; for CSC>=4 the low-usage arm dominates (empirical churn 0.88 low-day vs 0.24 high-day, which the network reproduces). The same hinge also lifts low-CSC, very-low-day customers (93 rows, predicted 0.17 vs empirical 0.04): a mild overextension. totalEveCharge equals totalEveMinutes after z-scoring, so the gate effectively uses evening usage. Ablation: linearising this gate drops train AUC 0.901 -> 0.851; restoring it alone on the fully linearised model gives 0.836 -> 0.899. It is the source of nearly all of the network s gain over a linear model.

Evidence (4 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form from get_formula(force=true); check_explanation closed-form max abs err <= 0.0077 on train.
  • empirical_viz: 807 is driven by totalDayMinutes (0.63), totalEveCharge (0.22) and CSC (0.20); 1264 adds totalIntlCharge; 252 is negligible.
  • input_output_sampling: Local forward passes on train. The gate is a hinge in low day usage whose kink moves right with each service call above 2 (13061/12926 turn on at 3 calls). With the backbone +2.02 dayMin the logit is V-shaped in day minutes; the low-usage arm reproduces the empirical CSC>=4 x low-day churn of 0.88.
  • ablation_study: Replacing this gate by its least-squares linear fit drops train AUC 0.901 -> 0.851; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model lifts 0.836 -> 0.899. It carries almost all the network s gain over linear.

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.44 + seven additive parts): sparse linear backbone (29 state offsets, voiceMailPlan -1.04, eve and night usage, day calls), CSC hinge (flat 0-2 calls, then ~+1.3 logit per call), day x eve charge interaction (up to +3.2 logit when both high), extra day-minutes hinge, intl-plan offset (+2.44), single-state units and a dead unit. No international usage input connected. Train AUC 0.892 vs 0.843 LR, 0.838 all-linearised.

Hypothesis (DB):

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.436 + linear_backbone + day_eve_charge_cascade + csc_hinges + intl_plan_switch + day_minutes_hinge + state_units + vmail_dead_unit): the seven children add in the logit. 25 inputs are unconnected (zero effect), including all three international usage columns. Unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries of this root.

Evidence (train, n=4000): full AUC 0.892 vs refit L2 logistic regression 0.843. Replacing every child by its least-squares linear fit in its own inputs gives AUC 0.838, so the nonlinear gain is 0.054 AUC. It comes from three hinges: csc_hinges (restoring it alone onto the linearised model +0.029; linearising it alone -0.018), day_eve_charge_cascade (+0.029 / -0.013) and day_minutes_hinge (+0.018 / -0.005); the gains are sub-additive because the cascade and day-minutes hinge both act on the identical day charge/minutes column. intl_plan_switch and state_units are exact category offsets (linear R2 1) and add nothing beyond linear; vmail_dead_unit is 0 on every row. Mean-ablation per child: csc_hinges -0.089, intl_plan_switch -0.062, linear_backbone -0.024, day_eve_charge_cascade -0.015, day_minutes_hinge -0.005, state_units -0.0001. SHAP (300 rows, probability scale) top: international plan 0.059, customer service calls 0.058, day charge 0.041, day minutes 0.029, voice mail plan 0.027, eve charge 0.025, night minutes 0.014. Rare categories: state:11 (-1.82 logit, 73 rows, empirical offset -1.20), state:39 (-1.68, 82, -0.84), state:46 (-1.54, 80, -0.82), state:5 (-1.01, 78, -0.45) and state:4 (+1.01, 41, +0.83) carry constant offsets on few rows, larger than their empirical log-odds offsets (shrinkage-free one-hot fits). Turning all states off costs 0.0086 train AUC (0.892 -> 0.883). The 5000 and 7530 tail units fire on 3 rows each (8-9 customer service calls).

Evidence (train, n=4000): internationalPlan takes two z-values (-0.324, 3.086): 14510 = 0 for no plan (3620 rows, churn 11.2%) and 1.19 for plan (380 rows, churn 42.4%), so the logit term is 0 vs +2.44. Exactly linear in the binary input (R2 = 1). No intl minutes/calls/charge input is connected anywhere, so the classic intl-plan x intl-calls interaction is absent. Ablation: logit-term sd 0.716, linear R2 1.0; full AUC 0.8918, replaced by its linear fit 0.8918, mean-ablated 0.8302.

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn100-s9.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('churn100-s9', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.32 + sparse linear backbone + additive hinge units), no gating between children. CS-calls threshold (0 for 0-2 calls, +1.03 logit at 4, then +0.92 per call); convex day-minutes x evening-charge usage hinge (up to +4.4 logit in the top day decile, damped by CS calls); low-day-usage x CS-calls unit; heavy-day hinge; intl-plan offset (+2.5). Train AUC 0.899 vs 0.840 all-linearised, 0.843 refit LR.

Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 4,000 training rows.

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(0.722xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_b−0.00623xtotalEveCalls−0.718)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 0.722 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_b} \\ &\quad - 0.00623 x_{totalEveCalls} \\ &\quad -0.718 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Customer-service-calls threshold. 1044 = relu(0.722 csc - 0.006 eveCalls - 0.718), output weight +1.65. csc z-levels: 0..9 calls = -1.20 + 0.766k, so the unit is 0 for 0-2 calls, +0.12 logit at 3 calls, +1.03 at 4, then +0.92 per extra call (eveCalls term negligible). Combined with the direct +0.37 logit/call slope this makes the CS-call effect convex: observed churn rate 0.11 for 0-3 calls, 0.44 at 4, 0.57 at 5, 0.68 at 6. Evidence: closed form max err 0.001; heatmap(train, 4000 rows) shows dependence on csc only. Linearising this unit alone costs 0.0067 train AUC; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model adds +0.022.

Hypothesis (DB):

4939 = relu(0.65 intlPlan + 0.14 relu(0.99 state:6 + 0.387) - 0.699), output weight +1.86; 8417 is always on (affine in state:6). Effectively: +2.50 logit for international-plan customers, 0 otherwise, plus a state:6 bump: +0.22 for state:6 without the plan and +4.34 (i.e. +1.84 extra) for the 7 train rows with state:6 AND intl plan (5/7 churned vs 42% of intl-plan customers overall). Linear fit R^2 0.993, so it is essentially a one-hot offset; linearising or restoring changes AUC by 0.0001. The state:6 x intlPlan term is a rare-category interaction fitted to 7 rows. No intl-plan x intl-minutes interaction is present (intl usage enters only linearly).

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn100-s3.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

One-line equivalent (same writer as the UI):

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('churn100-s3', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.258 + sparse linear backbone (35 inputs; internationalPlan +2.94, ~+0.64 per service call, 24 state offsets) + 6 additive children): a service-calls x low-day-usage gate (+1.9/+3.5/+5 logit at 4/5/6+ calls with <160 day minutes); a high-day-charge hinge only for customers with no voicemail messages (+3.4 logit at 250-300 day minutes); a combined day+evening heavy-usage hinge; small day-charge step with a state:0 offset; zero-calls bump; single-state offset units.

Closed forms are computed live with the same code as get_formula(force=True) on the replayed model state; a composition is shown with its children as named functions. Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 4,000 training rows.

Performance sources (train, local): full AUC 0.910; all nonlinear children replaced by least-squares linear fits 0.834 (jointly 0.833; refit L2 logistic regression 0.843). The 0.077 gain over linear comes from three hinges: day_charge_no_voicemail (restored alone +0.054, Shapley 0.031), service_calls_low_day_usage (+0.038, Shapley 0.022) and heavy_day_eve_usage (+0.038, Shapley 0.021); the two day-usage hinges overlap, so their gains are sub-additive. State one-hots act as fixed per-state offsets (direct weights and single-state units), plus three switches inside the service-call gate (state:43 off, state:0 and state:35 on).

Sparse linear backbone: 35 inputs summed at identity node lin_agg (read out by the output with weight 1). Largest z-scored weights: internationalPlan +0.86 (+2.94 logit for plan holders), numberCustomerServiceCalls +0.84 (about +0.64 logit per call), totalDayMinutes -0.48 (a negative slope that the day-usage hinges override above about 200 minutes), totalNightCharge +0.21, totalIntlMinutes +0.18, voiceMailPlan -0.14, accountLength +0.10. totalEveCharge (+0.15) and totalEveMinutes (-0.12) are the same column after z-scoring, net +0.03. 24 state one-hots enter directly; their z-scored value in-state is about 7-10, so small weights become large per-state offsets: state:11 -2.35 logit (73 rows, 3 churners), state:4 +1.42 (41 rows), state:47 +1.15, state:14 -1.02, state:26 +0.90, state:46 -1.29 (plus -1.14 via unit 10379), state:31 -2.0 (cancelled by unit 2016). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, 4000 rows): closed form is exactly linear (closed-form error 0.006 from rounding); sensitivity summary confirms constant slopes. Its logit contribution has SD 1.42, the largest of any child.

Hypothesis (DB):

Many customer-service calls AND low day usage -> churn. 7689 = relu(0.85*CSC + 0.30); 15054 = relu(1.11*dayCharge + 1.09*state:43 + 1.09); 4397 = relu(0.78*15054 - 0.74*state:0 - 0.81*state:35 - 0.52) is a day-charge ramp; 997 = relu(0.20*CSC + 0.23*7689 - 0.49*4397 - 0.41) fires when service calls are high and day charge low. 9974 = 1.05*997 + 0.066 is always on, so the output sees about 4.81*997: 0 for 0-2 calls, +0.45 logit at 3 calls with under 160 day minutes, +1.9 at 4 calls, +3.5 at 5 and +5 at 6+ (train churn for 4+ calls and under 160 minutes is 80-100%, vs 7-34% above 200 minutes). Rare-state switches inside the gate: state:43 (95 rows) adds +9.4 to 15054 and switches the rule off entirely (up to -2.4 logit on affected rows); state:0 and state:35 subtract about 6-7 from 4397 and switch the day-usage brake off, so in those states service calls alone trigger it (up to +2.0 logit). 5728 = relu(0.99*state:6 + 0.11*997 + 0.64) is always on; 827 = relu(1.06*state:12 + 0.30*eveCharge - 1.60*5728 - 0.75) is on only in state:12 (55 rows) and with readout -0.018 gives about -0.13 logit there; state:6 has no net effect. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train): closed form attached; local table of mean contribution by calls x day-minutes bin attached. Linearising this child (least squares on its 8 entry inputs, R2 0.39) lowers train AUC 0.910 -> 0.899; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model raises AUC 0.834 -> 0.872.

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(−0.25xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_b−0.875xnumberVmailMessages+0.72xtotalDayCharge_a−0.552)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 0.25 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_b} \\ &\quad - 0.875 x_{numberVmailMessages} \\ &\quad + 0.72 x_{totalDayCharge\_a} \\ &\quad -0.552 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

2899 = relu(0.72*dayCharge - 0.88*vmailMessages - 0.25*CSC - 0.55), readout +3.00: high day charge raises churn, but only for customers with no voicemail messages, and a little less for customers who call service (these are covered by the service-call units). For no-voicemail customers the mean contribution is +0.44 logit at 180-200 day minutes, +1.95 at 220-250, +3.41 at 250-300 and +5.44 above 300 (train churn 21%, 55%, 95%); for voicemail users it is about 0 below 300 minutes. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train): closed form and local table attached. Largest single nonlinear source: linearised (R2 0.58) AUC 0.910 -> 0.897; mean-ablated -> 0.848; restored alone onto the linearised model 0.834 -> 0.888. Largely redundant with heavy_day_eve_usage (both are high-day-usage hinges).

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(−0.667xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_cd−0.639)y1=relu⁡(0.285xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_cd+0.828)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 0.667 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_cd} \\ &\quad -0.639 \bigr) \end{aligned} \\ \begin{aligned} y_1 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 0.285 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_cd} \\ &\quad + 0.828 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Two single-input units on customer-service calls. 3237 = relu(-0.67*CSC - 0.64) is on only for customers with 0 calls (readout +1.09, value 0.21: +0.23 logit); 4279 = relu(0.28*CSC + 0.83) is always on, so with readout -0.25 it is linear, -0.054 logit per call. Together they bend the backbone's +0.64-per-call CSC slope slightly: 0 calls get +0.23 logit relative to a straight line. Any function of a discrete input with few values is a lookup table; this one is nearly linear. Evidence (train): closed form and table attached. Linear fit R2 0.80; linearising changes AUC by -0.0003; restoring alone adds 0.002. Nearly negligible.

Evidence (4 records, DB):

  • analytical_formula: Closed form of the exits (3 s.f.). Exits are read out by the output with the weights given in the hypothesis.

  • ablation_study: Local in-memory forward passes on train: this child's logit contribution replaced by its least-squares linear fit on its entry inputs (linearised), or by its train mean (mean-ablated); and restored alone onto the model with all nonlinear children linearised.
  • empirical_table: Local table on the full training split (raw feature units): mean logit contribution of this annotation's exits (times their output readouts), observed churn rate and row count per cell.

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(1.69−1.61xstate:31_a)y1=relu⁡(−1.53xstate:0_c−0.35xstate:22+0.919xstate:46_a−0.943)y2=relu⁡(0.978xstate:50_a−0.0781)y3=relu⁡(0.999xstate:15−1.14)y4=relu⁡(0.997xstate:40+0.841)\begin{gathered}y_0 = \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.69 - 1.61 x_{state:31\_a} \right)} \\ \begin{aligned} y_1 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 1.53 x_{state:0\_c} \\ &\quad - 0.35 x_{state:22} \\ &\quad + 0.919 x_{state:46\_a} \\ &\quad -0.943 \bigr) \end{aligned} \\ y_2 = \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.978 x_{state:50\_a} - 0.0781 \right)} \\ y_3 = \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.999 x_{state:15} - 1.14 \right)} \\ y_4 = \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.997 x_{state:40} + 0.841 \right)}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Hidden units fed only by state one-hots. The categories are mutually exclusive, so the block is exactly a per-state logit offset table. 2016 = relu(1.69 - 1.61*state:31) is on outside state 31 and off inside it; with readout -1.31 it gives state:31 +2.47 logit, which cancels most of the backbone's direct state:31 term (-2.0): net +0.76 (90 rows). 10379 = relu(0.92*state:46 - 1.53*state:0 - 0.35*state:22 - 0.94) is on only in state:46: -1.14 logit there (net with backbone -2.43, 80 rows, 5 churners). 11068 (state:50, -0.39), 15556 (state:15, +0.27) and 16346 (state:40, +0.38) are single-state offsets. state:0 and state:22 only push 10379 further below zero (no effect). Evidence (train): closed form attached; linear least-squares fit on the one-hots is exact (R2 1.0), so it is functionally linear. Mean-ablating it lowers train AUC 0.910 -> 0.903: a 0.007 train-AUC gain from per-state offsets on 55-90 rows each, likely overfit (the warranted offsets from observed churn rates are about half the fitted ones).

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn100-s6.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-2.455 + linear backbone + two service-calls x low-day-charge gates + high-day-minutes hinge + small account-length hinge + single-state offsets), additive. Service calls enter only through the gates: about +1 to +1.4 logit per call when day charge is below its median, nothing in the top quartile. Day-minutes hinge +1.46 logit above p90. Reproduces the empirical pattern (4+ calls, low day charge: 0.90-1.00 churn; high day charge: 0.19-0.20).

Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 4,000 training rows.

Summary (from the record)

Logit = -2.60 + linear term + two real nonlinear parts: (1) a two-stage usage hinge on 1.15 day + 0.65 eve + 0.37 night, gated off by a voice-mail plan (no plan, high usage: +5.8 to +12.6 logit vs 93-100% churn; with plan <= +0.7 vs 5-9%); (2) service-call hinges firing at >=4 calls, earlier/stronger for low day usage (+3.95 logit, 95% churn). Linear: internationalPlan +2.70, voiceMailPlan -1.57, 27 state offsets.

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): 27 -> 23 hidden nodes; train AUC 0.910 -> 0.930 with similar linearised AUC; usage hinge sharpened (day+eve+night with voice-mail gate; linearise drop 0.046 vs 0.025); service-call gain unchanged; new rare-state units (state:11 switch, state:25 gate on the usage hinge).

Hypothesis (DB):

HYPOTHESIS: a two-stage hinge on total usage (day+evening+night) that raises churn steeply for heavy users WITHOUT a voice-mail plan, with a state:25 switch that disables the second stage. 3460 = relu(0.615*dayMin + 0.535*dayCharge + 0.653*eveCharge + 0.365*nightMin - 0.99*voiceMailPlan - 1.83) (dayMin==dayCharge after z-scoring, so the day weight is effectively 1.15); output +3.12. 4045 = relu(0.81*dayCharge + 1.45*3460 - 1.62*6037 - 0.905), output +2.55. 6037 = relu(0.47 + 1.13*state:25) is always on; it is a constant except on state:25 rows, where it subtracts ~13 from 4045's pre-activation. EVIDENCE (train, n=4000): closed form (max err 0.009). 3460 on 522 rows (churn 49% vs 9%), 4045 on 381 rows (64% vs 9%). Leaf logit contribution by usage score (1.15*day+0.65*eve+0.37*night) without a voice-mail plan: [1.5,2) +2.3 / churn 28%; [2,2.5) +5.8 / 93%; >=2.5 +12.6 / 100%; with a plan the same scores give <=+0.7 and churn 5-9%. state:25 gate: only 3 training rows (all churners) are heavy enough to be affected, logit -5.8 (pred 0.98 -> 0.82): a rare-state switch that is wrong on train. Linearising this leaf costs 0.046 train AUC; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model gains 0.078: the largest single source of nonlinear performance.

Hypothesis (DB):

HYPOTHESIS: a dead state/voice-mail cascade plus an always-on relay, together affine in numberVmailMessages. 1887 = relu(-0.97 - 0.51*vmailMessages - 0.11*948 - 0.10*11368 - 0.09*14533) is never on: 11368 >= 1.05 and 14533 >= 1.79 by construction and vmail z >= -0.59, so the pre-activation is negative on the whole input domain, and 948 -> 11368 -> 14533 (states 23, 35, 50, area code 415, voice-mail plan) has no effect. 2377 is the constant 1.565; 5868 = relu(0.846 - 0.068*vmailMessages + 1.01*2377) -> 7162 -> 8428 -> 21969 are always on, so the leaf passes a small negative-sloped vmailMessages term to the logit (7162 x -0.23, 21969 x +0.02; total range ~0.06 logit). EVIDENCE: closed form (max err 0.011); 1887 active on 0/4000 rows; sensitivities nonzero only for numberVmailMessages (0.065, 0.049); linear fit R2 1.000; mean-ablation and linearise drops 0.000.

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing structural. Four of six leaves affine on the domain (near-inert annotations), one holding a provably dead cascade. Service-call hinge overshoots at 3 calls with low day usage (+2.15 logit, 6% churn on 68 rows).

Tool notes (record): `timeout` missing on macOS made the first rename_inputs call a silent no-op (re-run). get_input_distribution has no sample_fraction arg. compute_shap reports names with spaces.

  • Largest closed-form error: vmailRelayDeadCascade (0.0106). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in dayEveUsageHinges: “state:25 gate: only 3 training rows (all churners) are heavy enough to be affected, logit -5.8 (pred 0.98 -> 0.82): a rare-state switch that is wrong on train.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in rareStateSwitches: “on the 73 state:11 rows it moves the logit by -2.33 (3 churners, 4.1%), more than the raw log-odds offset -1.36 and close to the calibrating offset -2.54 given the other features: a fitted rare-category switch.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 10 split(s), all of input nodes (an input feeding two annotations). These are routine; check only that each input copy sits in the annotation whose hypothesis uses it.

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn200-s1.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

One-line equivalent (same writer as the UI):

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('churn200-s1', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

logit = -1.19 + exact linear backbone over 41 inputs (day minutes +2.34, voicemail -1.53, eve +0.87/+0.62, intl plan +0.75, intl charge +0.75) + a CSC x low-usage gate + a CSC>=4 hinge + small hinges + state/area offsets, additive. The gate's day slope cancels the backbone's, so the logit is V-shaped in day minutes, its low-usage arm rising with service calls (matches 0.86-1.00 churn at CSC>=4 with low day minutes). Train AUC 0.908.

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): Same core gate and CSC hinge carry nearly all the nonlinear gain (train AUC 0.901 -> 0.908); steeper linear usage slopes; new small hinges, more single-state units, and a new state:20 switch inside the gate.

Input names x carry their split suffixes. Live errors are max |closed form or numeric function − the subgraph's exit activations| over all 4,000 training rows.

Hypothesis (DB):

Low-usage x customer-service-calls gate. Node 807 = relu(-1.2 - 1.39 dayMin + 0.87*h2627 + 0.72*h2796 ...) is a hinge that is ON for low day minutes; its knot moves up with service calls (CSC enters via 13061->12926->2796 and 9555->2627) and with low eve charge / low night minutes (2796, 12926) and voicemail plan (9555). 1264 = relu(0.12 - 0.31 intlCharge + 0.43*807) amplifies 807, more for low international charge. Readout 1.68*807 + 1.92*1264 (+0.38*12809, which is dead: 12809 = relu(-0.78 - 0.54*h2796) is 0 on every row since h2796 >= 0). Its mean slope in day minutes (-2.31/z) cancels the backbone's +2.75/z, so the network's logit is V-shaped in day minutes, with the low-usage arm raised by about +1.8, +4.5, +6 logits at CSC = 4, 5, 6 relative to CSC <= 3. Evidence (train): gate logit by CSC x dayMin bins rises with CSC (CSC0 lowest-usage bin 8.64, CSC4 12.85, CSC6 13.22) and falls with dayMin; full-model partial dependence over dayMin is V-shaped with the low arm lifted by CSC (min logit -3.85 at CSC0, -1.50 at CSC4, +1.31 at CSC6). Empirical churn for CSC>=4 is 1.00/0.96/0.86 in the three lowest dayMin bins vs ~0.05 for CSC<4, matching. Performance: linearising this child alone drops AUC 0.908 -> 0.839; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model gives 0.905 of the 0.908. It also contains a rare-category switch: state:20 (82 rows) zeroes node 2796, removing the CSC/eve-charge path (logit effects -5.1 to +1.1 per row).

What resisted (from the record)

Nothing structural. Dead unit 12809; state:9 detector 25119 has no possible effect; intl_calls chain near-constant. The gate's knot is a 4-level ReLU composition, described empirically rather than as one closed-form threshold.

Tool notes (record): partial_dependence on a 2-input hinge plots against the first entry (uninformative). compute_performance without max_samples subsamples 1000 rows.

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: category_offsets (0.0272), then eve_state_hinge (0.0181). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in csc_usage_gate: “It also contains a rare-category switch: state:20 (82 rows) zeroes node 2796, removing the CSC/eve-charge path (logit effects -5.1 to +1.1 per row).” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in csc_hinge: “churn rate 0.11 for <=3 calls vs 0.44/0.57/0.68 for 4/5/6.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 15 split(s), all of input nodes (an input feeding two annotations). These are routine; check only that each input copy sits in the annotation whose hypothesis uses it.
  • 3 consolidation(s): copies merged back after a split. Check that the merged copies carry the same role.
  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn200-s2.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('churn200-s2', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-2.449 + linear backbone over 28 inputs + CSC threshold (+1.24 logit per call from 4) + high day/eve usage hinge (+2.47 in the top day decile, damped by voicemail plan) + low-day-usage hinge (+2.1 in the bottom decile: U-shaped day response) + small day-charge hinges + state offsets + affine accountLength), additive. Train AUC 0.911 vs 0.843 LR, 0.833 all-linearised.

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): Same skeleton; state-only hidden units became direct edges or always-on units; a new low-day x low-intl hinge; usage hinge weight 3.02 -> 4.25 and CSC threshold sharpened to 3-4 calls. Train AUC 0.898 -> 0.911, nonlinear gain 0.061 -> 0.079. The state:37 wrong-sign switch got worse.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: P(churn)=sigmoid(-2.449 + sum of the six children's readouts). Purely additive in the logit: linear backbone + CSC threshold + day/eve usage hinge + day-charge hinges + low-day x low-intl interaction + affine offsets. 31 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Additive composition in the logit: P(churn)=sigmoid(-2.449 + linear_backbone + csc_threshold + 4.251*dayEveHinge + (1.582*216 - 0.057*4311 - 1.169*6468) + 0.978*lowDayHinge + (0.263*3930 - 0.164*20832 + 0.23*2698)). No child gates another; 31 unconnected inputs (26 states, area codes 408 and 415, day/eve/night call counts) have zero effect. Train AUC 0.9113 vs refit L2 logistic regression 0.8433 and the all-children-linearised network 0.8327. Restoring one child's nonlinearity onto the all-linear model: linear_backbone +0.0, csc_threshold +0.0393, day_eve_hinge +0.0604, day_charge_cluster +0.0069, intl_lowday_interaction +0.0169, affine_offsets +0.0. Linearising only the three day-usage children jointly gives 0.872. The gain over linear (~0.079) comes from the high day/eve usage hinge and the 3-4 call CSC threshold; state one-hots all off costs 0.004 train AUC.

Customer-service-calls threshold: direct CSC slope plus relu 1255 that cancels it for few calls and releases it from about 3-4 calls; state 37 switches the relu off.

While 1255 is on the CSC slope nearly cancels (1.619 - 2.792*0.55 = +0.08/sd). Train, mean term by calls 0..6: 0.94, 1.06, 1.19, 1.89, 3.02, 4.25, 5.49; 1255 on in 98/96/72/25/3/0% of rows. Train churn: 0-3 calls 0.11, 4 calls 0.44, 5 0.57, 6 0.68. Threshold sits between 3 and 4 calls (sharper than at generation 100); +0.29*dayMinutes delays the release for heavy day users. State 37 (84 rows, z 6.8) forces 1255 off, so for those rows CSC is linear throughout: logit -1.56 on their 62 rows with 0-2 calls (model predicts 0.048 vs observed 0.113; without the switch 0.112), ~0 at 4+ calls. Linear R2 0.78. Train AUC: linearised 0.911 -> 0.895, mean-ablated -> 0.840; restoring it alone onto the all-linear model +0.039.

Evidence (train, n=4000): 26442 = relu(0.497 - 0.883*dayCharge + 0.979*595), 595 = relu(-0.556 - 0.817*intlCharge - 0.653*relu(0.342 + 0.991*intlCharge)), w 0.978. 595 is a low-intl-charge hinge: on for 100% of the lowest intl quintile (mean 0.60), 23% of the 2nd, 0 above. 26442 is a LOW-day-usage hinge: mean logit term by day decile 2.14, 1.48, 1.19, 0.91, 0.70, 0.48, 0.28, 0.12, 0.04, 0.02, with low intl charge adding ~+0.3 in the low/mid day tertiles. Train AUC: mean-ablated 0.911 -> 0.899; but its best linear fit (a straight negative day slope) gives 0.913, slightly ABOVE the full model, so its kink adds nothing to train ranking given the other hinges; restored alone onto the all-linear model it adds +0.017 (it supplies a day slope the linear backbone lacks).

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn200-s4.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('churn200-s4', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-2.01 + usageResponse + 3.0 intlPlan + near-linear usage hinges + state offsets + affine accountLength + 29-edge linear backbone). All gain over linear from usageResponse: a usage hinge shut for voicemail-plan customers, a convex second hinge (+6.6 logit in the top day decile for no-voicemail customers, churn 0.61), and a CSC gate (0/0/0/+1.2/+2.9/+4.7/+6.4 logit at 0..6 calls) open only while the usage hinge is off. No intl-usage interaction. Train AUC 0.926.

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): Same usage core (same node ids), sharpened; 19 new hidden units, mostly state-only or single-input offsets (two dead), adding no ranking ability. Train AUC 0.919 -> 0.926; usage nonlinear gain 0.085 -> 0.094.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-2.009 + usageResponse + intlPlanSwitch + usageHinges + stateUnits + areaCodeUnits + accountLengthUnits + linearBackbone). Purely additive in the logit: the seven children share no hidden nodes and interact only through the output sigmoid. All nonlinearity that matters is inside usageResponse (voicemail-gated usage hinge, convex top-usage hinge, and a service-calls gate that opens from 3-4 calls only below the usage hinge). The intl plan is a flat +3.0 offset; the other children are near-affine corrections and per-state offsets. 27 unconnected inputs (22 states, areaCode415, totalDayCalls, totalNightCalls, totalNightCharge) are zero-effect entries.

Evidence: Train n=4000: AUC 0.926 (refit L2 logistic regression 0.843). Every top-level child replaced by its least-squares linear fit jointly: 0.831. Restoring each child's nonlinearity alone onto that: usageResponse +0.094, intlPlanSwitch +0.0002, usageHinges -0.0008, accountLengthUnits -0.0003, others 0. Only usageResponse is far from linear (R2 0.37); the rest have linear R2 >= 0.95. All state one-hots set to 0: AUC 0.918. KernelSHAP on the root (train, max_samples 300, probability scale), mean |SHAP|: 4344 0.064, 6711 0.061, 10552 0.060, 879 0.057, identity_lin 0.029, 2297 0.016, 24997 0.014, all others < 0.005; unconnected inputs ~2.5e-4 (KernelSHAP noise; their true effect is exactly 0).

Hypothesis (DB):

Nonlinear usage core and the only source of the network's gain over a linear model. 879 = relu(-1.085 + 0.621 dayMin + 0.254 nightMin - 0.968 voiceMailPlan + 0.547*7558 - 0.075 state18 - 0.12 relu(state18 - 0.36)), with 7558 = relu(0.519 + 0.781 eveMin + 1.254*1406) and 1406 = relu(-0.531 + 0.592 dayCharge - 0.856 state41), a second day hinge above dayCharge z ~ 0.9 (dayCharge = dayMinutes after z-scoring). Readouts: +2.305*879, a service-calls gate +3.524*relu(-0.378 + 0.646 CSC - 3.643*879) that only opens when 879 is ~0, and a convex second hinge +3.622*relu(-0.895 + 1.415 relu(-0.399 + 1.258*879)) for the heaviest users. So: P(churn) rises steeply with total (mostly day) usage for customers WITHOUT a voicemail plan, and, for customers below the usage hinge, with customer-service calls from 3-4 calls up.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train n=4000. 879 is active for 41.4% of no-voicemail rows and 0.6% of voicemail-plan rows. Mean usageResponse logit by day-minutes decile (no voicemail plan): 0.43, 0.62, 0.48, 0.59, 0.48, 0.72, 0.84, 1.10, 1.89, 6.61; voicemail plan: 0.27-0.71 flat. Observed churn by decile: no-vm 0.11, 0.19, 0.08, 0.12, 0.08, 0.07, 0.06, 0.09, 0.22, 0.61; vm 0.04-0.11 flat -- the vm x heavy-day-usage interaction is in the data. In the top decile 10552 is on (mean 0.995) and supplies most of the +6.6. CSC gate: with 879 off, the gate adds 0, 0, 0, +1.16, +2.91, +4.65, +6.39 logit at 0..6 calls; observed churn 0.058, 0.047, 0.052, 0.047, 0.536, 0.632, 0.773, so the threshold is between 3 and 4 calls and the +1.16 at 3 calls is not supported by the data (churn 0.047 at 3 calls). With 879 on, the gate is mostly shut. Sensitivity (get_viz_summary, train): 879 most sensitive to voiceMailPlan 0.29, dayMinutes 0.19, eveMinutes 0.12; 4344 to CSC 0.10. Local AUC (train): full 0.926; this child replaced by its least-squares linear fit 0.831; mean-ablated 0.594; restored alone onto the all-linear model +0.094 (the whole nonlinear gain 0.095). Linear R2 0.37. Parts restored alone: direct 879 +0.053, CSC gate +0.040, second hinge +0.071 (overlapping). state18 and state41 enter here: state41 shuts the 1406 day hinge (on 2 saturated heavy users, logit -3.1/-5.5 but p 0.998-1.0, negligible); state18 lowers 879 and gives two non-churning customers p 0.43->0.11 and 0.56->0.016.

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.489 + seven additive parts): exact linear backbone with state offsets; a day x eve bill cascade (up to +2.5 logit when both high, switched off by 3+ calls); a CSC hinge; a CSC x low-day-charge unit (~+3 logit at 4 calls); a near-dead tail; a heavy-day-charge hinge only without voicemail (up to +2.8); international-plan offset +2.82. Train AUC 0.914.

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): Train AUC 0.892 -> 0.914 with all-linear flat (0.838 -> 0.839): extra 0.021 is nonlinear. A dead unit became a day x no-voicemail hinge; a new CSC x low-day unit is now the largest gain; CSC hinge weakened; state offsets grew.

Hypothesis (DB):

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.489 + sum of seven additive children): linear_and_state_offsets (identity_lin, weight 1) + day_eve_cascade (-0.717*103 + 0.082*10233 + 2.713*9165) + csc_hinge (1.965*11061) + csc_lowday (2.112*13711) + csc_tail (2.05*651 + 1.57*5000) + day_novmail_hinge (2.038*2149) + intl_plan (1.865*15558). Composition is purely additive in the logit; the only cross-child coupling is inside day_eve_cascade (service calls switch off the bill hinge). 27 inputs are unconnected (17 state one-hots, all 3 area codes, totalDayMinutes/EveMinutes/NightCharge/IntlMinutes, which duplicate connected charge/minute columns, and eve/night/intl call counts) and have zero effect.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Local train decomposition: full AUC 0.914 (refit L2 logistic regression 0.843). Every child replaced by its least-squares linear fit: 0.839. Restoring one child's nonlinearity onto that: csc_lowday +0.045, day_novmail_hinge +0.038, day_eve_cascade +0.036, csc_hinge +0.017 (all three CSC children together 0.886, +0.047), csc_tail 0, linear/intl 0 (exactly linear). Gains are strongly sub-additive (sum 0.136 vs total 0.075). Linearising one child at a time costs ~0.010 each for cascade, lowday and novmail. Function preservation checked by check_explanation.py.

Hypothesis (DB):

Sparse linear backbone plus single-state units, exactly linear on the data: identity_lin = 38 direct input weights (31 state one-hots, voiceMailPlan -0.659, numberVmailMessages +0.453, totalEveCharge +0.515, totalNightMinutes +0.198, totalIntlCharge +0.333, totalDayCalls +0.112, accountLength +0.147) plus 7 relu units on single state one-hots (3741 state:39, 12681 state:44, 16888 state:30, 18605 state:43, 9093 state:31, 7655/27279 state:25) which are affine in their binary input, so each acts as a state offset. Largest offsets are rare-state switches: state:11 (-2.5 logit, 73 rows), state:46 (-2.0), state:4 (+1.4), state:39 (-0.95, mostly via 3741).

Evidence (train, n=4000): Exactly linear (identity node; state units affine on binary inputs, linear R2 1.0). Mean-ablated AUC 0.914 -> 0.890. Setting every state one-hot to 0 everywhere gives AUC 0.906. Per-state logit effect (category on vs off) vs calibrating offset given other features: state:11 -2.49 vs -2.52 (73 rows, 3 churners; raw log-odds offset -1.22), state:46 -1.96 vs -1.96 (80 rows, raw -0.83), state:4 +1.37 vs +1.39 (41, raw +0.84), state:47 +1.20 vs +1.32 (72, raw +0.95), state:39 -0.95 vs -0.95 (82, raw -0.86). The network's state offsets equal the training-calibrated ones, i.e. roughly double the raw offsets: fitted to small samples.

y0=relu⁡(−0.277xstate:5_b+1.55xtotalEveCharge_b+0.928)y1=relu⁡(1.02relu⁡(−0.0432xstate:3_b+0.941relu⁡(−0.277xstate:5_b+1.55xtotalEveCharge_b+0.928)−0.0835)+0.00464)y2=relu⁡(0.609xtotalDayCharge_b−0.77relu⁡(0.884xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_g−0.848)+0.484relu⁡(1.02relu⁡(−0.0432xstate:3_b+0.941relu⁡(−0.277xstate:5_b+1.55xtotalEveCharge_b+0.928)−0.0835)+0.00464)−0.982)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 0.277 x_{state:5\_b} \\ &\quad + 1.55 x_{totalEveCharge\_b} \\ &\quad + 0.928 \bigr) \end{aligned} \\ \begin{aligned} y_1 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 1.02 \operatorname{relu}{\left(- 0.0432 x_{state:3\_b} + 0.941 \operatorname{relu}{\left(- 0.277 x_{state:5\_b} + 1.55 x_{totalEveCharge\_b} + 0.928 \right)} - 0.0835 \right)} \\ &\quad + 0.00464 \bigr) \end{aligned} \\ \begin{aligned} y_2 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 0.609 x_{totalDayCharge\_b} \\ &\quad - 0.77 \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.884 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_g} - 0.848 \right)} \\ &\quad + 0.484 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.02 \operatorname{relu}{\left(- 0.0432 x_{state:3\_b} + 0.941 \operatorname{relu}{\left(- 0.277 x_{state:5\_b} + 1.55 x_{totalEveCharge\_b} + 0.928 \right)} - 0.0835 \right)} + 0.00464 \right)} \\ &\quad -0.982 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Day x eve bill interaction. 103 = relu(1.554 eveCharge + 0.928) (off below eve charge ~14.5) is read out at -0.717 and passed through the near-identity relu chain 5908 -> 10233 into 9165 = relu(0.609 dayCharge + 0.484*10233 - 0.770*14599 - 0.982), read out at +2.713. Net: at low day charge the cascade cancels the backbone eve-charge slope (down to -2.2 logit), at high day charge it adds up to +2.5 logit when eve charge is also high, i.e. churn rises with the combined day+eve bill. 14599 = relu(0.884 CSC - 0.848) (on from 3 service calls) switches the bill hinge off for complaining customers, so bill and CSC effects do not stack.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train tables (CSC<=2), cascade logit by day-charge bin (rows) x eve-charge bin (cols, cut at 14.2/17.1/19.9/22.6): day<23: 0.00, -0.30, -0.90, -1.56, -2.16; day 38-42: 0.00, -0.24, -0.16, +0.48, +1.20; day>42: +0.39, +0.42, +1.14, +1.67, +2.48. Observed churn day>42: 0.21, 0.44, 0.65, 0.75, 0.76; day<23: 0.05-0.07 flat (so the cancelled eve slope at low day charge is supported). At top day-charge quintile, cascade mean +0.52 for CSC<=2 vs -0.48 for CSC>=4 (14599 shut-off). 10233 = 1.024*relu(0.941*103 - 0.083 - 0.043 state:3) + 0.005 to within 0.002. Sensitivity: 103/10233 to eveCharge 1.11/1.05, state:5 0.20; 9165 to dayCharge, eve and CSC.

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-3.246 + linear backbone + two CSC x low-usage gates (threshold chain fires from 3 calls when day charge is below ~median: +3.0/+5.3/+7.6 logit at 4/5/6 calls) + high-day-minutes hinge (+2.35 above p90, churn 0.49) + near-linear intl-minutes hinge + small hinges + exact state offsets), additive. Service calls enter only through gates.

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): Same two CSC x low-day gates and day hinge (train AUC 0.9006 -> 0.9081; nonlinear gain 0.065 -> 0.075); 104 now uses eveCharge; a state-42/intl-minutes modulator on the veto; new intl-minutes hinge; a new over-shot state-24 offset.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis (supported): P(churn) = sigmoid(-3.246 + linear_backbone + csc_low_usage_gate + csc_threshold_low_day + day_minutes_hinge + intl_minutes_hinge + account_length_hinge + vmail_messages_hinge + state_units); all children combine additively in the output logit; the 26 unconnected inputs (totalNightMinutes, totalIntlCharge, all 3 area codes, 21 states) have zero effect. The nonlinear structure is one idea plus one hinge: customer-service calls raise churn risk steeply only when day (and evening) usage is low, and day usage raises risk sharply only in the top quartile. Evidence (train): AUC 0.9081; all children linearised jointly 0.8331 (refit L2 LR 0.8433); restoring the two CSC gates together recovers 0.0693 of the 0.0750 gap, with the day-minutes hinge 0.0745; csc_threshold_low_day alone 0.053, csc_low_usage_gate alone 0.037, day hinge alone 0.031; intl/account/vmail hinges and state units ~0. SHAP (300 rows, probability scale): linear backbone 0.116, 104 0.060, 6238 0.054, 9029 0.025, 7506 0.023, 29980 0.019, others <0.003. Rare categories: state 24 offset -1.60 vs calibrating -0.55; state 42 lifts the day-charge veto on 8 rows; all states off costs 0.0076 AUC.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis (supported): service calls x low total usage. 104 = relu(0.228 + 0.383 CSC - 1.051 dayCharge - 0.995 eveCharge + 0.074 state30 + 0.101 state6), read out 0.911. The unit is on (56% of rows) when calls are many or combined day+evening charge is low. Evidence (train, 4000 rows): mean logit contribution 2.15 (0 calls) to 3.99 (5 calls) in the lowest decile of day+eve charge, 0 above the median for <=3 calls, and still +1.3 at 7+ calls in p50-75. Sensitivity: dayCharge 0.59, eveCharge 0.55, CSC 0.21, states 30/6 0.04-0.06. Part of it cancels the positive linear day/eve slopes for light users. Linearising it alone costs 0.008 train AUC; restoring it alone onto the all-linear model gains 0.037.

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.61 + affine backbone + readouts of one serial core): a CS-calls hinge steeper for light day users feeds a sharper 4+-calls threshold (0/0.1/0.6/2.0/4.0/6.6 logit for 2..6 calls), which feeds an international-plan unit (+2.5, damped at high calls), which damps a heavy-day-usage hinge (+3.35 in the top day decile without voicemail). Train AUC 0.918. Note: the AUC-trained network is miscalibrated (mean p 0.37 vs base rate 0.14).

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): 15 -> 20 hidden nodes; independent additive hinges fused into one serial chain; train AUC 0.899 -> 0.918, nonlinear gain 0.059 -> 0.088; state:2 became a -2.15 wrong-sign switch.

Heavy-usage hinge read out at +2.44: without voicemail it is ~0 below the 60th day-minutes percentile, 0.48 at the 8th decile, 0.93 at the 9th, 3.35 in the top decile; with voicemail messages it is 0.77 in the top decile (data: top-decile churn 61% without voicemail vs 8% with). On intl-plan rows the top-decile value drops 2.9 -> 2.0 through 7494. Exits 3151, 4939, 5868, 1044, 252 are all read by the output. Linearising usage_core costs 0.088 train AUC (0.918 -> 0.830); restoring 3151 alone onto the linearised model adds +0.066.

Restoring both CS units onto the linearised model adds +0.052 train AUC.

What to look at

  • Largest closed-form error: state_switches (0.0326), then state_chain_21_13 (0.0255). This is the cost of the 3 s.f. display rounding, in the exit's own units; the numeric function is exact. Check that the rounded formula still supports the hypothesis as worded.
  • Strong claim in lowday_csc: “…0 for 0-1 calls, rises with calls and is larger at low day usage: 3 calls 1.08/0.25/0.00 (low/mid/high day tercile), 5 calls 2.84/2.03/1.03, 7+ calls 4.49/3.85/3.64.” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • Strong claim in linear_backbone: “Affine logit backbone (exactly affine on train): identity_lin sums the 35 direct input->output edges: voicemail plan -0.99, voicemail messages +0.51, intl charge +0.16, day charge +0.13, CS calls -0.09, 26 state offsets (largest s…” Is this (exactness, threshold, rare category) supported by the evidence, or fitted to a few rows?
  • 11 split(s), all of input nodes (an input feeding two annotations). These are routine; check only that each input copy sits in the annotation whose hypothesis uses it.
  • 3 consolidation(s): copies merged back after a split. Check that the merged copies carry the same role.
  • Read the root's hypothesis against its closed form: does the stated combination of children (additive, gated, serial) match the formula?

Summary (from the record)

Logit = -3.08 + direct linear term (dayCharge +2.83/z, intl plan +2.87, voiceMailPlan -2.8, 28 state offsets) + a usage hinge (churn rises steeply only for heavy users: 33-72% at day z>1) + two partly redundant CSC x low-day paths firing at 3+ calls (89-100% churn at 4+ calls, day z<-0.5) + a tiny low-day hinge and memorised state/area offsets. Train AUC 0.917 vs 0.836 all-linearised.

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): 16 -> 23 hidden nodes; train AUC 0.905 -> 0.917; a strong day+eve usage hinge appeared (+0.053 alone); CSC interaction partly moved into a new cascade; state offsets similar; state gates added on the CSC unit.

Closed form:

y0=relu⁡(−0.173xstate:22_a−0.593xstate:29−0.672xtotalDayCharge_b+1.61relu⁡(0.515xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_a−0.198xstate:31_b−0.311)−0.514)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 0.173 x_{state:22\_a} \\ &\quad - 0.593 x_{state:29} \\ &\quad - 0.672 x_{totalDayCharge\_b} \\ &\quad + 1.61 \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.515 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_a} - 0.198 x_{state:31\_b} - 0.311 \right)} \\ &\quad -0.514 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Service calls x low day usage, plus a low-day hinge. 6258 = relu(0.515*csc - 0.198*state:31 - 0.311) opens at 3+ customer-service calls. 776 = relu(1.61*6258 - 0.672*dayCharge - 0.593*state:29 - 0.173*state:22 - 0.514), output weight +1.73. With 0-2 calls it is a plain low-day-charge hinge (z < -0.76; about +1.5 logit at z < -1.5). With 4+ calls it fires across a wider day range: mean +4.35 logit at day z<-1.5 and +2.97 at -1.5..-0.5, where churn is 100% (16 rows) and 89% (76 rows), against 3-7% for 0-3 calls. Evidence (train, n=4000): closed form; sensitivity is largest for dayCharge (0.23) and state:29 (0.20), then csc (0.11); linearising this child alone costs 0.007 AUC, restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model adds +0.047. Rare-state gates: state:29 (72 rows) switches the unit off (-1.8 logit on 10 rows, 1 churner); state:31 (-2.8 on 2 rows) and state:22 similar.

Hypothesis (DB):

Usage hinge plus a second service-call x low-usage path. With 7068 = 0 the relays are constant (7561=1.31, 12924=2.68, 9009=4.43+0.83*vmp), so 4496 = relu(1.79 - 2.01*dayMin - 1.08*eveCharge + 0.56*voiceMailPlan), output +1.31. It cancels the direct day (+2.83 dayCharge +0.27 dayMin) and eve (+0.95 eveCharge +0.42 eveMin) slopes below high usage: the net day slope is about +0.5/z below z~0.9 and +3.1/z above, so churn rises steeply only for heavy day+eve users (33% churn at day z 1-2, 72% at z>2, vs 8-12% below). A voice-mail plan shifts the hinge (+1.24 logit at low usage, offsetting part of the -2.8 direct edge). Branch: 10224 -> 10574 -> 21697 rises with day minutes and an international plan; 7068 = relu(0.467*csc - 1.18*21697 - 0.359) opens only at 3+ calls with low day usage and no international plan (306 rows) and feeds 4496 through the relays with gain ~4.2 (about +5.5 logit per unit of 7068): +8.6 mean contribution at 4+ calls and day z -1.5..-0.5 vs +4.7 at 0-2 calls. 10574 and 21697 also reach the output directly with tiny weights (-0.04, -0.02). Evidence (train): closed form; sensitivity of 4496 dominated by dayMin (1.69) and eveCharge (0.85). Linearising this child costs 0.037 AUC; restored alone onto the linearised model it adds +0.075 (base usage hinge alone +0.053, the csc branch alone +0.041). Forcing 7068 to 0 drops the full AUC 0.917 -> 0.904.

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-2.164 + linear backbone + 2.82 relu(total-usage hinge, switched off by voicemail messages) + service-call block (counts calls mainly for low day usage: +2.9 logit, 95% churn at 4 calls with day z<-1; a call hinge vetoed for heavy users and state:45) + small intl-charge hinges + state offset units + account-length hinge). Train AUC 0.924; miscalibrated (mean p 0.336 vs base 0.1415).

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): Same node lineage; a day-only hinge grew into a total day+eve+night usage hinge; a state:4 unit became intl-charge hinges; some state units removed. Train AUC 0.908 -> 0.924; nonlinear gain 0.072 -> 0.091, almost all from usage and service calls.

Hypothesis (DB):

HYPOTHESIS: churn logit = -2.164 + linearBackbone + 2.82*heavyUsageNoVmail + serviceCalls + intlChargeHinges + stateUnits + accountLengthHinge, an additive (parallel) composition in the output pre-activation; output = sigmoid. 25 unconnected inputs (incl. totalDayCalls, totalEveCalls, totalIntlMinutes, totalNightCharge, area codes and 17 states) are zero-effect entries. EVIDENCE (train, n=4000, local ablation): full AUC 0.9243 (L2 logistic regression 0.8433). All nonlinear children jointly replaced by least-squares linear fits on their own inputs: 0.8333; all hidden mean-ablated: 0.659. The 0.091 nonlinear gain comes from two children: heavyUsageNoVmail (restore alone +0.0708, Shapley 0.057) and serviceCalls (+0.0489, Shapley 0.035); restoring both gives 0.9244 (= full). intlChargeHinges, stateUnits and accountLengthHinge contribute nothing over their linear fits. The model is miscalibrated on train (mean p 0.336 vs base rate 0.1415; global shift -1.875 needed). Rare-category effects are constant offsets: state:11 -2.18, state:46 -1.63, state:4 +1.12 (mixed direct/hidden, range -0.53..+1.48), state:47 +0.92, state:39 -0.86, state:31 +0.70, state:45 off-switch of the call veto.

Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn200-s0.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

One-line equivalent (same writer as the UI):

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('churn200-s0', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py

Summary (from the record)

P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.348 + sparse linear backbone (intl plan +2.94, 20 state offsets, almost no linear service-call term) + 6 additive children): a service-call x low-usage gate (+1.25/+4.0/+7.0/+10.7 logit at 3/4/5/6+ calls below 150 day minutes, 0 for heavy users); a convex heavy day+eve usage hinge (up to +8.3); a high-day-charge hinge only without voicemail messages; small CSC hinge; negligible eve brake; state offsets. Train AUC 0.919; well calibrated (mean p 0.143).

Compared with the 100-generation network (record): Train AUC 0.910 -> 0.919, 18 -> 23 hidden nodes; same three hinges; the service-call gate became the biggest source and much steeper/convex, absorbing the linear service-call slope; heavy-usage hinge became convex; new state:35 gate switch; state:46 now also shuts the gate.

Hypothesis (DB):

Root: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.348 + linear_backbone + heavy_day_eve_usage + service_call_gate + day_charge_no_voicemail + csc_hinge + eve_charge_brake + state_offsets), additive in logit; the top-level children never feed each other (the heavy-usage hinge 1694 is split, with copy 1694_b inside the gate). The output also reads csc_escalation.10379 (the state:46 unit, grandchild exit) with weight -0.005. 30 unconnected inputs are zero-effect entries. Evidence (train, 4000 rows, local in-memory forward passes): full AUC 0.9193; all nonlinear children replaced by least-squares linear fits on their entries 0.8303 (jointly 0.8297; refit L2 logistic regression 0.8433). Restoring one child's nonlinearity alone onto the linearised model gains: service_call_gate +0.064, day_charge_no_voicemail +0.046, heavy_day_eve_usage +0.045, csc_hinge +0.007, eve_charge_brake -0.002. Shapley split of the gain: gate 0.041, day-charge 0.023, heavy-usage 0.022. Removing all state effects drops AUC to 0.9094 (0.010). SHAP top features: day minutes/charge, service calls, international plan, voicemail, eve charge.

Hinge on combined day+evening usage, read out twice. 1694 = relu(1.127*dayMinutes + 0.763*eveCharge - 0.009*state:27 + 0.012*28715 - 1.121) (z-scored), readout +2.03; 3237 = relu(0.871*1694 - 0.478), readout +1.05, makes the hinge steeper (convex) once 1694 exceeds 0.55. 28715 = relu(0.811 + 1.234*state:35 + 1.001*11600) and 11600 = relu(1.011*state:20 - 2.214) are state dribbles whose effect through the 0.012 weight is under 0.11 logit; state:27 shifts the threshold by at most -0.2 logit. Mean contribution is 0 unless both day and evening usage are well above average: +1.2 logit at 200-220 day and 250-300 eve minutes, +2.6 at 220-250/250-300, +4.3 at 250-280/250-300, +6.6 at 280+/250-300 and +8.3 when day > 280 and eve > 300 (train churn 60-72% in the heavy cells, vs 3-12% below 200 day minutes). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.9131 (linear-fit R^2 0.40); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8749 (gain +0.045).
