Closed form (children as functions):

y0=relu⁡(0.389xnumberCustomerServiceCalls_a+0.495csc_escalation_0⁡(−71c,−71e,−16,−42a,−51)−1.72usage_brake_0⁡(−61b,−61c,−61d,−64a,−30a,−59a,−64d,−21a,−30c,−14a)+0.206usage_brake_1⁡(−61b,−61c,−61d,−64a,−30a,−59a,−64d,−21a,−30c,−14a)−0.641)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 0.389 x_{numberCustomerServiceCalls\_a} \\ &\quad + 0.495 \operatorname{csc\_escalation\_0}{\left(-71_{c},-71_{e},-16,-42_{a},-51 \right)} \\ &\quad - 1.72 \operatorname{usage\_brake\_0}{\left(-61_{b},-61_{c},-61_{d},-64_{a},-30_{a},-59_{a},-64_{d},-21_{a},-30_{c},-14_{a} \right)} \\ &\quad + 0.206 \operatorname{usage\_brake\_1}{\left(-61_{b},-61_{c},-61_{d},-64_{a},-30_{a},-59_{a},-64_{d},-21_{a},-30_{c},-14_{a} \right)} \\ &\quad -0.641 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Many customer-service calls AND low usage -> churn. 997 = relu(0.389*CSC + 0.494*csc_escalation.7689 - 1.718*usage_brake.4397 + 0.206*usage_brake.1694_b - 0.641), readout +3.108. The convex service-call signal pushes 997 up; the usage ramp 4397 shuts it for anyone with average or higher day usage. Mean contribution: 0 for 0-2 calls at any usage; at 3 calls +1.25 logit below 150 day minutes, +0.6 at 150-180; at 4 calls +4.0 / +2.6 / +0.9 (below 150 / 150-180 / 180-200 minutes); at 5 calls +7.0 / +4.4 / +2.6; at 6+ calls +10.7 / +8.5 / +5.5; about 0 above 220 minutes except for 6+ calls. Train churn with 4+ calls and under 150 day minutes is 87-100% (86 rows) vs 4-6% for 0-3 calls. Rare-state switches inside the gate: state:35 removes the usage brake (via 20866), so 9 of its 87 rows with 3+ calls get +0.5 to +6.8 logit (only 3 of the 9 churned); state:46 lowers the service-call signal (via 10379), so its high-call rows lose up to 2 more logit. Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.8945 (linear-fit R^2 0.35); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8939 (gain +0.064). Closed form from get_formula; sensitivity summary attached.

y0=relu⁡(0.653xtotalDayCharge_b−0.804relu⁡(1.01xstate:35_a−0.317)+0.578relu⁡(1.01xtotalDayCharge_d−1.57)+1.33relu⁡(1.48xtotalDayCharge_c+0.998xtotalEveCharge_a+1.09)−0.502)y1=relu⁡(−0.00945xstate:27_a+1.13xtotalDayMinutes_a+0.763xtotalEveCharge_d+0.0119relu⁡(1.23xstate:35_c+1.0relu⁡(1.01xstate:20_a−2.21)+0.811)−1.12)\begin{gathered}\begin{aligned} y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 0.653 x_{totalDayCharge\_b} \\ &\quad - 0.804 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.01 x_{state:35\_a} - 0.317 \right)} \\ &\quad + 0.578 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.01 x_{totalDayCharge\_d} - 1.57 \right)} \\ &\quad + 1.33 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.48 x_{totalDayCharge\_c} + 0.998 x_{totalEveCharge\_a} + 1.09 \right)} \\ &\quad -0.502 \bigr) \end{aligned} \\ \begin{aligned} y_1 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( - 0.00945 x_{state:27\_a} \\ &\quad + 1.13 x_{totalDayMinutes\_a} \\ &\quad + 0.763 x_{totalEveCharge\_d} \\ &\quad + 0.0119 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.23 x_{state:35\_c} + 1.0 \operatorname{relu}{\left(1.01 x_{state:20\_a} - 2.21 \right)} + 0.811 \right)} \\ &\quad -1.12 \bigr) \end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Hypothesis (DB):

Two usage signals feeding the service-call gate 997. 4397 = relu(0.653*dayCharge + 1.327*15054 + 0.578*23191 - 0.804*20866 - 0.502), with 15054 = relu(1.483*dayCharge + 0.998*eveCharge + 1.089) and 23191 = relu(1.007*dayCharge - 1.567): a convex, increasing ramp in day charge (and to a lesser extent evening charge), zero only for low-usage customers; it enters 997 with weight -1.718, i.e. it is a brake that shuts the gate for heavy users. 20866 = relu(1.01*state:35 - 0.317) is on only in state:35 (value 6.45) and removes the brake there (4397 in-state mean 0.15 vs 1.77): a rare-state switch. 1694_b is the split copy of the heavy-usage hinge 1694 (same function as in heavy_day_eve_usage) entering 997 with weight +0.206. Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably.

Hypothesis (DB):

Hypothesis (DB):

19579 = relu(1.025*eveCharge + 1.015*23438 - 1.052), 23438 = relu(1.047*eveCharge - 0.386); readout -0.256. A convex function of evening charge alone with a negative readout: 0 below 220 evening minutes, -0.03 logit at 220-250, -0.29 at 250-280, -0.71 above 280. It slightly flattens the evening part of the heavy-usage hinge for customers whose day usage is not high; its AUC contribution is nil (linearising it changes train AUC by -0.0005). Note: after z-scoring, totalDayCharge and totalDayMinutes are identical columns (charge is an exact multiple of minutes), as are totalEveCharge and totalEveMinutes, so the network uses them interchangeably. Evidence (train, local forward passes): replacing this child's logit contribution by its least-squares linear fit on its entries changes train AUC 0.9193 -> 0.9188 (linear-fit R^2 0.49); restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model (AUC 0.8303) gives 0.8281 (gain -0.002). Verdict

Fill in and add to experiments/10seed/explanations/churn200-s6.json as a top-level key, then run uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py. Or use the UI's Review & verify form, which writes the same field. verified: true if the explanation is correct as it stands or after your changes, false if not. changes: what you changed (empty if nothing).

"mike_verification": {"verified": null, "minutes": null, "changes": "", "notes": ""}

One-line equivalent (same writer as the UI):

uv run python -c "from explaneat.analysis.explanation_records import write_verification as w; w('churn200-s6', True, minutes=0, changes='', notes='')" && uv run python experiments/10seed/build_explanations_csv.py
